5516: POSSIBLE (benefit) — the telephone evidence is one small randomised trial (81 caregivers) with benefits at post-treatment that mostly faded by 6 months, supported by a 19-person videoconferencing pilot and one face-to-face ACT trial; single-trial cap applies
5517: POSSIBLE (benefit) — two small randomised trials of therapy chatbots in students (70 and 74 participants, 2 to 4 weeks) found symptom reductions versus information-only controls; the Wysa evidence is observational only, and no randomised evidence for AI companions as a loneliness treatment was found

Small, short trials only

5275: POSSIBLE (benefit) — habit reversal training increased nail length versus wait-list (P<0.001 at 1 month) and beat object manipulation long-term in one 91-child randomised trial; NAC's one positive pilot (42 children) showed a difference at 1 month (nail growth 5.21 mm versus 1.18 mm) that was gone by 2 months. Small trials, short follow-up

5277: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference) for overall recovery — the Cochrane review found no significant difference in clinical improvement (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.99–1.15) and a mean cough just 0.46 days shorter, while adverse effects increased (RR 1.20; number needed to harm 24). 5278: POSSIBLE (benefit) — NSAIDs give a small average benefit over placebo in acute low back pain (pain −7.29 points on a 0–100 scale, moderate certainty; disability −2.02 on a 0–24 scale, high certainty) that the Cochrane authors judge probably not clinically relevant; no drug class provides a large or medium effect, and paracetamol is no better than placebo. Boundary: adding a muscle relaxant to an NSAID is a different question, homed on Shelf #786 — not covered here
5279: LIKELY (benefit) for the class in major depressive disorder — all 21 antidepressants were more effective than placebo across 522 trials (116,477 participants) — with the size stated plainly: an average advantage of 1.75 Hamilton points, a large response in 24.5% of patients on drug versus 9.6% on placebo, and a drug–placebo difference that may be minimal or nonexistent in mild-to-moderate symptoms (effect size d<0.20 below a Hamilton score of 23 in patient-level data)
5280: MAYBE (weak evidence) — replacing long-chain fats with MCTs lost an extra 0.51 kg (95% CI −0.80 to −0.23) across 13 small trials in which commercial bias was detected, and the trials swapped fats rather than adding MCT oil on top; the cognition claim rests on one maker-run 152-person trial positive at day 45 and in a genetic subgroup, while its 413-person confirmatory trial found no benefit (P=0.2458)
5281: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference) for patient-important outcomes — antipyretics reliably lower temperature, but the randomised evidence in sepsis shows no mortality benefit (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.77–1.13); intravenous ibuprofen in 455 septic patients gave 30-day mortality of 37% versus 40% on placebo, not significant; the one external-cooling trial with lower day-14 mortality missed its own primary endpoint. The ICU paracetamol trial (HEAT) is homed on Shelf #3160 and is cross-pointed here, not re-carded
5282: POSSIBLE (benefit) — prevention only: scopolamine beat placebo across 14 small trials (Cochrane) and first-generation antihistamines prevented symptoms in 40% versus 25% on placebo (RR 1.81, relative; moderate-certainty) with more sedation; ginger rests on one 80-cadet sea trial; no randomised trial has tested any of these drugs for treating symptoms once started
5283: POSSIBLE (benefit) — UKPDS 34's overweight substudy showed 32–42% relative reductions in diabetes endpoints and death versus diet-first policy (no absolute rates printed), SPREAD-DIMCAD favoured metformin over glipizide (HR 0.54, relative), but the pooled isolated-effect meta-analysis is non-significant on every outcome and UKPDS 34's own supplementary trial raised an unconfirmed mortality signal for early combination use; the 10-year legacy follow-up is homed on Shelf #284
5284: POSSIBLE (benefit) — GAP-E: for atrial fibrillation, rivaroxaban is trial-supported in stage 3 kidney disease at a creatinine-clearance dose (20 mg/day at CrCl ≥50 mL/min; 15 mg/day at CrCl 30–49, where it matched warfarin on stroke prevention and composite bleeding in ROCKET-AF's renal subgroup); exposure rises only ~1.5-fold at CrCl 30–49, observational stage III data show no detected penalty — but there is no trial evidence below CrCl 30 and none for VTE dosing on this shelf
5287: LIKELY (benefit) — ibuprofen plus acetaminophen is the best-supported first-line treatment for acute dental pain: it ranked first for benefit and maximum relief in the Moore 2018 overview of systematic reviews, gave the largest 6-hour relief in the 82-trial ADA network meta-analysis (MD 1.68 vs placebo, ahead of every opioid combination), and is first-line in the 2024 ADA guideline; opioids add harm without added relief
5288: POSSIBLE (benefit) — for watchful waiting in uncomplicated cystitis: spontaneous symptom cure was 28% at one week on placebo in the largest trial (Ferry 2004), up to 42% were symptom-free or improved by 9 days across placebo arms (Hoffmann 2020), but most women do not recover quickly without antibiotics (day-7 cure 17/33 on placebo vs 30/34 on nitrofurantoin), delayed prescribing traded 37% longer symptoms for less antibiotic use, and pyelonephritis, though rare, occurred on placebo
5289: SPLIT — in PRECISION, daily ibuprofen (≈2,000 mg/day) matched celecoxib and naproxen on cardiovascular events (2.7% vs 2.3% and 2.5%) but was significantly worse for gastrointestinal events (vs celecoxib, P=0.002) and renal events (P=0.004), raised 24-hour systolic pressure by 3.7 mmHg with new hypertension in 23.2% of normotensive users, and in the CNT meta-analysis carried the highest relative rate of upper GI complications (RR 3.97) of the traditional NSAIDs
5290: SPLIT — the blanket 'no alcohol on antibiotics' warning outruns the evidence for most agents (the 2020 systematic review found data supporting safe use with penicillins, several cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, azithromycin, tetracycline and nitrofurantoin), the famous metronidazole reaction is unproven under double-blind challenge and in the case literature — though the label's 72-hour abstinence advice stands — and a real disulfiram-like risk attaches to MTT/MTDT-side-chain cephalosporins, ketoconazole and griseofulvin
5291: (no treatment shown to work) — two systematic reviews (BMJ 2005; Addiction 2022) found no intervention with replicated, adequately reliable evidence for preventing or treating hangover: 21 placebo-controlled trials totalling 386 participants, no two testing the same remedy, every outcome rated very low quality; the best single prevention trial (prickly pear extract) missed significance on its overall symptom index
5292: SPLIT — at the 4 g/day ceiling, healthy volunteers commonly show ALT rises (31–44% above 3x ULN) but trials show no clinical liver injury at or below the ceiling; the liver-failure record is dominated by median doses of 24 g and staggered supratherapeutic use, where a normal presenting AST (<50 IU/L) predicted no hepatotoxicity
5293: (the treatment made no difference) — no treatment has been shown to work for optic atrophy in general; idebenone's only randomised trial is in Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (homed on Shelf #4253), and its dominant-optic-atrophy evidence is a non-randomised cohort and a 16-patient uncontrolled trial
5294: POSSIBLE — phenolisation after partial nail avulsion consistently reduces recurrence across three syntheses (14% vs 41% in the one like-for-like trial; RR 0.13 in the 2023 meta-analysis), but the underlying trial evidence is rated very low quality and an early infection signal (OR 5.69) is unresolved
5295: SPLIT — after severe hospitalised RMSF, lasting neurological sequelae are documented in a substantial minority of survivors (9 of 20 followed in 1995; 23% with neurologic sequelae on examination in 2022); after treated Lyme disease, persistent symptoms exceed background rates by only ~4–6 percentage points (27.2% vs 21.2–23.3%), and two controlled studies found no significant excess at all
5296: POSSIBLE — retrospective case series only: osteotomy corrects adult genu valgum accurately (96.1% correction accuracy in a 31-procedure series) with 10-year survival of ~74–90% in valgus knees with lateral arthritis, but there are no trials and almost no data in young adults without arthritis
5298: POSSIBLE — class data put drug-attributable discontinuation symptoms at ~15% (1 in 6–7) with severe symptoms ~2.8%, and bupropion ranks in the lower-risk group on both fetched stratifications, so abrupt cessation is usually tolerated — but no bupropion-specific incidence study exists
5299: POSSIBLE — diagonal earlobe crease is consistently associated with coronary artery disease (pooled diagnostic OR 3.27; sensitivity 0.62, specificity 0.67; prospective adjusted association in a 10,885-person cohort), but the evidence is observational only: association, not causation, and too weak to diagnose or exclude disease
5300: LIKELY — purine analogues produce complete remission in ~76–91% of patients (pentostatin 76% vs interferon 11% in the one RCT; cladribine 91% in the pivotal single-arm series), with median relapse-free survival up to 16 years, though relapse continues for decades and cure is not established

5302: POSSIBLE — plasma exchange plus steroids and cyclophosphamide is the standard on one 17-patient randomised trial (dialysis 2 of 8 versus 6 of 9) and concordant cohorts; presenting kidney function, not regimen choice, dominates renal survival (95% at 1 year if creatinine <5.7 mg/dL versus 8% if dialysis-dependent)
5303: POSSIBLE — cetuximab improved all 7 completers of a 9-patient single-arm trial and both patients in a 2-patient chronic-treatment report; no comparative trial of any Ménétrier treatment exists, and every n is printed on the face
5304: POSSIBLE (the treatments made no difference to kidney outcomes) — in matched and unmatched observational comparisons alike, vesicostomy and primary valve ablation did not differ on creatinine or renal replacement therapy; diversion cost more operations, and bladder-function signals conflict
5305: POSSIBLE — metformin, pioglitazone and a branded antioxidant combination each improved lesions within their own trial arms, but no trial has a placebo arm and no agent has beaten another; the honest reading is that treating insulin resistance may help, unproven against doing nothing
5306: SPLIT — radiosurgery controls tumours better than observation (one randomised trial: volume ratio 0.87 versus 1.51) without improving patient-reported outcomes; microsurgery controls better than radiosurgery in non-randomised pools (98% versus 92%) at five times the facial-nerve dysfunction (10% versus 2%); hearing preservation is the same across all three
5307: SPLIT — for simple fistulas fistulotomy and fistulectomy are equivalent and near-definitive; for complex fistulas every sphincter-sparing option fails 22–44% of the time, LIFT/VAAFT/flap are statistically alike, and the plug, fibrin glue and platelet-rich plasma failed significantly more than the flap in randomised comparisons
5309: SPLIT — observation for the small anterior low-risk aneurysm (5-year rupture 0–2.6%, and no ruptures at all under PHASES 8 in a 36-year conservative cohort), treatment for the large, posterior or high-score aneurysm (5-year rupture up to 40–50%); no randomised trial of treatment exists
5310: SPLIT — structured CBT-based treatment for anxiety in pregnancy is supported (postnatal depression 12% versus 41% in the one large trial; internet CBT anxiety effect g = 0.76), brief group CBT was no better than a booklet, and SSRI malformation signals are small relative risks (1.11–1.24) that disappear when women with a psychiatric diagnosis are compared fairly (1.04–1.06, non-significant)
5311: MAYBE (weak evidence) — three small randomised trials (120 children in total) show gains on trained tasks and self-report questionnaires, with behavioural measures null where they were tested separately; nothing here is blinded and the diagnosis itself is contested
5312: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only (no RCT exists): in 308 registry H5N1 cases survival was 60% with oseltamivir versus 24% with no antiviral, with a 49% relative mortality reduction on adjusted modelling, and earlier initiation was consistently associated with better survival
5313: POSSIBLE (benefit) — one small randomised trial (n=60, 4-week follow-up) and small series support short-term pain relief from aspiration plus corticosteroid injection; recurrence needing re-aspiration was 12.7% in the largest series; no surgical trial is carded

5316: POSSIBLE — no randomised trials; an 805-patient prospective registry, a 76-patient geriatric series and a 397-patient paediatric meta-analysis all show high stone clearance by every route, with route choice in practice driven by stone size and anatomy rather than proven superiority

5321: POSSIBLE (benefit) — plate fixation reduces nonunion (0.8% vs 11% at 9 months in the 301-patient UK trial; relative risk 0.14, 95% CI 0.06–0.32, across 6 RCTs) and speeds early function, but 1-year function gains were small (4.4–5.1 points, not clinically relevant) and total secondary operations were similar once plate removal is counted (17.6% vs 16.6%)

5323: SPLIT — overall no significant difference (SPRINT: relative risk 0.90, 95% CI 0.71–1.15) · closed tibial shaft fractures favour reamed nailing (events 11% versus 17%; relative risk 0.67) · open fractures trend against reamed nailing (29% versus 24%; relative risk 1.27, not significant)
5324: POSSIBLE — local anaesthesia for closed reduction matched general anaesthesia in one small RCT (29 patients) and one prospective comparison (40 patients); early reduction reported better than late in one cohort (54 patients) without per-group numbers
5325: LIKELY — serratus anterior plane block added to standard care improves early pain control (41% versus 19.6% met the 4-hour pain goal in SABRE, 210 patients) and halves 24-hour opioid use (median 45 versus 91 mg morphine equivalents); no pneumonia or mortality benefit shown
5328: POSSIBLE — no definitive RCT exists; the CARE pilot (72 patients) showed a definitive trial is feasible but had 2 events in each arm; observational cohort comparisons favour intervention but are confounded by selection
5329: SPLIT — surgery relieves cervical radiculopathy pain faster (better short-term pain outcomes in both randomised trials), but physiotherapy/collar care catches up: no significant differences at 1 year (Cochrane/Persson) and disability never differed over 24 months (Engquist, P=0.23)

5332: POSSIBLE — in the one randomised trial (IATS, 114 infants), contact-lens correction and primary IOL implantation gave identical median vision at 4½ years (both 0.90 logMAR), but the IOL group had more adverse events (81% vs 56%) and far more additional intraocular operations (72% vs 21%) by age 5
5333: POSSIBLE — cuspal-coverage (crown/onlay) restoration of a cracked vital tooth is associated with fewer pulpal complications and extractions than an uncovered direct filling in pooled observational data; repairing a defective restoration was no worse than replacing it in the one long comparative study; and pulp capping and partial pulpotomy both succeeded in over 80% at one year in the one randomised trial (carious exposures)

5336: POSSIBLE — observational cohorts only: a differential pressure (diastolic minus compartment) under 30 mmHg was the threshold that missed no case in 116 monitored tibial fractures, and monitored patients were decompressed sooner with fewer sequelae; but on timing itself cohorts conflict — amputation rose with delay after earthquake crush injury (0% <24 h to 31.4% >48 h) while a 546-patient series found no association between time to fasciotomy and death or amputation
5337: SPLIT — corns: 40% salicylic acid plasters beat scalpel debridement in the one randomised trial (resolution 34% vs 21% at 3 months, longer time to recurrence) · calluses: scalpel debridement's pain advantage over sham was only 2–7 mm and non-significant, and full versus partial debridement did not differ — its specific effect on callus pain is small
5338: MAYBE (weak evidence) — the Cochrane review found only six small randomised trials (310 infants), all very low-certainty, and no trials of the antifungals, mineral oils or salicylic acid actually used for cradle cap; the one antifungal-versus-steroid comparison (48 infants, non-randomised) found no difference, with all lesions cleared by two weeks on both sides
5340: SPLIT — phakic eyes: scleral buckling improved vision more than vitrectomy in the SPR study (−0.71 vs −0.56 logMAR) · pseudophakic eyes: vitrectomy reattached first time more often (72.0% vs 53.4%) with equal vision · PIVOT-eligible detachments: pneumatic retinopexy gave better 12-month vision (+4.9 letters) but lower primary success (80.8% vs 93.2%), final success ~99% both ways
5341: MAYBE (weak evidence) — task-oriented therapy and CO-OP improve performance on the goals children practise (waitlist RCT: goal scores 2.7 to 7.0, P<0.001, maintained at 3 months), but the Cochrane review's RCT-only analysis found no effect on motor performance (51 children), and it rated all its evidence very low to low quality
5343: SPLIT — adjunctive online Finding Solid Ground programme: significant gains versus waitlist at 6 months in an interim RCT of 291 patients (no between-group effect sizes printed) · stabilising group treatment added to individual therapy: no immediate advantage in the RCT of 59 patients · phase-oriented therapy itself: 19 studies, essentially all uncontrolled
5344: MAYBE (weak evidence) (the treatment made no difference) — the two large randomised trials (129 children, 123 young adults) found no significant between-group difference on their primary measures, and the Cochrane pooling of the adult donepezil studies (192 participants) spans no effect, with more adverse events on donepezil
5345: POSSIBLE (benefit) — comparative observational pooling puts final adult height 4.83 cm higher (95% CI 2.32 to 7.34) in treated versus untreated girls with idiopathic CPP, and suppression reverses after stopping (menarche ~0.9 years later); no randomised trial exists, so the stamp is capped at POSSIBLE
5348: POSSIBLE (benefit) — in the one randomised trial (53 patients, open, blinded endpoints, stopped early), arterial rupture/dissection occurred in 20% on celiprolol versus 50% on no treatment (HR 0.36, a 64% relative reduction; 30-percentage-point absolute difference), and the 144-patient national cohort found better, dose-dependent survival on celiprolol
5349: POSSIBLE (benefit) — the single phase III EASE trial found first complete target-wound closure within 45 days in 41.3% on Oleogel-S10 versus 28.9% on control gel (RR 1.44, a 44% relative increase; 12.4-percentage-point absolute difference; P = 0.013), with sustained wound-burden reduction over 24 months open-label
5350: POSSIBLE (benefit) — in the only double-blind trial (20 patients with >4 attacks/year), continuous acyclovir 400 mg twice daily gave a median of 0 attacks versus 3 on placebo over 6 months (P < 0.0005), with 7 of 11 attack-free; a single small trial caps the stamp
5351: POSSIBLE (benefit) — HDSS responders 60% versus 27% on placebo at 6 weeks in the largest of three small short RCTs (n=62, 50 and 32), with dry mouth in 43% versus 11% (and 100% at 10 mg/day in the post-sympathectomy trial)
5352: LIKELY (no difference in survival) — in the COMS randomised trial (1,317 patients with medium choroidal melanoma), 5-year survival was 81% after enucleation versus 82% after iodine-125 plaque brachytherapy (P=.48; adjusted relative risk of death 0.99, 95% CI 0.80–1.22), and 12-year all-cause mortality was 41% versus 43%; brachytherapy keeps the eye, but median vision in the treated eye fell to 20/125 by 3 years
5353: MAYBE (weak evidence) (the treatment made no difference) — across 12 randomised trials (1,080 participants) patching did not speed healing at 24, 48 or 72 hours (relative risks 0.89, 0.97, 1.01) and time to heal differed by +0.14 days; pain and complications leaned against the patch without reaching significance
5354: SPLIT — against a lactose load in breath-test-confirmed intolerance, lactase cut breath hydrogen 55% (relative) and improved symptoms in a 47-person crossover trial · at ordinary intakes (240 ml milk daily) blinded symptoms were trivial-to-mild and identical on regular and hydrolysed milk, and the AHRQ review (36 trials) rated the symptom evidence for lactose-reduced products insufficient
5355: SPLIT — by organism: Campylobacter symptoms shortened 1.32 days (95% CI 0.64–1.99) across 11 randomised trials · Shigella dysentery shortened by antibiotics (diarrhoea at follow-up, relative risk 0.21–0.30 vs no drug) · non-typhoidal Salmonella: no benefit (duration differences ~0 days) and one-month carriage almost doubled (relative risk 1.96)
5356: POSSIBLE (benefit) — adjuvant fluoropyrimidine after resection of biliary tract cancer (including gallbladder): BILCAP's primary analysis missed significance (HR 0.81, p=0.097; medians 51.1 vs 36.4 months) though its sensitivity/per-protocol analyses were positive, and ASCOT was clearly positive for S-1 (5-year survival 64% vs 52%, HR 0.72); no gallbladder-only randomised estimate exists
5357: SPLIT — short term: excision beat aspiration plus steroid in the only randomised trial (success 94.4% vs 61.1%, 36 patients) · long term (prospective cohort, mean 70 months): recurrence 39% after excision and 58% after aspiration, symptom resolution no different from no treatment, and 23 of 55 untreated ganglia resolved on their own
5358: POSSIBLE — observational evidence only (no randomised trials): youth cohorts associate starting hormones/blockers with better 12-month depression and suicidality odds (aOR 0.40 and 0.27, relative); Swedish registers found no association between years on hormones and mental-health treatment (aOR 1.01/year) and, after correction, no surgery advantage; long-term post-surgical mortality stayed above general-population levels (aHR 2.8); transfeminine estrogen carried a venous thromboembolism excess (16.7 per 1,000 by 8 years)
5359: POSSIBLE (benefit) — beyond the standard creams (homed on #2198): cryotherapy clearance matched the topical treatments across 11 RCTs, sinecatechins beat vehicle (complete clearance 53.6–54.9% vs 35.4%, two phase III trials), and adding quadrivalent HPV vaccine to treatment was not shown to help (aOR 1.46, 95% CI 0.97–2.20)
5360: MAYBE (weak evidence) (the treatment made no difference) — for routine symptom control: Cochrane found steroid benefit only at 12 hours and not maintained (7 trials), antiviral evidence very low quality with effectiveness uncertain (7 trials, 333 participants), and the single-dose dexamethasone trial's pain advantage (60% vs 26% at 12 hours) had vanished by 24 hours
5361: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no controlled trials exist; in the one systematic review of generalised disease (689 patients, all case reports/series), complete response ranged from 17.7% on topical steroids to 82.8–84% in small JAK-inhibitor and anti-TNF case collections, with the review itself warning that spontaneous remission and publication bias cannot be excluded
5363: SPLIT — pooled across all trials, IVIG is associated with fewer exchange transfusions (typical RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.49; risk difference −0.22; NNTB 5) · in the only two trials that masked treatment with a placebo and blinded outcome assessment, there was no difference (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.48 to 1.98) — the apparent benefit lives in the high-risk-of-bias trials
5364: MAYBE (weak evidence) — IVIG added to conventional therapy shortened fever clearance, rash regression and clinical cure times in a meta-analysis of 8 small RCTs (1,450 children), with no mortality outcome and no pooled effect sizes in the abstract; large retrospective hospital series find no advantage for IVIG or steroids, and one stage-stratified series found an IVIG association only in early stage IV disease; methylprednisolone and milrinone showed no mortality benefit at any stage
5365: SPLIT — acute treatment: paracetamol 1000 mg and ibuprofen 400 mg are each modestly better than placebo for a single attack (pain-free at 2 hours in 24 vs 19 and 23 vs 16 per 100 people) · prevention: tricyclic antidepressants reduce headache frequency by about 4.8 headaches/month versus placebo, and acupuncture roughly doubles-to-triples the responder rate versus routine care but exceeds sham acupuncture only slightly (relative risk 1.3)
5366: SPLIT — treating symptoms: prednisone eased abdominal and joint pain scores in the largest placebo-controlled trial and steroids speeded abdominal-pain resolution in the pooled record (POSSIBLE benefit) · treating established kidney disease: Cochrane found no significant effect of prednisone on persistent kidney disease (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.32) and no benefit for cyclophosphamide · kidney-disease PREVENTION is not this shelf's question — it is homed on Shelf #3914

5651: SPLIT (BMD: benefit; fractures and safety in stage 3 CKD: unproven): bisphosphonates improve bone mineral density in CKD stage 3, but no carded source demonstrates fewer fractures in this population, and safety signals (hypocalcaemia HR 1.324; CKD progression HR 1.12 in a cohort; a fracture signal in the small G3B subgroup) are unresolved
5652: SPLIT — observational only (by diabetes status): in the first 2 years, peritoneal dialysis survival was similar to or slightly better than hemodialysis in general incident populations (matched HR 0.92; 24-month survival 71.1% vs 68.0%), but diabetic cohorts associate peritoneal dialysis with higher mortality (HR 1.20); no randomised evidence exists
5653: POSSIBLE (benefit): more frequent dialysis improved left ventricular mass and volumes on cardiac imaging in small randomised trials (between-group mass difference 15.3 g in the 52-patient nocturnal trial; −11.0% end-diastolic volume with frequent in-center dialysis in FHN) — surrogate outcomes over 6–12 months, no mortality-powered trial
5654: LIKELY (benefit): tacrolimus prevents acute rejection better than cyclosporine (30.7% vs 46.4% and 19.6% vs 37.3% in two large randomised trials; pooled relative risk 0.69 at 1 year, graft loss RR 0.56), with more posttransplant diabetes (19.9% vs 4.0%; pooled RR 1.86 for insulin-requiring diabetes) as the trade-off
5669: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: holding a GLP-1 receptor agonist before elective endoscopy was associated with less retained gastric content (4.4% vs 12.7% in the one study that classified holding), but no study shows fewer aspirations, no trial has randomised holding, and patients with diagnosed gastroparesis were excluded from the key cohort
5670: POSSIBLE (benefit, infliximab) — indirect and observational only: no head-to-head randomised trial exists; infliximab ranked first for induction in a network meta-analysis and showed less symptomatic non-response in one cohort, while persistence, surgery and hospitalisation were equal — its clearest advantage is in perianal Crohn's disease
5671: SPLIT (maintenance monitoring: benefit — NOR-DRUM B sustained control 73.6% vs 55.9% and TAXIT flare reduction after level correction; induction/escalation monitoring: no benefit — NOR-DRUM A and TAILORIX both null on remission)
5672: SPLIT (calprotectin-guided management: benefit on composite and subgroup outcomes in ulcerative colitis — OPTIMISE composites and Lasson's calprotectin-risen subgroup; no significant benefit on any carded trial's primary endpoint, and none for treat-to-target in Crohn's disease in STARDUST; the positive CALM trial is homed on live shelf #324)
5673: MAYBE (weak evidence): no randomised trial has ever tested a low-residue diet during an ulcerative colitis flare — the Cochrane review found the whole diet literature in IBD uncertain, so the practice is unproven rather than disproven
5674: MAYBE (weak evidence): the combination has never been randomised against metronidazole alone in acute pouchitis — the only head-to-head trial (N = 16) favours ciprofloxacin alone, and combination evidence is a single-arm study in refractory disease
5675: SPLIT — observational only (quitting worsened colitis activity and treatment needs in a small matched cohort, Beaugerie 2001; a nationwide cohort of 6,754 patients found no worse outcomes in quitters than in persistent smokers, Blackwell 2019)
5676: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: continuing biologics through pregnancy was not associated with malformations, abortion, preterm birth, low birth weight or infant infection in 1,490 PIANO-registry pregnancies, while higher disease activity was (spontaneous abortion HR 3.41)
5677: SPLIT (medical remission: possible benefit — pooled relative risk of relapse 0.47 across small trials, anchor trial 13% vs 29%, P = 0.06; postoperative recurrence: no benefit — the largest trial found endoscopic recurrence 58% vs 66% on high-dose vitamin D)
5678: POSSIBLE (benefit) — diagnostic-yield evidence only: about 28–32% of IBS-D patients have bile acid malabsorption on SeHCAT testing and most respond to a bile acid binder, so testing before rifaximin identifies a large treatable subgroup — but no trial has tested the test-first sequence, and blood tests miss cases (FGF19 sensitivity 58%)
5679: SPLIT (guideline practice: benefit; randomised comparisons: no added benefit, possible harm) — sodium restriction is standard adjunct care for ascites, but the carded randomised comparison of 40 versus 120 mmol/day found the diet made no difference to diuretic response, and reviews describe the trial conclusions on restriction as contradictory
5681: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: in strictly selected patients with severe alcohol-related hepatitis not responding to medical therapy, early transplantation was associated with much higher survival (6-month 77% vs 23% in the founding cohort) and post-transplant survival similar to standard transplantation, but alcohol relapse was not shown non-inferior and high-intake relapse was more frequent
5682: MAYBE (weak evidence) — one small randomised crossover trial (n = 24) found fat digestion tended to be better when enzymes were taken distributed along with meals or just after meals than just before; no other randomised timing evidence exists in the carded records
5683: POSSIBLE (benefit) — pooled series show complete ductal clearance in 69.8% and complete pain relief in 64.2% after ESWL for large pancreatic duct stones, and the one randomised trial found ESWL alone matched ESWL plus endoscopy for pain relapse at one-third of the cost; no carded trial compares ESWL with no ESWL
5684: LIKELY (benefit) for visualization — simethicone consistently reduced bubbles/foam and improved cleansing across randomised trials and two meta-analyses, and lessened bloating; adenoma detection divided the meta-analyses (increased in one, no significant overall increase in the larger one, with benefit confined to single-dose preparation)
5685: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only: GLP-1 use is associated with more retained gastric contents and, in one cohort, poorer bowel preparation and more repeat colonoscopies, but absolute aborted-procedure rates were low (0.6%) and no aspiration excess was shown — the records do not establish that routine stopping before colonoscopy is needed
5686: LIKELY (benefit) — for polyps ≥20 mm, especially proximal: clip closure reduced postprocedure bleeding from 7.1% to 3.5% in the randomised trial (proximal: 9.6% to 3.3%), and randomised meta-analyses agree (relative risk 0.47–0.54 relative for ≥20 mm); little to no benefit for smaller or distal lesions
5687: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (DIRECT): elective sigmoidectomy improved quality of life at 6 months and 5 years in patients with recurrent (≥3 presentations in 2 years) or persistent complaints, at the cost of anastomotic leakage in about 11–15% of operated patients; the trial did not test an automatic resection rule after exactly two episodes
5688: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme: in the one randomised trial, biofeedback gave adequate relief to 87% of patients with examination-confirmed levator ani syndrome versus 45% for electrogalvanic stimulation and 22% for massage, maintained at 12 months; patients without levator tenderness did not benefit from any treatment
5689: MAYBE (weak evidence) — fat-intake-based enzyme dosing is the conventional framework and the regimen used in a positive placebo-controlled trial (fat absorption 88.6% vs 49.6%), but a fixed-dose regimen also beat placebo and no trial has ever compared fat-adjusted versus fixed dosing; the Cochrane review states there is no evidence on dose variations based on meals or meal sizes
5690: SPLIT (small trials/meta-analysis: benefit — flatus 10.4 hours and bowel movement 12.7 hours earlier across 81 trials; largest enhanced-recovery trial, n = 402: the treatment made no difference to bowel function or hospital stay)
5691: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: pulmonary valve replacement was associated with a lower risk of death or sustained ventricular tachycardia (adjusted HR 0.41) in a propensity-matched registry analysis, concentrated in advanced right ventricular dilatation, but no randomised or comparative mortality trial exists and an earlier analysis of the same registry was null
5692: LIKELY (benefit) — using an inhaled corticosteroid with every reliever use reduced severe exacerbations versus reliever alone or usual care (0.69 vs 0.82 per year, HR 0.85, in the reliever-triggered trial; 0.195 vs 0.400 per year, relative rate 0.49, for reliever-carried budesonide–formoterol) and matched daily maintenance for exacerbations in mild asthma
5693: MAYBE (weak evidence) — nebulised therapy is not shown to be better than inhaler-plus-spacer therapy in COPD (primary outcome FEV1 at one hour: the treatment made no difference, across 8 trials and 250 participants), and no trial has enrolled the poor-inhaler-technique population this question is about
5694: LIKELY (criteria as modelled) — at least 20 pack-years and quit within 15 years, ages 50–80, is the modelling-supported eligibility rule (estimated 469–558 vs 381 deaths averted per 100,000 versus the old 30 pack-year rule); the quit-time limit is contested, with the American Cancer Society dropping it entirely, and risk-model selection estimated to outperform any pack-year rule
5695: POSSIBLE (harm) — avoid sedating antihistamines for sleep: diphenhydramine's trial benefit is small (one improved diary measure in elderly insomniacs; modest 14-day gains in mild insomnia), tolerance develops rapidly, and sedative harms are documented in older adults — and no trial has tested these drugs in adults with insomnia and depression at all
5696: POSSIBLE (benefit) — for post-stroke depression (one open 70-patient prevention trial: depression in 5.7% vs 40%; top response ranking in a 51-trial network meta-analysis), but the sleep benefit rests on a single uncontrolled 10-patient study that also showed worsened sleep apnoea in some patients
5697: MAYBE (weak evidence) — tapering gets many older adults off Z-drugs (discontinuation 56%/55% vs 26% at 6 months in the one Z-drug trial), but no trial has measured long-term sleep quality after Z-drug tapering, and adjacent benzodiazepine follow-up shows 42.6% relapse by 24 months
5698: MAYBE (weak evidence) — caffeine taken even 6 hours before bed significantly disrupted sleep in a randomised timing study, and a 24-study meta-analysis put the latest safe time for a standard coffee at 8.8 hours before bed (13.2 hours for high-dose products), but a midday cutoff itself has never been trialled and no carded study enrolled adults with insomnia
5699: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: across large routine-practice cohorts apixaban was consistently associated with less major and gastrointestinal bleeding than rivaroxaban, with no consistent difference in stroke or systemic embolism prevention; no head-to-head randomised trial exists
5701: MAYBE (weak evidence) — dual antiplatelet therapy clearly reduced microembolic signals in two small randomised trials in symptomatic large-artery stenosis, but no trial has been powered to show it reduces clinical stroke after minor stroke with carotid stenosis, and the one carotid subgroup analysis compares two dual regimens rather than dual versus single therapy
5704: POSSIBLE (benefit) — starting by day 4 rather than waiting to day 14: a small dedicated randomised trial in mild-to-moderate stroke favoured the earliest start, and a pooled analysis of 5,441 randomised patients found fewer 30-day recurrences with starts within 4 days and no increase in symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage; no trial isolates exactly day 4 versus day 14 within moderate stroke alone
5705: LIKELY (benefit) — carotid endarterectomy within 14 days of the symptomatic event: in the pooled randomised trials the benefit of surgery was greatest in patients randomised within 2 weeks (number needed to treat 5, versus 125 after more than 12 weeks), and in neurologically stable patients early surgery carried no higher operative risk than later surgery
5706: POSSIBLE (benefit) — intensive lowering toward below 120 mm Hg systolic: the one dedicated trial was stopped early and its own result was not significant (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.49 to 1.11), but pooled with three earlier trials intensive control reduced recurrent stroke (relative risk 0.78, absolute difference 1.5 percentage points, number needed to treat 67); achieved pressures in the trials fell well short of the below-120 target
5708: MAYBE (weak evidence) — oral baclofen versus tizanidine for post-stroke spasticity: the only head-to-head data pool multiple sclerosis with cerebrovascular lesions and show similar tone reduction with either drug; no trial has compared the two drugs in post-stroke spasticity alone, and systematic reviewers rate the whole oral-antispastic evidence base as weak
5709: POSSIBLE (benefit) — rTMS improved naming and other language measures across small randomised trials (47-trial meta-analysis, 2,190 patients, no pooled effect size in its record; one sham-controlled trial, N = 44, aphasia-quotient gain ~13–15 points over sham); protocols vary and no large multicentre trial exists
5710: LIKELY (benefit — fewer gastrointestinal side effects) — in the IDEAL randomised trial (N = 1,195) the 9.5 mg/24 h patch caused nausea in 7.2% vs 23.1% on capsules and vomiting in 6.2% vs 17.0%, at similar efficacy; single trial programme, standard dose only
5711: LIKELY (risk — trial safety data + observational cohorts, labelled on the face) — ARIA-E in 34.5% of ApoE ε4 homozygotes vs 16.8% of ε4 carriers overall on lecanemab (Clarity AD safety data); ARIA-H microhaemorrhages in 16.0% of all treated; real-world ARIA in 44% of homozygotes (4/9) vs 17% of heterozygotes
5712: SPLIT (fewer dyskinesias: benefit — pooled odds ratio 0.51 vs levodopa, 29 trials, 5,247 participants; symptom control and tolerability: harm — levodopa gave significantly better motor relief in both long trials, and agonists doubled discontinuations for adverse events, odds ratio 2.49)
5713: LIKELY (benefit) — extended-release carbidopa-levodopa reduced off time vs immediate-release (23.8% vs 29.8% of waking hours; extra -1.17 h/day) in a phase 3 RCT (N = 393), with a concordant phase 3 win vs immediate-release plus entacapone (3.8 vs 5.2 h/day, N = 91); conversion raised total levodopa dose
5714: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only: manufacturer switching was associated with breakthrough seizures in a nationwide cohort (brand-to-generic odds ratio 1.85, relative; switch rates 5.5% vs 2.4%), with case evidence of lower drug levels after switching; pharmacokinetic studies show no average difference and clinical reports conflict
5715: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: early high-efficacy therapy was associated with less disability accrual than escalation in three large cohorts (5-year EDSS change 0.3 vs 1.2; 10-year gap 0.63–0.67 EDSS points; escalation hazard ratio 1.36 for confirmed accrual, relative); no randomised strategy trial has reported
5716: POSSIBLE (no benefit shown) — pooled randomised trials found no reduction in annualised relapse rate (rate difference -0.05, 95% CI -0.17 to 0.07; 12 trials, 933 participants; the treatment made no difference), a dose-ranging early-disease trial was null at all doses, and blood levels rose without moving a nerve-injury biomarker
5717: LIKELY (benefit) — exercise reduced fatigue vs no exercise across 45 randomised trials (2,250 participants; standardised mean difference -0.53, 95% CI -0.73 to -0.33), a 58-study network analysis ranked combined and resistance training best, and a trial in fatigued patients showed ~10-point fatigue-score gains
5718: POSSIBLE (benefit) — plasma exchange beat sham (42.1% vs 5.9% of courses with moderate-or-better improvement) in the single small randomised trial of steroid-refractory attacks, with 59–79% improving in two observational cohorts (N = 153 and 118); earlier treatment responded better
5719: LIKELY (benefit): IV immunoglobulin improves strength and function in multifocal motor neuropathy — two small placebo-controlled trials agree (disability score +6.7 vs −2.1 points; responders 7/9 vs 2/9), and the Cochrane synthesis of six crossover trials (90 participants) found strength improved in 78% on IVIg versus 4% on placebo (relative risk 11.00, low-certainty evidence)
5720: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme: erenumab reduced monthly migraine days by 2.5 days more than placebo in chronic migraine (667 patients), and in the subgroup with at least one prior preventive failure the advantage was −2.5 days (70 mg) and −3.3 days (140 mg), rising to −4.3 days at 140 mg after at least two failures
5721: POSSIBLE (benefit of continuing) — observational only: in the one real-life cohort, 20% of patients below a 30% response at 3 months reached at least 30% by months 4–6, and no carded guideline validates a 30%-at-3-months stopping rule — continue to about 6 months before deciding
5722: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single direct trial: gabapentin plus nortriptyline reduced pain to 2.3/10 versus 3.2 on gabapentin alone and 2.9 on nortriptyline alone at maximum tolerated dose (differences −0.9 and −0.6 points), with the Cochrane combination review confirming this pairing rests on that one 56-patient trial
5723: SPLIT (randomised open-label trial: tapentadol benefit; routine-practice registry analysis: oxycodone/naloxone benefit) — and the tested comparator throughout is oxycodone/naloxone, not oxycodone alone, for which no head-to-head record was found
5724: MAYBE (weak evidence): starting amitriptyline at 10 mg at night in older adults is an untested, prudence-based convention — no carded trial tests that dose or population, geriatric reviews advise lowest therapeutic doses, and amitriptyline's own efficacy evidence is third-tier only (adverse events 55% vs 36% on placebo, relative risk 1.5)
5725: SPLIT (immediate rehabilitation: the treatment made no difference — recovery odds ratio 1.0 and no outcome differed at 26 weeks; rehabilitation starting at 4–6 weeks: benefit over no treatment for pain and function, standardised mean differences −0.90 and −0.67, low-quality evidence)
5726: SPLIT (pain: possible small improvement after tapering in a mostly poor-quality meta-analysis, with no significant improvement in physical functioning and only stable pain in the one randomised trial; harms: tapering associated with overdose 9.3 vs 5.5 and mental-health crisis 7.6 vs 3.3 per 100 person-years in a 113,618-patient cohort)
5727: SPLIT (guidelines recommend high-dose 5 mg folic acid periconceptionally for women on anti-seizure medications; the 2,104-pregnancy register analysis found no significant effect of folic acid dose on malformation rates or spina bifida, and a register cohort links high-dose exposure to childhood cancer at adjusted hazard ratio 2.7 relative, absolute 1.4% vs 0.6%)
5728: POSSIBLE (benefit) — small effect for the named tested preparations (THC/CBD oromucosal spray including nabiximols, dronabinol, nabilone, trial-prepared herbal cannabis; no manufacturer named in the records): 30% pain relief 39% vs 33% on placebo (NNTB 11) and 50% relief 21% vs 17% (NNTB 20), against nervous system adverse events 61% vs 29% (NNTH 3)
5729: POSSIBLE (benefit) — switching after SSRI nonresponse remits about 1 in 4 patients: a second SSRI remitted 23.5% versus 28% for switching class in pooled randomised trials (relative risk 1.29, NNT about 22), and an early-switch strategy did not beat guideline care (24% versus 16%, not significant)
5731: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only: valproate in pregnancy is consistently associated with specific malformations (spina bifida adjusted odds ratio 12.7), a dose-dependent malformation risk, and lower child IQ (97 versus 105–108) — avoid in women of childbearing potential with bipolar disorder whenever an effective alternative exists
5732: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no trial has tested buspirone added to an SSRI for generalised anxiety disorder after SSRI nonresponse; buspirone beats placebo as GAD monotherapy (NNT 4.4) and matched bupropion as an add-on in depression (remission 30.1%), but neither result is the asked use
5733: SPLIT (psychotherapy benefit consistent; antidepressant safety signals divide) — psychotherapy beats control in 80+ randomised trials (NNT 4.39), the largest adjusted cohort found no cardiac-malformation increase (relative risk 1.06), but a depressed-women cohort found citalopram and paroxetine signals; no head-to-head drug-versus-therapy trial in pregnancy is carded
5734: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on exposure data (evidence types labelled on the cards): sertraline usually produces undetectable infant plasma levels in pooled level data, 87.4% of 167 infant levels were below detection in meta-analysis, and the calculated infant dose was 0.54% of the maternal dose — among the preferred antidepressants in breastfeeding
5735: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: combination immunosuppression was associated with longer survival in the multicentre series (average 12.3 versus 3.0 months) and suppresses biopsy inflammation, but there is no randomised trial, relapse continues for years, and fulminant cases usually still require transplantation
5736: POSSIBLE (benefit) — 300 mg/day gave slightly more pain relief than 150 mg/day in the one direct dose-ranging trial (placebo-adjusted reductions 1.07 versus 0.88 points), a small average gain; 600 mg/day gave more relief (1.79 points) with more adverse effects
5737: LIKELY (benefit) — short-term only: clinically relevant pain relief for about 2–6 weeks after one injection, a small residual benefit to about 13 weeks, and no benefit by 26 weeks (the treatment made no difference at 6 months)
5738: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no randomised trial of gabapentin taper schedules in chronic pain was found in the records fetched; taper gradually rather than stopping abruptly (abrupt cessation is associated with seizures), with a short taper sufficient after months of use in trial conditions and slower, monitored tapers after long-term or high-dose use or a substance-use history
5739: SPLIT (short trials: benefit; beyond 12 weeks: no benefit shown) — tramadol beat placebo in trials lasting about 13 weeks or less, but there are no placebo-controlled trials supporting effectiveness beyond 12 weeks, and the one 56-week trial found tramadol made no difference versus placebo at week 16
5740: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: withdrawing culprit (especially cardiovascular) medications was followed by about half the fall hazard and by resolution of orthostatic hypotension on retesting in prospective cohort data, but no randomised trial of stopping these drugs has ever reported falls or syncope
5743: LIKELY (benefit) — procalcitonin guidance safely reduces antibiotic duration in adults with pneumonia (median 12 to 5 days in the pneumonia-only trial; 10.7 to 7.2 days in the large trial's pneumonia subgroup), with no worse outcomes and fewer antibiotic side-effects
5744: MAYBE (weak evidence) — prolongation beyond 6 months has never been tested in tuberculosis with diabetes: diabetes is associated with more failure, death and relapse on standard treatment (relapse relative risk 3.89), but no study shows longer treatment removes that excess
5745: POSSIBLE (no benefit shown) — the one randomised trial of gabapentin started within 72 hours of rash onset found the treatment made no difference to pain at 12 weeks (18.2% vs 9.5% with placebo), and no early drug treatment, gabapentin included, has been shown to prevent postherpetic neuralgia
5746: MAYBE (weak evidence) — observational only: no trial has randomised treatment duration in acute prostatitis; cohorts show relapse tracks drug adequacy (OR 12.3 for inadequate therapy), and the standing guideline standard is about 14 days, with shorter courses validated only for male cystitis and selected bacteraemic urinary infections
5748: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: a COVID booster reduces the relative risk of hospitalisation by roughly half in the first weeks (53.0% at 2–4 weeks, waning to 35.9% after 10+ weeks), but the absolute benefit for adults aged 50–64 without major risk factors is small (overall median number needed to vaccinate 205 to prevent one hospitalisation, least favourable in younger, healthier adults) and no study isolates that exact subgroup
5749: LIKELY — earlier timing within the 60 minutes before incision made no difference: the randomised trial (OR 0.93) and the 54,552-patient meta-analysis agree there is no timing gradient inside the window; infection risk rises only when prophylaxis is given after incision (OR 1.89) or more than 120 minutes before it (OR 5.26)
5750: MAYBE (weak evidence) — starting antivirals after 72 hours is untested: every trial enrolled patients within 72 hours of rash onset, where famciclovir shortened neuralgia by about 2 months but aciclovir did not significantly prevent neuralgia in the Cochrane review; no effect size exists for a late start
5751: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no head-to-head trial shows antibiotic ointment superior to warm compresses and lid hygiene, and the Cochrane review (34 studies, 2,169 participants) found symptomatic relief from both but no strong evidence any treatment cures chronic blepharitis; antibiotics additionally eradicate lid-margin bacteria in anterior disease
5753: LIKELY (as effective for haemoglobin control) — vadadustat (3,923 patients), roxadustat (2,133) and daprodustat (312) each met haemoglobin noninferiority against an ESA on dialysis, and a 17-trial network meta-analysis finds the class broadly comparable; the stamp covers haemoglobin, not long-term safety
5754: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: rotation to or addition of methadone under specialist supervision relieved refractory neuropathic cancer pain in about half to two-thirds of patients in three small uncontrolled series (N = 48, 19, 19); no randomised trial tests methadone for this indication, and the Cochrane review restricts initiation to experienced practitioners
5755: SPLIT — pooled trials show a small short-term pain reduction from adding a corticosteroid (0.84 points at one week, low-quality evidence), but the dedicated randomised adjuvant trial of dexamethasone 8 mg found no added analgesia (the treatment made no difference to pain intensity or opioid use)
5756: POSSIBLE (benefit) — as an adjunct to standard antiemetics: acupuncture-point stimulation modestly improves nausea control (complete protection 52.9% versus 34.5% in the best sham-controlled trial) and slightly reduces acute vomiting relatively (RR 0.82), on evidence of low certainty; it does not replace antiemetic drugs
5757: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only for the over-80 post-MI question: cohorts associate continuation with fewer events (HR 0.81) and discontinuation with 13 excess events per 1,000 person-years, and trial meta-analysis shows mortality benefit in elderly secondary prevention up to age 82 — but continuing versus stopping past 80 has never been randomised
5758: LIKELY (benefit) for treating hypertension and aiming lower — systolic below 140 and toward 120–130 mm Hg if tolerated — in ambulatory older adults; no trial isolates patients over 85, so the target past 85 is extrapolated from trials at 75–80+ (SPRINT ≥75: HR 0.66 for events, 0.67 for mortality) and must be individualised for frailty
5759: POSSIBLE (no increase in falls detected) — intensive lowering did not increase injurious falls in SPRINT's age-75+ report (4.9% vs 5.5%), its age-80+ report, or its frailty analysis, and a 21-trial review agrees; one trial programme plus a review, in ambulatory volunteers rather than institutionalised frail patients
5760: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no increase in cardiovascular events demonstrated after supervised deprescribing (TONE event rates flat; Cochrane differences null), but trials are small, intervals wide (mortality odds ratio 2.08, 95% CI 0.79–5.46, relative) and frail long-term-care data are sparse and unpooled
5761: SPLIT (cluster and pooled evidence: benefit, pooled odds ratio 0.40 relative; individually randomised trials: the treatment made no difference — HIP PRO 3.1% protected vs 2.5% unprotected hips)
5762: SPLIT (tighter targets cause severe hypoglycaemia in trials, relative risk 2.18 relative; but in older adults A1C level itself did not predict hypoglycaemia — insulin/sulfonylurea burden did; no trial has randomised frail patients to <8.5% vs <7.5% targets)
5763: MAYBE (weak evidence) — cognition and balance measures improved after stopping in small uncontrolled studies (n = 30 and n = 89, printed on their faces) and tapering is achievable (62% vs 21%), but no carded study counted falls after benzodiazepine-only discontinuation
5764: LIKELY (benefit) — postoperative delirium fell in both carded surgical trials of multicomponent Elder Life Programs (2.6% vs 19.4%, relative risk 0.14 relative; 6.6% vs 15.1%, relative risk 0.44 relative), with a concordant program meta-analysis (odds ratio 0.47, relative)
5765: SPLIT — observational only for vascular risk (headache course divides by regimen: withdrawal-interval worsening on standard pills, improvement in one small step-down-pill pilot; ischaemic-stroke risk with aura consistently increased in observational studies, relative risk up to 8.72 relative in the older meta-analysis)
5766: POSSIBLE (topical safer; as effective untested head-to-head) — observational only for safety: topical imidazoles are effective in pregnancy trials (clotrimazole vs placebo odds ratio 0.14 relative), while oral fluconazole shows small absolute risk increases across three large cohorts (musculoskeletal adjusted relative risk 1.30 relative vs topical azoles; miscarriage odds ratio 2.23 relative at 150 mg)
5767: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only: estrogen-containing contraception carries the highest stroke odds in migraine with aura (odds ratio 6.1 relative for combined exposure); progestin-only methods show no stroke signal because the systematic review found no stroke studies of them — their supporting evidence is headache relief, not vascular outcomes
5768: LIKELY (equal benefit) — transdermal estradiol matched oral estrogen for hot-flash relief in KEEPS (7.4% vs 4.2% still flushing at 6 months, vs 28.3% placebo; no significant difference between routes) and in the head-to-head trial and 32-trial review (the route made no difference)
5769: SPLIT (short-term endometrial histology: protection comparable to synthetic progestins in a randomised trial; long-term endometrial cancer: a large cohort associates micronized progesterone — unlike synthetic derivatives — with increased risk, especially beyond 5 years)
5770: SPLIT (efficacy: divided — null on the primary outcome of the one placebo-controlled trial and inferior to CBT in a small trial; breastfeeding safety: consistently very low infant exposure in observational pharmacokinetic data, with no infant adverse events reported)
5771: POSSIBLE — observational and modelling evidence only: screening can be stopped at 65 when adequate prior screening is documented and the woman is not at high risk (USPSTF D recommendation against further screening in that group); a negative HPV exit test marks the lowest remaining risk (modelled 1 in 6,525 lifetime) — do not stop on age alone when the history is inadequate or unknown
5772: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: twice-daily PPI (esomeprazole 1 mg/kg per dose) induced histological remission in about half to two-thirds of children in prospective cohorts (68.6% response at 8 weeks; 50.5% pooled remission), with no randomised trial in children and no significant twice-daily advantage over once-daily dosing in the pooled data
5774: POSSIBLE (benefit): universal screening with intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis is associated with substantially less early-onset newborn GBS infection (treatment RR 0.17 relative in small trials; screening vs risk-based RR 0.43 relative observationally) — trial evidence small and at high risk of bias, strategy evidence observational, and no mortality effect shown
5775: LIKELY (benefit): Rh(D) immune globulin prevents alloimmunisation — postpartum anti-D cut it to RR 0.04 relative at 6 months (six trials, over 10,000 women) and antenatal prophylaxis reduced first-pregnancy alloimmunisation from about 1% to about 0.2% — thereby preventing hemolytic disease of the newborn in subsequent pregnancies; trials measured alloimmunisation, not hemolytic disease itself
5777: POSSIBLE (no association) — observational only: MMR vaccination was not associated with autism in nationwide cohorts of 657,461 and 537,303 children (adjusted HR 0.93 relative; RR 0.92 relative) or in a 1,256,407-child meta-analysis (OR 0.84 relative), with no clustering of diagnoses after vaccination and no increased risk in susceptible subgroups
5778: SPLIT (protection: equal — MMRV immunogenicity and 1-year persistence comparable to separate MMR + varicella; safety: MMRV carries about twice the relative risk of febrile seizure 7–10 days after the first dose, RR 1.98 relative, an excess of 4.3 per 10,000 doses or 1 extra seizure per 2,300 doses)
5789: POSSIBLE (benefit): vitamin D deficiency is common on enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (54% vs 37% on non-inducing drugs in 596 adults) and a small randomised trial shows supplementation prevents the fall in levels — monitor and supplement when low; clinical-outcome (fracture) benefit is untested
5790: SPLIT (amputation-free survival in the RCT: endovascular-first better; graft patency in pooled series: vein bypass better): bypass-first did not improve amputation-free survival in BASIL-2 (63% vs 53% primary outcome, adjusted HR 1.35), while vein grafts show the highest infrapopliteal patency (87% at 1 year)
5792: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: preoperative BNP independently predicts perioperative cardiac events (pooled OR 19.3) and improves on the Revised Cardiac Risk Index (net reclassification improvement 58%, 84% in intermediate risk); no trial has tested BNP-guided management
5793: POSSIBLE (benefit) — indirect evidence only: radioiodine leaves roughly 27–59% of patients euthyroid long term (dose-dependent: 41% hypothyroid at 60–100 months in one trial arm; 73% with a 150 Gy regimen), a chance total thyroidectomy does not offer; no head-to-head trial versus surgery exists
5794: POSSIBLE (benefit): preoperative oral supplementation reduced postoperative complications in pooled gastrointestinal-cancer trials (relative risk 0.53; absolute risk reduction 0.14, NNT 7), with individual trials agreeing on minor/serious complications but showing no difference in major complications
5795: MAYBE (weak evidence): surgery and radioiodine each relieve compressive symptoms in their own uncontrolled series (relief in all 30 radioiodine patients; significant post-thyroidectomy gains in breathlessness, dysphagia and quality of life) — no head-to-head comparison exists
5796: POSSIBLE (benefit): earlier (expedited/immediate) cataract surgery improves visual acuity sooner than waiting (OR 7.22 for acuity improvement; −0.15 logMAR at 6 months) — quality-of-life benefit is inferred from acuity, and no falls benefit is proven (OR 0.81, not significant)
5797: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: screening echocardiography detects bicuspid aortic valve in 6.6–14% of first-degree relatives (plus aortic dilatation in 2.9%); a model finds screening cost-saving, but no trial shows detection improves outcomes
5798: MAYBE (weak evidence): ambulatory monitoring reclassifies suspected white coat hypertension (office accuracy only 54.8%) and the confirmed group carries higher risk if untreated (HR 1.36 for events), but no trial shows monitoring-guided care changes hard outcomes
5799: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only for the mortality association: annual surveillance mammography after treatment is the schedule tested in follow-up trials and linked in cohort data to lower breast cancer mortality; no randomised trial has compared annual with less frequent mammography
5800: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only: combined oral contraceptives are associated with a several-fold higher venous thromboembolism risk than non-use, whereas oral progestin-only pills are not associated with increased risk, so the combined pill carries the higher risk in an indirect comparison through non-users
5801: SPLIT (oestrogen-only: lower breast cancer incidence and mortality in the WHI trial; oestrogen plus progestagen: higher breast cancer incidence, rising with duration) — all-cause mortality neutral over 18 years in both trials; no duration of combined therapy is shown to be free of breast cancer risk
5802: POSSIBLE (safest-exposure ranking) — observational only: sertraline and paroxetine show the lowest measured infant exposure and fluoxetine the most concerning signal, but all carded evidence is small pharmacokinetic or cohort data with no randomised infant-outcome comparison
5803: MAYBE (weak evidence) — foam dressings have not been shown to heal pressure ulcers better than simple dressings: pooled healing risk ratios versus basic wound contact dressings were 1.33 and 1.17 (both not significant) on very low-certainty evidence
5804: MAYBE (weak evidence) — for stopping at 74/75: the recommendation to screen to 74 rests on trials that included women only up to their early 70s; for women 75 and older the evidence is insufficient to determine the balance of benefits and harms, so there is no evidence-proven stopping age, only a boundary of the evidence at 74
5805: LIKELY (benefit) — brief advice from a clinician increases quitting (physician advice relative risk 1.66, an absolute gain of about 1–3 percentage points), supported by three concordant Cochrane meta-analyses of randomised trials
5806: POSSIBLE (no benefit) — the one randomised trial shows short-term urine clearance without durable or clinical benefit (the treatment made no difference to candiduria rates two weeks after therapy), and cohort follow-up finds no outcome advantage for treated patients
5808: POSSIBLE (benefit) — empagliflozin's HFmrEF evidence is the mildly-reduced subgroup of a single trial programme (EMPEROR-Preserved, homed elsewhere) plus concordant class-level pooling that separates HFmrEF (hazard ratio 0.77); a single trial programme caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
5809: LIKELY (benefit) — in HFrEF with LBBB, cardiac resynchronization therapy reduces death or heart failure hospitalisation across concordant trial-level and patient-level meta-analyses; the benefit is morphology-specific and is not seen in non-LBBB wide QRS
5810: SPLIT (older randomised evidence: benefit on all-cause mortality; DANISH long-term follow-up: no all-cause mortality benefit, sudden-death benefit persists) — an ICD reliably prevents sudden arrhythmic death in nonischemic cardiomyopathy, but whether it prolongs overall survival divides by era and follow-up length
5811: POSSIBLE (benefit) — early initiation in acute heart failure reduces death and rehospitalisation in a 7-trial meta-analysis, concordant with the acute-HF trial programmes homed elsewhere; capped at POSSIBLE because the timing-specific pooling rests substantially on small trials and safety outcomes could not be determined
5812: POSSIBLE (benefit) — in elderly patients with atrial fibrillation, edoxaban reduces major bleeding compared with warfarin (hazard ratio 0.83 at age ≥75, with greater absolute benefit at older ages); a single trial programme (ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48) caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
5813: POSSIBLE (benefit of discontinuation in moderate-risk patients) — pooled randomised trials show no significant thromboembolic increase after stopping anticoagulation following successful ablation and significantly more bleeding with continuation; the total randomised base is 2,324 patients at moderate stroke risk, so this does not extend to higher-risk patients
5814: SPLIT (randomised evidence: no mortality increase; observational evidence: higher mortality with digoxin) — digoxin's safety for rate control in AF with heart failure is unresolved: the harm signal lives in observational data prone to prescription bias, and the AF-with-HF subgroup itself divides between meta-analyses
5815: POSSIBLE (benefit) — andexanet alfa reverses anti-Xa activity and achieves good or excellent haemostasis in about 4 of 5 patients in a single-arm programme, and observational comparison favours it over 4-factor PCC for in-hospital mortality; with no randomised trial in major bleeding generally, this caps at POSSIBLE
5816: POSSIBLE (benefit) — idarucizumab rapidly and completely reverses dabigatran and is followed by timely bleeding cessation and normal procedural haemostasis in the single-arm RE-VERSE AD programme; with no comparator arm, improved clinical outcomes are plausible but unproven, capping this shelf at POSSIBLE
5817: LIKELY (benefit) — ticagrelor monotherapy after 3 months of DAPT reduces major bleeding without a significant ischaemic penalty, concordantly in two individual-patient meta-analyses of the randomised trials and in the high-bleeding-risk subgroup, where the absolute gain is largest
5818: LIKELY (benefit) — FFR-guided PCI improves outcomes over angiography-guided PCI in multivessel disease (fewer stents; FRAME-AMI primary endpoint 7.4% vs 19.7%, HR 0.43; FAME benefit up to 2 years, converging by 5 years at 28% vs 31%), while routine pressure-wire screening of all vessels adds nothing (RIPCORD 2, the treatment made no difference)
5819: SPLIT (at low complexity, death and the main composite: the strategies made no significant difference — 5-year death 11.2% PCI vs 10.2% CABG, HR 1.10; spontaneous MI and repeat revascularisation: CABG better — HR 2.35 and 1.78 with PCI; early stroke: PCI better — first-year HR 0.37)
5820: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (COMPASS): aspirin plus rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily reduced the primary outcome in stable coronary disease (4% vs 6%; HR 0.74) and mortality (HR 0.77), with more major bleeding (3% vs 2%; HR 1.66), mainly gastrointestinal
5821: POSSIBLE (benefit) — short DAPT (1-3 months) followed by P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy reduces bleeding after complex PCI (TWILIGHT complex: BARC 3 or 5 bleeding 1.1% vs 2.6%, HR 0.41) without a detected ischaemic penalty, on subgroup and post-hoc evidence rather than complexity-randomised trials
5822: LIKELY (benefit) — ranolazine improves angina symptoms and exercise tolerance in chronic coronary syndrome (weekly angina 3.8 vs 4.3 episodes in TERISA; pooled exercise duration +30 seconds), with no demonstrated reduction in death or myocardial infarction (HR 0.97 in the MERLIN chronic-angina subgroup)
5824: LIKELY (no benefit — the treatment made no difference) — pelacarsen lowered Lp(a) from a median 236 nmol/L to 64.4 vs 233.4 nmol/L at 12 months, but major adverse cardiovascular events in Lp(a)HORIZON were 12.3% vs 12.1% (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.90-1.15; P=0.76) over a median 4.7 years
5825: MAYBE (weak evidence) — evolocumab lowers LDL cholesterol in familial hypercholesterolemia, but no trial has tested clinical events in FH: the FH events record is four adjudicated events in the uncontrolled TAUSSIG study (N=106) and uncontrolled registry incidence (MI 0.7%, stroke 0.3% over 104 weeks), so event lowering in FH is unproven
5826: SPLIT (PROACT Mitral, the mitral-specific trial: low-dose INR 2.0-2.5 vs standard 2.5-3.5 made no difference to the composite — 11.9% vs 12.0% per patient-year — but noninferiority of the lower target was not achieved; the older intensity meta-analysis found higher intensity reduced thromboembolism and total events in mitral valves, RR 0.74 and 0.84)
5827: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (TRA 2°P-TIMI 50 PAD analyses): vorapaxar reduces limb events in peripheral arterial disease (acute limb ischaemia HR 0.58; major adverse limb events HR 0.70; peripheral revascularisation HR 0.84), with increased bleeding (7.4% vs 4.5%; HR 1.62) and no significant reduction in the cardiovascular composite in PAD (HR 0.94)
5828: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (CLEVER, aortoiliac disease only): supervised exercise worked as well as stenting for durable walking improvement at 18 months (peak walking time +5.0 vs +3.2 minutes; difference not significant) and cost less ($9,804 vs $14,590 per patient), though many quality-of-life scales favoured stenting
5829: LIKELY (benefit) — after a first unprovoked VTE, extending anticoagulation beyond 3–6 months prevents recurrence for as long as it is continued (recurrence ~0.4–1.3% on treatment vs 5.6–27.4% on placebo across three trial programmes), with major bleeding of 0.3–0.9% on treatment vs 0% on placebo; no finite extension has been shown to keep protecting after it stops
5830: SPLIT — PADIS-PE: 18 extra months of warfarin after 6 months cut the on-treatment composite (HR 0.22) but the benefit was lost by 42 months after stopping (HR 0.75); WODIT-PE: extending to 6–12 months made no difference to recurrence (rate ratio 0.81; idiopathic PE relative risk 0.99)
5831: POSSIBLE (benefit) — reduced-dose apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) prevents recurrence after 6 months of treatment in non-cancer VTE: placebo-controlled proof in AMPLIFY-EXT (primary report carded on live shelf #1580; hospitalisations HR 0.64 in its secondary analysis), with RENOVE showing low 5-year recurrence on reduced dose (2.2%) and less major or clinically relevant bleeding than full dose (9.9% vs 15.2%; HR 0.61), though formal non-inferiority was not met
5832: SPLIT — in patients who cannot be anticoagulated: the randomised trauma trial found early filters made no difference to PE or death at 90 days (13.9% vs 14.4%; HR 0.99), while a matched cancer-VTE cohort found lower PE-related mortality with filters (0.8% vs 4.0%) but higher recurrence (7.3% vs 3.2%); meta-analysis: fewer PEs (OR 0.50), more DVT (OR 1.70), no mortality change
5833: LIKELY (benefit) — after stopping anticoagulation for a first unprovoked VTE, aspirin 100 mg daily reduces recurrence versus placebo (pooled 5.1% vs 7.5% per year; HR 0.68, a 32% relative reduction) and major vascular events (HR 0.66), with major bleeding 0.5% vs 0.4% per year; ASPIRE's own primary outcome narrowly missed significance (P = 0.09)
5834: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: beta-blocker therapy is associated with substantially fewer cardiac events in congenital long QT syndrome (event rates 0.97 to 0.31/year after starting in probands; 67–71% relative reductions in high-risk LQT1/LQT2 subsets), with residual events concentrated in previously symptomatic patients; no randomised trial exists
5848: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single direct head-to-head trial: in the one randomised components trial (EQUATE), phentermine-topiramate extended-release produced greater percentage weight loss than its respective phentermine monotherapy arms (P < 0.05) and more patients reaching at least 5% weight loss; no second direct comparison exists in the records fetched
5849: LIKELY (benefit): across the carded COR phase 3 trials in adults with obesity generally, naltrexone-bupropion 32/360 mg produced consistently greater weight loss than placebo when both were combined with lifestyle intervention (−6.4% vs −1.2% at 56 weeks in COR-II; −9.3% vs −5.1% with intensive behaviour modification in COR-BMOD), with nausea the most common adverse event
5850: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: in pooled adult cohort studies and case series of frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent minimal change disease/FSGS, rituximab induced complete remission in 84.2% with 27.4% relapsing over 12–43 months; no randomised trial in adults has compared rituximab with calcineurin inhibitors, so the versus-CNI half of the question is untested in the records fetched
5851: POSSIBLE (benefit): pasireotide achieves biochemical control in a minority of patients inadequately controlled on first-generation somatostatin analogs where continued octreotide/lanreotide achieved none in the head-to-head trial cross-pointed from #745; the reports carded on this shelf (a PAOLA biomarker analysis, a single-arm switch study, and a real-world meta-analysis) are supportive but indirect, and hyperglycaemia is the price
5852: LIKELY (benefit): across a meta-analysis of the randomised cabergoline-versus-bromocriptine trials in prolactinoma and idiopathic hyperprolactinaemia, a small randomised trial in prolactinoma patients, and a 498-patient retrospective comparison, cabergoline normalizes prolactin more often, shrinks tumour more, and causes fewer adverse effects than bromocriptine
5853: POSSIBLE (benefit — equivalence in practice): in three small switch studies totalling 38 adults, oral desmopressin maintained antidiuresis and symptom control comparable with previous intranasal therapy, at an oral-to-nasal dose ratio of about 16–17 to 1; no randomised equivalence trial exists in the records fetched
5854: SPLIT (leucine alone: no benefit — the treatment made no difference to muscle strength in pooled randomised trials; leucine combined with vitamin D: possible benefit, with handgrip strength improved by a weighted mean difference of 2.17 kg in the meta-analysis subgroup)
5855: MAYBE (weak evidence): whether slower initial calorie introduction reduces complications in at-risk adults has never been tested in a randomised trial in the records fetched; the recommendation to start low rests on consensus guidance, and the comparative observational data that exist (largely eating-disorder wards) do not show more refeeding syndrome with higher-calorie starts under monitoring
5856: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single strategy trial: in the one randomised head-to-head comparison (GO TEST Overture, 308 participants), a treat-to-target strategy (serum urate under 0.36 mmol/L, ≈6.1 mg/dL) produced remission in 39.4% versus 24.0% under symptom-driven management, and pooled trial data show patients reaching target urate had fewer flares; the large US strategy trial (TRUST) has reported design only
5857: LIKELY (benefit) — steatohepatitis activity and resolution improve consistently across every placebo-controlled trial (Aithal 2008 injury P = .005; Huang 2021 improvement without worsening fibrosis 46.7% vs 11.1%) and every synthesis (Musso resolution OR 3.22; Shi 2025 ranked first, SUCRA 91.4%); the one discordant note is PIVENS' primary composite missing its prespecified threshold while its activity endpoints were strongly positive; this stamp claims activity/resolution only — fibrosis and stiffness are asked on the companion shelf #5865, and weight gain is the consistent cost
5865: SPLIT (fibrosis on biopsy: benefit in the smaller trials and in pioglitazone-only pooled analyses — Boettcher 2012 pioglitazone-only OR 1.68 (95% CI 1.02–2.77); Musso 2017 advanced fibrosis OR 3.15, any-stage OR 1.66; Luo 2022 ranks pioglitazone first for reducing biopsy fibrosis score — but no significant fibrosis benefit in the largest trial, PIVENS (improvement 44% vs 31%; P = 0.12, cross-pointed in the balance), and the thiazolidinedione-class pool was likewise not significant; liver stiffness: thin evidence — one small elastography trial in early disease positive at 48 weeks (−0.184 vs +0.554 kPa; P = 0.016), one retrospective series without a significant stiffness reduction, and no MR-elastography trial exists; steatohepatitis activity and resolution are asked on the companion shelf #5857, and weight gain is the consistent cost)
5918: SPLIT (clonazepam: better objective efficacy — it alone improved REM sleep without atonia in the 34-patient head-to-head trial; melatonin: better tolerated — sleepiness and insomnia improved on melatonin, depressive symptoms rose on clonazepam, and reviews judge melatonin the gentler drug in vulnerable patients). No trial measures falls or injuries head-to-head
5919: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme, total N = 30: trazodone 50 mg added 42.5 minutes of actigraphic night-time sleep versus placebo over 2 weeks in Alzheimer's dementia (Cochrane: low-certainty, mean difference 42.46 minutes, 95% CI 0.9 to 84.0), with no cognitive effect and no adverse-event difference detected
5920: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no trial has tested amitriptyline versus topiramate in chronic migraine patients with poor sleep: the one adult head-to-head trial (episodic migraine, N = 331) found the treatment made no difference in migraine episodes (-2.6 vs -2.7 per month), amitriptyline was more sedating (somnolence 17.8% vs 11.9%) and added weight, and for chronic migraine no includable amitriptyline trial exists
5921: POSSIBLE (benefit) — short-term surrogate outcomes only: sleep extension in habitual short sleepers is feasible (about +51 minutes to +1.2 hours per night) and reduced energy intake by 270 kcal/day in the largest trial (N = 80), with blood-pressure benefit pooled only in pre-hypertension/hypertension; no trial has tested mortality or clinical events
5922: LIKELY (harm) — in symptomatic carotid stenosis at age 70 or over, stenting is not as safe as endarterectomy: pooled 120-day stroke or death 12.0% vs 5.9% (relative risk 2.04, 95% CI 1.48 to 2.82), with no long-term catch-up (postprocedural ipsilateral stroke 0.64% vs 0.60% per year)
5923: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: in high-risk PE, thrombectomy-treated patients in FLAME had in-hospital mortality of 1.9% versus 29.5% with contemporary therapy and a 28.3% pooled background rate, but treatment was chosen, not randomised, so selection may explain the gap; no randomised trial exists
5928: POSSIBLE (benefit) — structured aerobic exercise probably reduces post-stroke fatigue: a small randomised trial of home-based cardiorespiratory interval training cut fatigue by 5.35 points versus usual care, and graded activity training added to cognitive therapy raised clinical fatigue improvement to 58% versus 24%; the wider fatigue-intervention literature remains insufficient
5929: POSSIBLE (benefit) — the standardised extract EGb 761 improves cognition modestly in Alzheimer's disease (1.4 ADAS-Cog points over placebo at 52 weeks; SKT advantage about 1.9 points; Alzheimer's-only pooled relative response ratio 1.98); the tested product is EGb 761 specifically — the fetched records do not name its manufacturer, and other ginkgo products may differ in safety and effectiveness
