5930: MAYBE (weak evidence) — computerised cognitive training improves cognitive test scores in mild cognitive impairment (g = 0.35), but an everyday-function benefit is unproven: the Cochrane review could not determine any functional effect and the one two-year trial measuring IADL, driving and mobility directly found the treatment made no difference
5931: POSSIBLE (benefit) — tai chi probably reduces falls in Parkinson's disease compared with usual activity: in the one direct trial 21.6% fell versus 48.7% on no intervention over 6 months, and meta-analyses pool a relative falls odds ratio of 0.47; the direct evidence is a single small trial in prior fallers
5932: POSSIBLE (benefit — tolerability and retention, not seizure superiority): levetiracetam was as effective as controlled-release carbamazepine for newly diagnosed focal epilepsy (seizure freedom and time to first seizure not different) with roughly half the adverse-event discontinuations (17.2% versus 32.2%; 11.3% versus 35.0%) — on direct evidence confined to patients aged 60 and over
5933: POSSIBLE (benefit) — buccal midazolam should be preferred over rectal diazepam for prolonged seizures in the community: at least as effective (75% versus 59% stopped in the one out-of-hospital trial, not significant), pooled buccal-versus-rectal relative risk 1.54 in one meta-analysis, faster and more socially acceptable to administer
5934: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only for the triptan-specific claim: stop the overused triptan and start preventive therapy together — triptan overusers improved most after a drug-free period (p < 0.0001), and reviews find preventive-plus-discontinuation beats discontinuation alone; no randomised trial restricted to triptan overusers exists
5935: SPLIT (a small positive trial and positive subgroup reviews versus a 2023 meta-analysis finding insufficient randomised evidence in medication overuse) — topiramate cut headache days to 8.1 versus 20.6 per 28 days in one small trial in analgesic overuse, but its isolated effect in medication-overuse headache, especially after withdrawal, is not established
5936: LIKELY (benefit) — rimegepant is effective for both acute treatment and prevention of migraine: three concordant placebo-controlled prevention trials of 75 mg every other day found 0.8 to 1.6 fewer monthly migraine days than placebo, and its acute efficacy is homed on live shelf #689
5937: POSSIBLE (benefit) — ubrogepant probably works for acute migraine in patients who do not respond to triptans: its efficacy did not differ by historical triptan response in the ACHIEVE trials and functional outcomes favoured it within the insufficient-responder subgroup (normal function 38% versus 29% at 2 hours), but all the evidence is post-hoc subgroup analysis, with no prospective non-responder trial
5939: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (ELEVATE): atogepant 60 mg daily reduced monthly migraine days by 2.4 days more than placebo over 12 weeks (95% CI −3.2 to −1.5) in episodic migraine patients who had failed two to four classes of conventional oral preventives
5940: POSSIBLE — carbamazepine remains the most effective first treatment for trigeminal neuralgia on current evidence: it is the AAN–EFNS guideline's only Level A drug and no alternative has beaten it in adequate head-to-head trials, but the comparative trial base is old, small and poor quality
5941: POSSIBLE (harm) — continuing long-term opioids for chronic neuropathic pain when function does not improve: trials of ≤12 weeks show modest pain relief with no improvement in functioning, and tapering studies show pain is usually unchanged after dose reduction, so continuation without functional gain carries harm without demonstrated benefit (tapering should be voluntary and monitored)
5942: LIKELY (benefit) — continuing antidepressants for at least 12 months after a second (recurrent) depressive episode prevents relapse: PREVENT recurrence 23.1% versus 42.0% at 12 months and 28.5% versus 47.3% at 24 months, with the imipramine programme showing protection at 3–5 years
5943: POSSIBLE (benefit) — regular repositioning on a pressure-redistributing mattress prevents grade II-or-worse pressure injuries in immobile older adults: 3.0% versus 14.3–24.1% against other regimens including standard care in one 838-patient nursing-home trial; Cochrane reviews leave the best frequency and surface uncertain
5944: SPLIT (older meta-analysis: benefit; 2024 Cochrane review: little to no difference) — protein-and-energy supplementation to prevent pressure injuries: odds ratio 0.75 (95% CI 0.62 to 0.89) in Stratton 2005 versus relative risk 0.92 (95% CI 0.71 to 1.19) in the larger Cochrane 2024 pooling; prevention is unproven on current evidence
5945: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (ESCAPE-TRD): esketamine nasal spray beat quetiapine XR augmentation on remission at week 8 (27.1% versus 17.6%) and on relapse-free remission through week 32 (21.7% versus 14.1%) in treatment-resistant depression, in one open-label, rater-blinded trial
5946: SPLIT (nonpsychotic, less severe depression: rTMS as effective as ECT on small-trial evidence; severe or psychotic-spectrum depression: ECT superior) — response 12/20 versus 11/20 in the nonpsychotic-restricted trial, versus remission 59.1% versus 16.7% for ECT in severe ECT-referred patients; meta-analysis relative risk 1.41 for response favouring ECT overall, with equivalence in its nonpsychotic subgroup
5947: LIKELY (benefit, for bipolar depression prevention rather than mania) — lamotrigine maintenance delayed intervention for depressive episodes (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.90) with no effect on manic episodes (hazard ratio 0.91) and higher manic recurrence than lithium (relative risk 2.13); enriched trial designs, as on home shelf #1436
5948: SPLIT — one direct meta-analysis gives EMDR a modest immediate edge for PTSD symptoms (standardised mean difference −0.43), the Cochrane adult review and a second meta-analysis find no difference, and the one three-way trial favours exposure therapy on avoidance and re-experiencing; at follow-up no analysis separates trauma-focused CBT and EMDR
5949: SPLIT — in the randomised double-blind trials buprenorphine did not reduce illicit opioid use better than methadone (the treatment made no difference); completer analyses of a small open trial and one non-randomised comparison tilt toward buprenorphine
5950: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference to bone density) — cinacalcet normalised calcium but bone mineral density was unchanged versus placebo at 1 year and unchanged over 5.5 years; no carded record reports a fracture benefit
5951: LIKELY (no benefit) — calcium plus vitamin D did not prevent hip fractures in community-dwelling older adults: pooled relative risk 1.09 (95% CI 0.85 to 1.39), with concordant null results in the RECORD and Women's Health Initiative trials (the treatment made no difference)
5952: SPLIT — daily vitamin D (800–1,000 IU) reduced fall rates in two nursing-home trials (rate ratios 0.28 and 0.73), but a quarterly-bolus regimen in the largest trial (3,717 residents) made no difference to falls (44% vs 43%)
5953: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only: long-term proton pump inhibitor use is associated with a modestly higher fracture risk (relative risks about 1.3, rising to odds ratio 1.62 with long use), with absolute hip-fracture risk 2.02 vs 1.51 per 1,000 person-years in the largest cohort; no carded randomised evidence confirms the association
5954: MAYBE (weak evidence) — longer relief than pregabalin in postherpetic neuralgia is unproven: no PHN head-to-head trial exists in the carded records; the one head-to-head trial (mixed peripheral neuropathic pain, 8 weeks) found non-inferior relief with faster onset for the patch (55.7% vs 54.5% achieving ≥30% relief), and duration beyond 8 weeks was never compared
5955: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only: opioid use for osteoarthritis in older adults is associated with substantially more falls and fractures than NSAID use (fracture hazard ratio 4.47 in one matched cohort; fall/fracture odds ratios 3.3–4.1 in another; hip-fracture hazard ratio 1.4–1.6 for tramadol, about 2 extra hip fractures per 1,000 person-years)
5956: SPLIT — meta-analyses of the small trials find low-dose naltrexone reduces fibromyalgia pain (mean difference −0.86), but the largest double-blind trial (6 mg, 99 women) found no difference from placebo (−0.34 points, P = 0.27); all carded trials enrolled women only
5957: POSSIBLE — cryotherapy is not more effective than salicylic acid for plantar warts: complete clearance 13.6% vs 14.3% at 12 weeks in the dedicated trial (the treatment made no difference), and 11% vs 20% as second-line treatment; absolute clearance is low on both
5859: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only for treatment of established hypercalcemia: denosumab lowered calcium similarly to intravenous bisphosphonate in the one direct treatment cohort (−2.0 vs. −1.8 mg/dL, with less hypocalcemia) and prevented hypercalcemia better than zoledronic acid in pooled randomised trials (first HCM 1.7% vs. 2.7%), but no randomised head-to-head treatment trial exists
5860: SPLIT (lifestyle: strong benefit over 60; metformin: effect faded with age) — in the DPP age analysis, incidence at age 60–85 was 3.3 cases per 100 person-years on lifestyle intervention versus 9.3 on metformin, and metformin risk rose with age (hazard ratio 1.63, oldest vs. youngest); metformin was safe long-term, so the preference for lifestyle over 60 is about efficacy, not tolerability
5861: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm evidence only, total N = 10 with POMC deficiency: 80% of the pivotal POMC cohort achieved at least 10% weight loss at 1 year on setmelanotide against a natural history of continuous gain, but no placebo-controlled trial exists, so no placebo-adjusted effect can be stated
5862: LIKELY (benefit) — six months of ursodiol after bariatric surgery prevents gallstone formation versus placebo: 32% vs. 2% at 6 months (600 mg/day, gastric bypass) and 22% vs. 3% at 12 months (500 mg/day, restrictive procedures), with a pooled formation odds ratio of 0.25 across 11 randomised trials
5863: SPLIT (enriched protein supplements during a weight-loss programme: benefit; higher-protein diet alone: no significant difference) — whey/leucine/vitamin D supplements preserved appendicular muscle mass (+0.95 kg and +0.36 kg between-group) in two trials with exercise in both arms, but the factorial trial of a high-protein diet alone found no significant fat-free-mass effect; no trial required a formal sarcopenic-obesity diagnosis
5864: POSSIBLE (benefit) — G-POEM clinical success was numerically higher than botulinum toxin injection in the only double-blind randomised head-to-head (65% vs. 40% at 3 months, P = 0.10, not significant; 60% vs. 40% at 1 year), but the trial had 40 patients of mixed etiology (11 diabetic, with no diabetic-subgroup results reported), so superiority in diabetic gastroparesis is plausible, not demonstrated
5866: SPLIT (lifestyle modestly ahead overall; metformin essentially as effective in younger, more obese cohorts) — pooled head-to-head data favour lifestyle (relative risk 0.747 for diabetes incidence), but in the younger IDPP cohort lifestyle and metformin were near-identical (3-year incidence 39.3% vs. 40.5%) and the DPP found metformin's effect greatest in the more obese
5867: SPLIT (off-medication efficacy shown in non-resistant hypertension; resistant-hypertension effect smaller and unproven off medication) — denervation beat sham off medication by −5.0 and −6.3 mm Hg in two trials of non-resistant hypertension, but pooled resistant-hypertension trials (all on medication) show a non-significant −1.86 mm Hg ambulatory effect, and no trial has studied resistant patients off medication
5868: LIKELY (benefit): blood-pressure lowering after renal denervation is maintained at 3 years — adjusted 36-month differences versus sham of −10.0 mm Hg ambulatory systolic (SPYRAL HTN-ON MED) and −16.5 mm Hg ambulatory / −22.1 mm Hg office (SYMPLICITY HTN-3), with sustained reductions in open-label and registry cohorts and no late safety signal reported
5869: MAYBE (weak evidence): no head-to-head trial of linagliptin versus a dose-adjusted DPP-4 inhibitor in stage 4 CKD was found — linagliptin (HbA1c −0.72 points vs placebo at 1 year in severe impairment), dose-adjusted vildagliptin (−0.7 points vs placebo) and dose-adjusted sitagliptin (noninferior to glipizide, less hypoglycaemia) are each proven only in parallel, so the comparison is indirect only
5870: MAYBE (weak evidence): no mortality benefit shown versus placebo in non-dialysis CKD — relative risk of death 0.45 (95% CI 0.13 to 1.53) for sevelamer and 0.33 (0.10 to 1.05) for lanthanum, low-certainty with intervals crossing no effect, no cardiovascular deaths reported, and mechanistic trials showing no FGF23 or vascular benefit
5872: MAYBE (weak evidence) — observational only: allopurinol has never been tested against placebo in uric acid stones in the records fetched; bundled with potassium citrate it was associated with smaller recurrences and fewer operations but the same recurrence rate (32%), so its benefit for uric acid stones is unproven
5874: POSSIBLE (harm) — observational only for hyponatraemia and fractures: tramadol should generally be avoided in older adults with neuropathic pain — modest short-term relief (53% vs 30% achieving 50% relief) against adverse events in 58%, early hyponatraemia (adjusted OR 2.34 for hospitalisation in the first 90 days; rate ratio 1.57 for early laboratory hyponatraemia) and more fractures versus codeine (HR 1.50), though recorded falls did not differ significantly
5875: MAYBE (weak evidence): increasing citrate intake raises urinary citrate (lemonade +383 mg/day in hypocitraturic stone formers; fruit juices pooled +167.2 mg/day), but stone prevention is unproven — the only long-term stone-rate fall (1.00 to 0.13 per patient-year) was not statistically significant and no randomised trial has tested intake against stone recurrence
5876: POSSIBLE (benefit): a late-evening snack improves nitrogen balance and nutritional status in cirrhosis — nighttime supplementation raised total body protein by 0.53 kg over 12 months where daytime feeding did not, and pooled trials show higher albumin and improved energy metabolism — but no survival or complication benefit is reported in the carded records
5877: MAYBE (weak evidence): a bedtime alginate add-on may help PPI non-responders with night-time symptoms by extrapolation — add-on alginate doubled complete heartburn resolution versus PPI alone in nonerosive reflux (56.7% vs 25.7%) — but no free record tests the bedtime dose or night-time symptoms specifically, and the homed bedtime trial's confirmatory study was null
5878: MAYBE (weak evidence) — observational only: no trial compares surveillance intervals in non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus; a prospective cohort found no evidence that longer-than-recommended intervals worsen cancer curability or cause-specific mortality, and programme data put detection at about 1 high-grade dysplasia/T1 cancer per 77.6 endoscopy-years
5879: SPLIT (observational studies associate aspirin/PPI use with less Barrett's cancer — adjusted incidence density ratio 0.64 for aspirin/NSAIDs on a near-universal PPI background; the bias-adjusted 2025 review finds aspirin nonsignificant, adjusted OR 0.84, and the single randomised trial no significant cancer-specific association) — unproven for cancer alone
5880: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no head-to-head trial in adults: indirect meta-regression puts histologic response in the same range for swallowed steroids (68.3–76.8%) and six-food elimination diet (69.0%), and a cost-utility model found them about as effective, so neither can be called better
5881: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme, subgroup evidence: dupilumab improved histologic, symptomatic and endoscopic outcomes irrespective of prior swallowed-steroid failure or intolerance in LIBERTY EoE TREET subgroup analyses, with histologic remission 60.9% vs 0.0% in the paediatric steroid-refractory subgroup
5882: POSSIBLE (benefit) — vonoprazan heals severe (LA C/D) erosive esophagitis better than lansoprazole (week 8 relative risk 1.175, 4 trials) and potassium-competitive acid blockers suppress night-time acid more than PPIs in healthy-volunteer pH studies, but no trial has tested the class in severe esophagitis patients with nighttime breakthrough
5883: LIKELY (benefit) — adding bismuth in salvage after first-line failure raised eradication to 98.0% vs 69.2% in the direct randomised trial (absolute difference 28.8 points) and bismuth quadruple regimens of 10–14 days ranked among the most effective across two network meta-analyses
5885: LIKELY (benefit) — two concordant phase 3 placebo-controlled trials: risankizumab 600 mg induced CDAI remission in 45% vs 25% (ADVANCE) and 42% vs 20% (MOTIVATE) at week 12, with endoscopic response roughly triple the placebo rate
5887: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single pivotal trial: continuing weekly intramuscular methotrexate after methotrexate-induced remission kept 65% vs 39% in remission at 40 weeks (absolute relapse-risk reduction 26.1 points); oral methotrexate maintenance is unproven
5888: POSSIBLE (benefit) — the named tested preparations (Escherichia coli Nissle 1917; Lactobacillus GG) maintained ulcerative colitis remission as well as mesalazine in randomised trials (12-month per-protocol relapse 36.4% vs 33.9%, equivalence P = 0.003), but no carded trial shows a probiotic beating placebo: the one small placebo-controlled trial (N = 32) made no significant difference
5889: MAYBE (weak evidence) — observational only: no trial has randomised the length of the strict low FODMAP phase; in the reported services restriction ran weeks to 2 months before reintroduction, and completing reintroduction (not prolonged restriction) was associated with long-term improvement, so the strict phase should be treated as a short diagnostic phase followed by structured reintroduction
5890: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (TARGET 3): in IBS-D patients who responded to a first rifaximin course and then relapsed, repeat rifaximin produced responders in 38.1% vs 31.5% on placebo (P = .03), with no difference on stool consistency; no randomised evidence covers patients who never responded to a first course
5891: MAYBE (weak evidence) — indirect evidence only: no trial has enrolled IBS patients defined by non-response to diet changes; in the neighbouring refractory/referred populations hypnotherapy beat supportive control (adequate relief OR 2.9 in IMAGINE; 54.3% vs 25.0% improved over 15 months in refractory patients), but a network meta-analysis found no significant hypnotherapy effect in refractory-only trials
5893: SPLIT (comparator split: benefit versus a low-fat/high-carbohydrate control in one small crossover — relative steatosis reduction 39% vs 7% — and versus usual care on liver stiffness; but no advantage over a low-fat diet in the two larger head-to-head trials, where the Mediterranean diet made no difference between groups)
5894: LIKELY (benefit) — four concordant randomised trials and a 9-trial meta-analysis: lactulose reversed covert (minimal) hepatic encephalopathy in 47.5–69.1% versus 10–22.6% untreated, halved the relative risk of no improvement (relative risk 0.52) and reduced progression to overt encephalopathy (relative risk 0.17), with more diarrhoea and no mortality difference; grade 1 covert disease was not trialled separately
5895: POSSIBLE (benefit) — pooled individual-patient data from the four placebo-controlled trials (589 patients) show beta-blockers prevent first bleeding (78% vs 65% free of bleeding at 2 years, P = 0.002) and fatal bleeding, with no significant overall-survival difference; but the trials enrolled large varices and split individually, and no trial has isolated medium varices
5896: POSSIBLE (benefit) — trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prevented spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in one small randomised trial (3% vs 27% on no prophylaxis, P = 0.025) and showed no detected difference from norfloxacin in two head-to-head trials, though with more definite/probable adverse events (22.5% vs 0%); the Cochrane network meta-analysis rates the whole prophylaxis evidence base low to very low certainty
5897: SPLIT (baclofen: the homed cirrhosis trial and a pooled cirrhosis review favour it — relative risk of alcohol consumption 0.68 — but the largest free randomised trial was null, P = 0.95, and the baclofen-specific pooled randomised comparison was non-significant, relative risk 1.42, 95% CI 0.41–4.92; acamprosate: no abstinence or mortality benefit demonstrated in advanced liver disease, with higher readmission in confounded real-world data)
5898: POSSIBLE (benefit) — adding alpha-fetoprotein to 6-monthly ultrasound raises early-stage HCC sensitivity in cirrhosis from about 45-52% to 63-74% (combination sensitivity 96% vs 76% for ultrasound alone in direct comparisons), at the cost of lower specificity and more false positives; diagnostic-accuracy evidence only, with no randomised mortality trial of the combined strategy (partial completion of live shelf #3387)
5899: SPLIT (small trials: benefit; larger controlled trials: the treatment made no difference) — a 32-patient pilot and a 54-patient frailty trial report muscle gains with BCAA, but a 60-patient placebo-controlled trial and the largest trial (150 patients vs whey protein) found no muscle-mass advantage; partial completion of live shelf #5367
5900: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: after removal of 3-4 small (under 10 mm) adenomas, advanced neoplasia is uncommon (2.1% at 3 years; 5.07% at first follow-up when all adenomas are small), supporting a longer-than-3-year interval on the low-risk timetable rather than routine 3-year recall, with a 6-9 mm adenoma in the set arguing for the shorter end (partial completion of pack #5549)
5901: POSSIBLE (benefit) — in selected adults with uncomplicated diverticulitis, outpatient management is as safe as hospitalisation (single randomised trial, 132 patients: failures 3 vs 4; pooled readmission 7%, emergency surgery 0.2%) and substantially cheaper; the randomised base is one small trial, and the evidence applies only to selected patients (partial completion of live shelf #3621)
5902: POSSIBLE (benefit) — botulinum toxin heals most topical-refractory chronic fissures (89-96% by 2 months with retreatment) and avoids permanent sphincter injury, but in patients who had failed conservative treatment it healed significantly fewer fissures than sphincterotomy and recurred significantly more; a continence-sparing step, not the most durable cure (partial completion of live shelf #2472)
5903: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single trial programme (post hoc/review evidence): dupilumab reduces exacerbations in severe eosinophilic asthma, with demonstrated benefit at blood eosinophil counts of 300/µL or above (and at 150-300/µL for the 300 mg dose), relative reductions of 48-72% in severe-asthma strata; one comparative cohort favours anti-IL-5 biologics over dupilumab at counts of 300/µL or above (partial completion of live shelf #1031)
5904: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FeNO-guided adjustment in adults reduces exacerbations (pooled odds ratio 0.60-0.61; rate ratio 0.59-0.67) but has no demonstrated effect on severe exacerbations, symptoms, lung function or steroid dose, and the Cochrane authors state universal use cannot be advocated; most plausible value is in adults with frequent exacerbations (partial completion of live shelf #1728)
5905: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: bronchial thermoplasty improved control and exacerbations in refractory severe-asthma cohorts in which biologic exposure was common (43% in the largest registry), but no study has enrolled or separately reported patients after biologic failure — effectiveness in that exact population is untested (partial completion of live shelf #1036)
5906: MAYBE (weak evidence) — the 5-vs-14-day question has never been trialled in home-treated COPD exacerbations: the only home trial of a 5-day course found no benefit over placebo (failure 42.0% vs 34.5%), a 10-day course after emergency discharge did reduce relapse (27% vs 43%), and the one home duration trial in progress compares 3 vs 5 days; the 5-day answer is extrapolated from hospitalised patients (partial completion of live shelf #3926)
5907: SPLIT (targeted high-intensity ventilation in marked hypercapnia: benefit — 1-year mortality 12% vs 33%, hazard ratio 0.24; unselected stable-patient trials: the treatment made no difference — pooled relative risk 0.88) — survival benefit in stable hypercapnic COPD depends on baseline PaCO2 (55 mmHg or above) and achieving a large PaCO2 reduction (partial completion of live shelf #1645)
5909: MAYBE (weak evidence) — antifibrotic survival benefit in non-IPF progressive fibrosis rests on a Bayesian modelled estimate (median 6.34–6.50 vs 3.42–3.76 years), a subgroup mortality HR of 0.54 (95% CI 0.14–2.11), and 1 vs 5 deaths in a stopped-early trial; no powered observed mortality result exists
5910: POSSIBLE (benefit) — home treatment of selected low-risk PE with a DOAC: no PE-related deaths across 8 studies in the DOAC-specific review, but that review could not pool its heterogeneous studies and states no robust conclusions can be drawn
5913: SPLIT — objective sleep latency improves in older adults (28.7–30.8 vs 38.4 min polysomnographic; 70.2 vs 78.5 min patient-reported at week 1), but a meta-analysis subgroup found subjective latency reduced only at ages 18–64, not over 65
5914: POSSIBLE (benefit) — low dependence potential: Drug Liking matched placebo at therapeutic and 6× doses in the dedicated abuse-potential study (N = 38 completers), with no dependence signal in 1-year and 42.6-month follow-up — but dependence was a measured endpoint only in that one small volunteer study
5915: SPLIT — AHI: CPAP better (pooled −25.4 vs −9.3 events/hour; +4.1 events/hour advantage at 1 year in mild/moderate OSA); sleepiness: equal (ESS −1.6 on both) — with adherence and tolerability favouring the MAD
5916: POSSIBLE (benefit) — timed light shifts circadian phase in the intended direction (DLMO delays of about 4 hours with a compromise-phase protocol; +2.3 h advance / −4.1 h delay with daytime light control), but complete adaptation was not consistently achieved and all evidence is from small laboratory simulations (total N = 116)
5917: POSSIBLE (benefit) — timing over dose: 0.5 mg and 3.0 mg melatonin yield similarly sized phase shifts when each is given at its optimal time relative to DLMO, while mistimed dosing shifts less or the wrong way; the dose comparison is from healthy volunteers, not DSWPD patients (printed on the face)
5958: POSSIBLE (benefit) — an early corticosteroid injection speeds range-of-motion and pain recovery in frozen shoulder over the first weeks to months (placebo-controlled and pooled evidence), but by 12 months outcomes converge with no injection
5959: MAYBE (weak evidence) — early vasopressor use has not been shown to prevent dialysis: a cohort-heavy meta-analysis reports less renal replacement therapy use without printing an effect size, while the trial-inclusive meta-analysis found no difference in dialysis-free days
5960: SPLIT (observational only — by subgroup definition: broadly defined normal-ALT cohorts show excess liver cancer when untreated, hazard ratio 2.54 relative, while stringently defined immune-tolerant cohorts show negligible risk with zero events; no trial shows treating normal-enzyme patients prevents liver cancer or death)
5961: POSSIBLE (benefit) — unproven for mortality in all-comer community-acquired pneumonia: pooled mortality differences were not significant (5.0% vs 5.9%; adjusted odds ratio 0.75, 0.46–1.21); the consistent gain is about one day faster stability and discharge, with more hyperglycaemia and readmission
5962: POSSIBLE (benefit) — trial efficacy was 92.1% relative against lower respiratory tract disease in the combined cardiorespiratory subgroup and real-world effectiveness against RSV hospitalisation was 58% relative over two seasons, but no carded record reports a chronic-lung-disease-specific hospitalisation estimate (hospitalisation evidence observational)
5963: POSSIBLE (benefit) — real-world effectiveness was similar at 75+ and 60–74 (75.1% relative overall against RSV illness), but no randomised trial record reports an over-75-only efficacy estimate; trial efficacy (81.38% relative pooled, first season) is proven for the pooled 60+ population
5966: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only for hospitalisation: pneumonia hospitalisation after polysaccharide vaccination was lower in diabetic patients (unadjusted odds ratio 0.63 relative), and the conjugate vaccine's vaccine-type efficacy was 89.5% relative in the trial's diabetes subgroup, but no trial has tested hospitalisation in diabetes directly
5967: LIKELY (benefit) — direct-acting antivirals cure hepatitis C in compensated cirrhosis nearly as well as without cirrhosis (97.9% vs 98.9% overall in 5,552 real-world patients), with cure lower in treatment-experienced patients (88.9% on 12 weeks) and genotype 1a with resistance substitutions (73%)
5968: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no randomised trial has tested procalcitonin guidance in febrile infants under 3 months; the two trials enrolling from the first weeks of life found revealing the result made no difference to antibiotic prescribing, and procalcitonin alone discriminates serious bacterial infection in infants under 91 days less well than clinical prediction rules
5969: POSSIBLE (benefit) — network meta-analyses rank benzoyl peroxide plus a retinoid above topical antibiotic monotherapy for moderate acne (clearest for noninflammatory lesions), but the comparison is indirect, confidence was rated low, and no direct head-to-head trial was found in the records fetched
5970: LIKELY (harm) — a higher haemoglobin target with ESAs increases stroke: 5.0% versus 2.6% with darbepoetin in TREAT (hazard ratio 1.9) and relative risk 1.51–1.74 for higher versus lower targets across the target-trial meta-analyses
5971: POSSIBLE (benefit) — intravenous iron improved fatigue in pooled non-anaemic iron-deficiency evidence and in the ferritin ≤15 ng/mL subgroup of the one dedicated trial (82% versus 47% improved), but the trial's overall comparison was null (P = 0.07) and the syntheses rate the evidence low quality
5973: LIKELY (benefit) — in patients whose oral iron had failed or could not be used, intravenous ferumoxytol produced a ≥2.0 g/dL haemoglobin rise in 81.1% versus 5.5% on placebo, and head-to-head evidence shows intravenous iron at least as effective as oral iron with far fewer intolerance discontinuations (0.9% versus 8.0% in PROFOUND; odds ratio 0.27 in the IBD meta-analysis)
5975: LIKELY (benefit) — ESAs reduce transfusion needs in CKD anaemia: odds ratios 0.19–0.28 versus placebo for epoetin alfa, epoetin beta and darbepoetin alfa in the 2023 Cochrane network meta-analysis (117 studies, 25,237 participants), with relative risk 0.32 for requiring transfusion in pre-dialysis patients; no survival benefit accompanies the effect
5977: POSSIBLE (benefit) — preoperative intravenous iron reduced transfusion in the large cardiac-surgery trial ITACS (61.1% versus 68.2%; relative risk 0.90) and across major-surgery trials pooled (relative risk 0.84), but the hip-fracture trial was null and the abdominal-surgery trial on home shelf #1126 was null, so the benefit is modest and setting-dependent
5978: LIKELY (benefit) — in lower-risk MDS, ESAs reduce transfusion needs: darbepoetin alfa transfusion incidence 36.1% versus 59.2% on placebo and epoetin alfa erythroid response 31.8% versus 4.4%, in two phase 3 placebo-controlled trials
5979: POSSIBLE (benefit) — scalp cooling reduces alopecia across chemotherapy regimens (randomised meta-analysis RR 0.57 for substantial alopecia; 50-56% of 7,424 registry patients needed no head cover), but randomised evidence remains breast-cancer-dominated and some regimens (TAC) largely defeat cooling
5980: LIKELY (benefit) — exercise during adjuvant chemotherapy reduces fatigue in breast cancer: significant physical-fatigue benefit in the PACES randomised trial and a pooled SMD of -0.38 during chemotherapy across randomised trials, strongest for supervised combined resistance-plus-aerobic training
5981: SPLIT (randomised: no benefit; observational: apparent benefit) — pooled randomised data including the 80-plus trial show levothyroxine made no difference to cardiovascular events (HR 0.74, interval crossing 1), while a large observational emulated trial reports lower cardiovascular risk on treatment (adjusted HR 0.82) in a younger (median 66) population
5982: POSSIBLE (no survival advantage shown for dialysis in frail older adults) — observational only: in geriatric-assessment and performance-status strata, dialysis showed no survival benefit over conservative management over age 80 or at poor performance status, with about twice the hospitalisation
5983: MAYBE (weak evidence) — diabetes-specific deprescribing has not been shown in a completed trial to reduce adverse drug events: the review evidence is very low certainty (adverse events fell in 2 of 4 controlled studies), and the dedicated OMED2 randomised trial has published a protocol only
5984: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no trial defines a safe-use duration: efficacy is established only for short-term use (at most 4 weeks in the European guideline), long-term efficacy is unproven with tolerance/dependence risk, and harm data are observational only
5985: MAYBE (weak evidence) — regular acetaminophen alone is unproven for agitation: both direct placebo-controlled trials found no difference on agitation/neuropsychiatric outcomes (the treatment made no difference), though a paracetamol subgroup did show reduced pain scores
5986: SPLIT (randomised: stopping non-inferior on mortality; observational: stopping associated with more cardiovascular admissions) — in SAGA/SITE (75 and over, median 80, no cardiovascular disease) 3-year mortality was 7.2% stopping versus 7.9% continuing, while the French nationwide cohort found discontinuation associated with cardiovascular admission (adjusted HR 1.33)
5987: POSSIBLE (harm) — regular high-dose vitamin D did not reduce falls versus 200 IU/day in STURDY (HR 0.94) or versus placebo in VITAL (OR 0.97), and STURDY found significantly more serious falls (HR 1.87) and fracture falls (HR 2.66) at doses of 1,000 IU/day or more; harm rests on a single trial programme
5988: SPLIT (function improves, falls unproven in frail-specific trials) — multicomponent programmes improved strength, balance and mobility in frail community-dwellers, and a review of smaller trials leans toward fewer falls, but LIFE (serious fall injuries, hazard ratio 0.90, not significant) and Fairhall 2014 (fall rate ratio 1.12, not significant) found no fall reduction (the treatment made no difference to falls in either trial). Partial completion of live #459
5991: POSSIBLE (benefit) — prompted voiding/scheduled toileting reduced incontinent episodes in the short term across five small trials (Cochrane, 355 people) and in one six-month staff-delivered randomised trial (N = 52); long-term effects unstudied. Partial completion of live #2869 (which covers prompted voiding only combined with exercise)
5993: MAYBE (weak evidence) — a single double-blind trial of 20 women found cycle-timed magnesium pyrrolidone carboxylic acid 360 mg/day reduced headache days in menstrual migraine; supporting evidence is observational (ionised magnesium deficiency in 45% of menstrual attacks) or from premenstrual-symptom trials of named preparations. Partial completion of live #2442 (general migraine prevention)
5994: LIKELY (benefit) — low-dose vaginal estrogen relieves vaginal dryness (44-study review; randomised trial N = 230, P < .001 versus placebo), systemic estradiol stays within or near the postmenopausal range at 4–10 mcg doses, and endometrial hyperplasia/cancer were extremely rare; long-term randomised safety outcomes are absent. Partial completion of live #2736 (breast-cancer survivors)
5996: LIKELY (as good as hysterectomy for long-term quality of life) — quality of life was indistinguishable at 5 and 10 years in the EMMY randomised trial and comparable across four trials, with the trade-off printed here: 28.4% of embolization patients had a hysterectomy by 5 years and 35% by 10 years. Partial completion of live #830 (UAE versus myomectomy)
5999: SPLIT (population) — vaginal progesterone reduced preterm birth before 34 weeks in pooled high-risk singleton pregnancies (EPPPIC relative risk 0.78), but the largest broad-population trial (OPPTIMUM) made no difference on its primary outcomes and neither EPPPIC nor PREDICT found any benefit in twin pregnancies
6000: LIKELY — primary HPV testing every 5 years is at least as effective as Pap testing every 3 years: pooled randomised evidence shows fewer invasive cancers with HPV-based screening (rate ratio 0.60, relative), 5-year HPV sensitivity matching 3-year cytology sensitivity, and a lower 5.5-year cancer risk after a negative HPV test (8.7 per 100,000) than after a negative Pap (36.0 per 100,000)
6001: POSSIBLE (benefit) — the levonorgestrel IUD reduced measured blood loss more than oral tranexamic acid at 6 months in the one small direct head-to-head trial (85.8% vs 60.8% reduction; 62 women evaluated), with a large pragmatic trial concordant against usual medical treatment as a bundle but not against tranexamic acid alone
6003: POSSIBLE — observational only: narrow-spectrum aminopenicillin treatment (amoxicillin in outpatients, ampicillin/penicillin in hospital) was as effective as broader-spectrum antibiotics across three large cohorts (same stay, intensive-care and readmission rates in hospital; no fewer hospitalisations with broad-spectrum treatment in outpatients); no randomised trial compares spectrum
6004: SPLIT (setting) — parent-initiated oral prednisolone at home made no difference to symptoms or admissions in the dedicated randomised trial and the Cochrane review of home courses found no benefit, while a clinician-started 3-day course in the emergency department shortened hospital stay (median 370 vs 540 minutes)
6005: POSSIBLE (benefit) — strain-specific: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BB-12 (two randomised trials, 272 infants) and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG ATCC 53103 (one small trial plus a four-trial meta-analysis) each reduced crying versus placebo; the records name strains and doses but no manufacturer or branded product, and no class-wide probiotic claim is supported
6006: LIKELY (benefit) — biologic therapies clear skin substantially more than methotrexate: in the direct CHAMPION trial PASI 75 was 79.6% on adalimumab versus 35.5% on methotrexate at 16 weeks, and the Cochrane network meta-analysis ranks the biologic classes far above methotrexate and the other conventional systemics for PASI 90
6007: LIKELY (benefit) — apremilast beat placebo in three randomised trials (PASI 75 at week 16: 33.1% vs 5.3%, 28.8% vs 5.8%, and 39.8% vs 11.9% in biologic-naive patients), with responses maintained to 52 weeks; no trial enrolled only biologic-ineligible patients, so that use rests on this moderate-to-severe psoriasis evidence
6008: POSSIBLE — oral finasteride 1 mg beat topical minoxidil in all three head-to-head trials (improvement 80% vs 52% and 80.5% vs 59%), but every comparison is open-label with largely subjective endpoints
6009: LIKELY — topical minoxidil improved hair density versus placebo in two large double-blind trials in women (381 and 280 participants) and in the Cochrane pooling (regrowth relative risk 1.93; +13.18 hairs/cm²), with modest absolute gains
6010: SPLIT — observational evidence disagrees by study design (protective in hospital case-control studies and a high-SPF cohort comparison; null in population case-control pooling; positive association in other cohorts), so a melanoma-preventive effect in average-risk adults is unproven outside the single randomised trial homed on #221
6011: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference) — three head-to-head randomised trials: ketoconazole shampoo was not more effective than selenium sulfide/disulfide shampoo (one day-8 advantage in 1993 that did not persist; no significant between-group difference in the 2024 and 2026 double-blind trials)
6012: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no randomised trials; nonrandomised programme analyses suggested no melanoma mortality benefit from total body/visual skin examination screening in average-risk adults, and the only positive signal is a surrogate (fewer thick melanomas, OR 0.86) alongside more thin melanomas (OR 1.38)
6013: POSSIBLE — antihistamine eye drops relieved ocular itching better than an oral antihistamine alone in three small direct comparisons (challenge trial, adjunctive trial, and an 8-week seasonal trial), with no advantage for nasal symptoms
6014: LIKELY — intranasal corticosteroids beat oral antihistamines on nasal blockage, discharge, sneezing, itch and total nasal symptoms in a 16-trial meta-analysis and the largest head-to-head trial, with no difference for eye symptoms
6015: SPLIT — quality of life: hearing aids consistently improved hearing-specific quality of life in trials and reviews (HHIE −26.47 points pooled); cognition: benefit shown only in observational data (HR 0.81) and one small trial subscale, with the large randomised cognition trial homed on #350 null on its primary outcome
6016: SPLIT — pooled/meta-analytic mortality benefit for ablation in AF with HFrEF (relative risk 0.52) driven primarily by the CASTLE-AF trial homed on #271, with AATAC positive on a secondary endpoint but RAFT-AF (HR 0.71, P = 0.066) and AMICA null
6017: POSSIBLE — catheter ablation has not been shown to reduce mortality in ischaemic ventricular tachycardia: every randomised comparison is null for death (the treatment made no difference), though all were powered for arrhythmia outcomes rather than survival
6018: POSSIBLE (benefit) — pelvic-floor-based exercise programmes improve incontinence in community-dwelling older women in randomised trials, but effects are modest and one trial found a self-help booklet nearly as effective
6020: POSSIBLE — the evidence supports opening the PSA discussion at about age 50 (with a baseline PSA in the late 40s usable for risk stratification); the demonstrated mortality benefit is concentrated at ages 55–69, and the age-60 PSA level should steer whether screening continues
6023: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — on mortality in general critical illness: two randomised trials and the Cochrane pooling (long-term mortality relative risk 1.00) agree that glutamine supplementation does not reduce deaths
6024: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational evidence only: in three adult cohorts the six-food elimination diet induced histologic remission in roughly 54–70% of adults with eosinophilic oesophagitis, with no randomised or untreated comparison carded
6025: MAYBE (weak evidence) — in women taking antiseizure medication, a reduction in birth defects from folic acid has not been demonstrated in the direct observational evidence; supplementation is still recommended by guideline, extrapolated from the general population
6026: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — vitamin D alone did not prevent total, nonvertebral or hip fractures in adults not selected for deficiency: HR 0.98 in VITAL (25,871 participants), HR 0.94 in D-Health (20,326), and a pooled relative risk of 1.00 across 81 trials
6027: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: spironolactone-based medical treatment lowered blood pressure substantially in non-surgical primary aldosteronism (175/106 to 129/79 mm Hg over at least 5 years in one adenoma cohort), but complete clinical response was only 18.3% in the 1,258-patient PAMO cohort, and no randomised trial tests spironolactone against no treatment in this population
6028: SPLIT (device generation and access route) — at 10 years in intermediate-risk patients, second-generation SAPIEN XT TAVI had higher mortality than surgery (86.1% vs 82.8%; HR 1.13 relative) and more reintervention (6.3% vs 1.6%), driven by transthoracic access, while third-generation SAPIEN 3 TAVI matched surgery on mortality (HR 1.01 relative) and reintervention (2.0% vs 1.9%); in lower-risk NOTION, severe structural valve deterioration was less frequent after TAVI (1.5% vs 10.0%)
6029: SPLIT (enduring risk factors) — 3 months of anticoagulation fits VTE provoked by surgery alone (recurrence after stopping about 0.7% per patient-year, the lowest of any VTE category, and longer primary treatment doubled major bleeding, relative risk 2.02, in the 22-trial duration pool); where enduring risk factors coexist with the provocation, 12 further months of low-dose apixaban cut recurrence from 10.0% to 1.3% in one trial (HI-PRO)
6030: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only, with no randomised trial in older adults specifically: early cholecystectomy at age 70 and over carried 24% morbidity and 3.5% mortality in the pooled series, delay beyond 72 hours was associated with higher bleeding and mortality in NSQIP (a penalty the authors found most significant in the elderly), and in octogenarians drained first, waiting 6 weeks or more brought recurrent cholecystitis in 52.9% versus 4.9%
6031: SPLIT (symptoms versus mortality) — percutaneous cholecystostomy resolves symptoms in 86–93% of high-risk patients who cannot have surgery and can be definitive treatment (80% had no further attack after drain removal in one grade-3 series), but the single randomised trial found no mortality benefit over conservative treatment (30-day mortality 17.5% versus 13%)
6032: POSSIBLE (benefit) — observational only: in existing users undergoing major surgery, perioperative beta-blocker withdrawal was associated with markedly higher mortality (30-day odds ratio 3.93 relative in one cohort; 1-year hazard ratio 2.7 relative in vascular surgery), while continuous use was associated with lower mortality; no randomised trial has tested continuation versus withdrawal
6035: POSSIBLE (observational) — cascade screening improves early treatment uptake: identified relatives in the Dutch national programme went from 39% on lipid-lowering treatment at identification to 93% one year later, and a paediatric cascade series started statins in 35.3% of parents; but UK routine-care data show 70% of identified patients still not at treatment targets, and no trial isolates the cascade step
6036: POSSIBLE (observational) — penicillin prevents congenital syphilis better than other antibiotics on all available comparative evidence: 98.2% prevention with CDC penicillin regimens prospectively, threefold adjusted odds of congenital syphilis with non-penicillin treatment in the Shenzhen cohort, and no randomised comparison in pregnancy has ever been done
6037: MAYBE (weak evidence) — argatroban appears as effective as other non-heparin anticoagulants for HIT on thrombotic and bleeding outcomes, but every head-to-head report is retrospective (largest: 138 patients vs bivalirudin) and no randomised comparison exists
6039: POSSIBLE — the etonogestrel implant and the standard 52 mg levonorgestrel IUD are comparably effective for long-term pregnancy prevention (every carded long-term rate is under 1 per 100 woman-years; no pregnancies in 444 implant woman-years of extended use versus 0.25–0.43 per 100 woman-years for the IUD in years 6–7), with no demonstrated difference and no head-to-head pregnancy trial
6041: LIKELY — multilayer (four-layer) compression bandaging heals venous leg ulcers faster than no compression: two pragmatic randomised trials beat usual care (healing rate ratio 1.45; 54% vs 34% healed at 3 months) and all 8 direct compression-versus-no-compression trials in the Cochrane review favoured compression
6042: SPLIT (outcome) — a daily multivitamin does not prevent cardiovascular disease (HR 1.01 over 11.2 years in PHS II; HR 0.98 in COSMOS); for cancer, PHS II found a modest 8% relative reduction in total incidence (HR 0.92) with no site-specific or mortality effect, which COSMOS did not reproduce (HR 0.97)
6043: POSSIBLE (observational) — BRCA1/BRCA2 testing in women with a strong family history demonstrably triggers earlier intervention (intensified surveillance; 29 risk-reducing mastectomies and 90 salpingo-oophorectomies in the prospective testing cohort, with no stage III/IV cancers detected after results), but no trial has measured whether testing itself reduces cancer deaths, and BRCA1 carriers under surveillance still had only 73% 5-year survival
6044: LIKELY — prolonged implantable monitoring detects substantially more atrial fibrillation after cryptogenic or otherwise unexplained stroke than conventional follow-up (three concordant randomised trials; detection yield only — none of these trials tested whether the extra detection prevents recurrent stroke)
6047: POSSIBLE (benefit) — plozasiran lowered triglycerides by about 80% versus 17% on placebo in the single phase 3 chylomicronemia trial (PALISADE, 75 patients) and pancreatitis was less frequent (odds ratio 0.17, relative), a secondary outcome with few events; supporting programme data are biomarker and open-label reports
6049: POSSIBLE (observational) — coronary artery calcium predicts coronary events beyond risk scores (adjusted risk about tenfold for scores above 300 versus zero) and reclassifies statin candidacy in both directions in large prospective cohorts; no randomised trial has tested a calcium-guided statin strategy against score-guided care
6051: SPLIT (design) — the double-blind randomised CASCADE trial found no vein graft patency benefit from adding clopidogrel to aspirin (94.3% vs 93.2% at 1 year), while a pooled analysis of 11 mostly observational studies found less early graft occlusion (relative risk 0.59), concentrated in off-pump surgery, with a trend to more bleeding
6053: POSSIBLE (benefit) — built under precedent (b) from secondary analyses of the single SOUL trial (primary report homed on live #72, not re-carded): total first-plus-subsequent major cardiovascular events were fewer with oral semaglutide (mean ratio 0.86, relative), with a heart-failure composite benefit seen in participants with heart failure at baseline (hazard ratio 0.78) and sustained risk-factor improvements
6054: POSSIBLE (benefit) — automated insulin delivery lowered HbA1c by 0.6 percentage points more than continued usual insulin delivery with CGM in the one randomised trial (13 weeks), with single-arm switch studies in the same direction and hypoglycaemia remaining low
6056: POSSIBLE (benefit) — an anabolic-first sequence followed by an antiresorptive preserved and extended bone density and, in the one fracture-counting extension, cut vertebral fractures versus no anabolic first; the reverse order blunted the anabolic response (direct fracture head-to-head homed on live #92)
6059: POSSIBLE (benefit) — secondary-analysis evidence only: SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with roughly a fifth fewer reported new atrial fibrillation events across the outcome-trial programme (DECLARE hazard ratio 0.81; pooled relative risk 0.76), with AF captured as adverse events, not a monitored endpoint
6060: POSSIBLE (test-accuracy, observational evidence) — at the 50 nmol/L (about 1.8 µg/dL) cutoff the 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test is a sensitive screen for autonomous cortisol secretion but with limited, threshold- and assay-dependent specificity; positive results need verification (dexamethasone level, ACTH pattern, repeat testing)
6061: LIKELY — recombinant human TSH preparation achieved radioiodine ablation success equivalent to thyroid hormone withdrawal in low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer (ESTIMABL equivalence; pooled odds ratio 0.87 with confidence interval spanning 1), with better quality of life and fewer adverse events
6062: POSSIBLE (test-accuracy, observational evidence) — the aldosterone-to-renin ratio is a usable screen whose accuracy is assay- and threshold-dependent (sensitivity 10–100% across rigorously verified studies; about 77–87% sensitivity and 85–93% specificity at locally derived cutoffs), so positives need confirmatory testing and negatives can miss disease
6063: POSSIBLE (benefit, observational evidence only) — metformin use in heart failure with type 2 diabetes is associated with lower mortality than mostly sulfonylurea therapy (pooled adjusted estimate 0.80), with no randomised trial and confounding by indication unresolved
6066: POSSIBLE (observational) — home haemodialysis was associated with lower all-cause mortality than in-centre haemodialysis in pooled non-randomised studies (relative risk 0.80) and registry analyses (adjusted hazard ratios 0.51–0.55), at very low certainty with selection bias the main alternative explanation; quality of life was only marginally better physically (SMD 0.14, mostly peritoneal-dialysis studies) and no different mentally
6067: POSSIBLE (observational, test-prognosis) — urine output under 200 mL in the 2 hours after a furosemide stress test predicted progression to stage 3 AKI with an AUC of 0.87 in both derivation (sensitivity 87.1%, specificity 84.1%) and validation (73.9%, 90.0%), and pooled sensitivity/specificity of 0.84/0.77 for later kidney replacement therapy across 11 studies
6068: MAYBE (weak evidence) — an incremental peritoneal dialysis start has not been shown to preserve residual kidney function: the one randomised trial (3 vs 4 exchanges, 139 patients) and the balANZ dose analysis both found no difference in residual-function decline, the one favourable cohort started with double the GFR, and a 10-study review found no survival or technique differences and conflicting residual-function data
6069: POSSIBLE — insulin-dextrose and nebulised salbutamol each shift potassium by about 0.65–0.85 mmol/L and together by about 1.2 mmol/L (additive), while sodium bicarbonate alone made no difference (−0.03 mmol/L) and did not potentiate either agent; insulin's main cost is hypoglycaemia
6070: POSSIBLE (observational) — cystatin C-based eGFR predicts death and kidney failure better than creatinine-based eGFR: net reclassification improvement 0.23 for death and 0.10 for end-stage kidney disease, and a cystatin eGFR at least 30% below the creatinine eGFR carried a mortality hazard ratio of 1.69 and a kidney-failure hazard ratio of 1.29 (all relative measures, from cohort meta-analyses)
6071: MAYBE (weak evidence) — febuxostat may protect kidney function compared with allopurinol, but the supporting evidence is indirect: FREED compared febuxostat with conventional therapy (not allopurinol) in asymptomatic hyperuricaemia, the one direct randomised trial enrolled 120 patients for 6 months at low fixed doses, the retrospective comparisons are all at serious risk of bias, and the CARES post-hoc credits achieved urate under 6 mg/dL rather than the drug
6072: POSSIBLE — late conversion from a calcineurin inhibitor to belatacept improved graft function in two randomised trials of stable established recipients (eGFR 55.5 vs 48.5 mL/min/1.73 m² at 24 months in the phase 3b trial), with survival with a functioning graft unchanged (98% vs 97%), biopsy-proven rejection roughly doubled (8% vs 4%), and fewer de novo donor-specific antibodies (1% vs 7%)
6073: SPLIT (single trial vs programme) — balANZ (homed on live #1738) found fewer peritonitis episodes with neutral-pH, low-GDP solution, but the pooled trial programme (Cochrane, 29 trials) found peritonitis differences uncertain and technique failure or death little or no different, a small randomised trial found no peritonitis difference, and a national registry analysis found a higher peritonitis rate on biocompatible solutions (incidence rate ratio 1.49, relative)
6074: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — GFR is set by the filtration coefficient and net filtration pressure (Guyton & Hall; Boron & Boulpaep), and human clearance studies behave accordingly: protein loading raises GFR by about a third (107 to 146 ml/min by inulin clearance), while low-dose ANP raises filtration fraction without changing GFR
6075: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — insulin and beta-adrenergic stimulation drive potassium into cells (epinephrine cut a load's rise from 0.6 to 0.1 mEq/L; physiological insulin lowered potassium ~0.3 mmol/L), beta-blockade does the reverse, and acid-base status shifts potassium as Ganong / Boron & Boulpaep describe (textbook-labelled leg)
6076: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — cardiac output rises ~3–4-fold in exercise: stroke volume roughly doubles early then plateaus (and expands to fully compensate when beta-blockade caps heart rate), heart rate rises linearly and carries the upper range, and muscle vasodilation permits the rise (Guyton & Hall)
6077: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — the arterial baroreflex buffers short-term pressure variability and answers standing mainly through sympathetic vasomotor control, with a fast vagal cardiac limb (neck-chamber, drug-bolus and ganglion-blockade evidence in humans; Ganong; Guyton & Hall)
6078: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — aldosterone answers potassium first (a 0.2 mEq/L rise raised it 46% with renin/angiotensin II unchanged), angiotensin II second with adrenal gain set by sodium balance, and ACTH only transiently (continuous ACTH back to baseline by 72 h) — Guyton & Hall; Boron & Boulpaep
6079: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — vasopressin is switched off below an osmotic threshold of ~287 mosmol/kg and rises ~0.33 pmol/L per mosmol/kg above it, and its level sets urine concentration and free water clearance across water-balance states (Ganong; Boron & Boulpaep)
6080: LIKELY — terlipressin is as effective as octreotide for controlling acute variceal bleeding and for survival (5-day success 86.2% vs 83.8%; pooled mortality relative risk 1.01), with more adverse events at drug-family level (relative risk 2.39)
6081: LIKELY (rebleeding) — ligation plus a nonselective beta-blocker cut rebleeding versus ligation alone (14% vs 38%; pooled relative risk 0.44); mortality benefit unproven (relative risk 0.58, 95% CI 0.33–1.03)
6082: POSSIBLE — albumin plus antibiotics reduced renal impairment (8.3% vs 30.6%) and mortality (16.0% vs 35.4%) across pooled SBP trials, but the base is four small trials (288 patients) dominated by one homed trial (Sort 1999, live #167, not re-carded here)
6083: LIKELY — carvedilol reduces HVPG more than propranolol on the mean (pooled −1.75 mmHg / −8.02 percentage points; every direct trial in the same direction), though the responder-proportion advantage was non-significant in the largest trial and Cochrane pooling, and carvedilol lowers arterial pressure more (PARTIAL of #3594: direct HVPG slice only)
6084: POSSIBLE — in ACLF, albumin cover for paracentesis reduced circulatory dysfunction and in-hospital death in one small randomised trial, and an albumin-containing bundle was linked to better 28-day survival observationally, but albumin versus another fluid in critically ill cirrhosis improved blood pressure without improving survival; a general survival benefit in ACLF is unproven
6085: LIKELY — sofosbuvir-based DAAs cured 83–94% of Child-Pugh B and most Child-Pugh C patients across ASTRAL-4, SOLAR-2 and ALLY-1, MELD scores improved after treatment while untreated patients worsened, and decompensation events fell; the survival benefit rests on treated-versus-untreated programme comparisons, not a randomised survival trial
6086: POSSIBLE — after pancreatoduodenectomy the one large placebo-controlled trial was null on weight as prescribed (intention-to-treat) but positive as taken (per-protocol, +3.37 kg vs placebo), a small trial found no significant fatty-liver advantage over conventional enzymes, and a cohort linked enzyme use to better survival observationally
6087: LIKELY — combined oral + rectal mesalamine beat oral mesalamine alone for inducing remission in the PINCE trial (64% vs 43% at 8 weeks) and in meta-analysis (relative risk of failing to achieve remission 0.65, number needed to treat 5), with the clearest benefit in extensive disease
6088: SPLIT (severity) — 4.8 g/day beat 2.4 g/day in moderately active ulcerative colitis across the ASCEND trials (treatment success up to 72% vs 59%; remission 43% vs 35% in ASCEND III), but made no difference in the overall mild-to-moderate population of ASCEND I (56% vs 51%)
6089: LIKELY — once-daily mesalamine maintained remission as well as twice-daily dosing in three head-to-head trials (64.4% vs 68.5% at 12 months for MMX; non-inferior endoscopic remission in 826 patients) and in a 7-trial meta-analysis (relapse relative risk 0.94, 95% CI 0.82–1.08)
6090: POSSIBLE — adding surgical closure (after seton drainage) to anti-TNF tripled MRI healing at 18 months in PISA-II (32% vs 9%) and reduced re-interventions in both PISA trials, but clinical closure was not significantly better (68% vs 52%) and the randomised base is small and partly preference-based
6091: POSSIBLE (observational) — no randomised trial exists: pooled series show dilation relieves symptoms in ~81% but 42.9% still reach surgery by 24 months, and the one direct comparison found re-intervention more likely after dilation than surgery (odds ratio 5.62); dilation delays surgery more reliably than it avoids it
6092: LIKELY — low-dose budesonide maintained remission far better than placebo after induction in collagenous colitis (76.5% vs 12% at 24 weeks on 6 mg/day; 61.4% vs 16.7% at 12 months on ~4.5 mg/day), with relapse the rule after stopping; maintenance in lymphocytic colitis is untrialled
6093: LIKELY — in chronic non-cancer pain, subcutaneous methylnaltrexone produced a rescue-free bowel movement within 4 hours in 34.2% vs 9.9% on placebo and oral methylnaltrexone raised responder rates to 49.3–51.5% vs 38.3%, in two phase 3 placebo-controlled programmes
6094: POSSIBLE (observational evidence for the timing comparison) — ERCP within 24 hours was associated with lower in-hospital mortality than later drainage in pooled observational studies (odds ratio 0.81, a relative measure), and emergency endoscopic drainage itself beat emergency surgery in the one randomised trial (10% versus 32% hospital mortality); no randomised trial has tested drainage timing directly
6095: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — urgent colonoscopy within 24 hours did not reduce further bleeding, transfusion, length of stay, surgery or mortality versus elective colonoscopy in three randomised trials and their meta-analysis (463 randomised patients)
6096: POSSIBLE (observational evidence — diagnostic yield, not patient outcomes) — capsule endoscopy finds a small-bowel lesion in roughly half of adults with iron deficiency anaemia after negative bidirectional endoscopy (pooled yield 47–61% for any lesion, ~40% for a lesion likely responsible, 8% actionable in the exact-population cohort)
6097: POSSIBLE — daily maintenance proton pump inhibitor therapy prevented relapse of healed erosive oesophagitis better than on-demand therapy (remission 81% versus 58% at 6 months in the one large head-to-head trial, concordant with the systematic review); symptom relief in mild disease was closer, and on-demand therapy used about a third as much drug
6098: SPLIT (duration) — a bedtime H2 blocker improves nocturnal gastric acid control on the first nights in small pH studies (breakthrough 82% without versus 40% with), but the only study that kept measuring found the advantage gone by one week (tolerance), and no study measured symptom relief in documented twice-daily-PPI non-responders
6099: SPLIT (outcome) — rubber band ligation and infrared coagulation controlled grade II haemorrhoids about equally (satisfactory outcomes 92–97% versus 85–92%; no efficacy difference in the 2023 meta-analysis of 9 trials), with more recurrence or failure after coagulation in the grade II trial but consistently more pain after band ligation
6101: POSSIBLE — trientine was non-inferior to penicillamine for maintaining copper control in the one head-to-head randomised trial (CHELATE, 53 stable patients; non-caeruloplasmin-bound copper difference −9.1 μg/L, inside the −50 μg/L margin), with long-term switch cohorts consistent
6102: POSSIBLE — zinc supplementation improved psychometric encephalopathy tests versus standard therapy alone in small trials and their meta-analyses (number-connection standardised mean difference −0.62 to −0.97), but did not significantly reduce encephalopathy recurrence (relative risk 0.64, 95% CI 0.26–1.59) and no trial reported mortality; tested preparations were zinc acetate and polaprezinc
6103: POSSIBLE — oral antibiotics performed as well as intravenous therapy in three small randomised trials of uncomplicated diverticulitis (79, 50 and 118 patients; one a step-down design, one with both routes given to outpatients), with no conversions, failures or readmission signals favouring the intravenous route
6104: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference) — standard-dose ursodeoxycholic acid improved liver blood tests but did not improve transplant-free survival in the one standard-dose placebo trial or in either meta-analysis of the randomised trials
6105: POSSIBLE (observational) — no randomised trial and no direct surveillance-versus-none mortality comparison exists; cohorts put the annual gastric cancer incidence in intestinal metaplasia at about 0.25% and one cohort links a 2–3-year surveillance interval in extensive disease to earlier cancer detection, so a death benefit is plausible but unproven
6106: POSSIBLE — pregabalin reduced pain more than placebo in one small 3-week trial (64 patients; pain relief 36% vs 24%), with supportive mechanistic data from the same trial's patients and a positive combination-therapy trial that cannot separate pregabalin's own effect
6107: SPLIT — the phase IIb trial found clear benefit over placebo (57–64% vs 41% responders), but two larger phase III trials found no difference in global symptom response (the treatment made no difference on their co-primary global assessment), while a meta-analysis pooling placebo and active comparators found a modest advantage (relative risk 1.11 for global assessment)
6108: POSSIBLE (single-arm and observational evidence) — in prospective treatment studies of people with recent injection drug use, direct-acting antivirals cured 91–94% (SIMPLIFY, D3FEAT), and a meta-analysis pooling 670 people with recent injecting found an 87.4% cure rate — near, but not proven equal to, the 90–99% rates in the general-population trials homed on live #593
6109: LIKELY — adding a second endoscopic method after epinephrine injection reduced further bleeding from 18.8% to 10.4%, emergency surgery from 10.8% to 7.1% and mortality from 5% to 2.5% in the Cochrane pooling of 17 trials, with concordant results in the earlier meta-analysis and the individual trials
6110: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference to patient outcomes) — pre-endoscopy proton pump inhibitor reduced the need for endoscopic therapy (8.6% vs 11.7% pooled; 19.1% vs 28.4% in the largest trial) and down-staged bleeding stigmata, but made no difference to mortality, rebleeding or surgery in any pooling
6111: SPLIT (measure; imaging surrogate) — empagliflozin reduced liver fat on MRI proton-density fat fraction in two small trials (between-group difference −4.0% in E-LIFT; median change −2.49% vs −1.43% against placebo over 52 weeks), but elastography-based measurement showed no advantage (controlled attenuation parameter unchanged versus placebo, and a 3-trial meta-analysis found no improvement); liver fat is an imaging surrogate, with no histology or clinical-outcome evidence carded
6112: POSSIBLE — anamorelin increased lean body mass versus placebo in three independent trial reports outside the ROMANA programme (pooled phase 2 difference 2.09 kg; Japanese phase 2 and phase 3 trials concordant), but handgrip strength and walking did not improve in any of them (function made no difference)
6113: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference in the placebo trial) — SCARLET, the only large placebo-controlled trial, found 28-day mortality of 26.8% on thrombomodulin versus 29.4% on placebo (P = .32, not significant), and the updated meta-analysis estimate (relative risk 0.87, 95% CI 0.74–1.03) remains nonsignificant with only 42% of the required information size accrued
6114: POSSIBLE (benefit, observational evidence) — a gluten-free diet heals the mucosa in many adults but slowly and often incompletely: recovery 34% at 2 years and 66% at 5 years in the Mayo cohort, complete normalisation only 8% at a median 16 months in the largest adult series
6115: POSSIBLE (benefit) — intravenous iron improves quality-of-life scores as it corrects IBD iron-deficiency anaemia (FERGIcor; PHOSPHARE-IBD), and beats oral iron on haemoglobin response pooled (relative risk 1.17; 368/554 vs 205/373), but a quality-of-life advantage over oral iron specifically is not directly demonstrated
6116: POSSIBLE (benefit, low-certainty evidence) — intravenous selenium (sodium selenite in the trials) pooled at relative risk 0.82–0.86 for overall mortality, but 28-day mortality was not significantly reduced and the largest trial's intention-to-treat primary analysis was null
6117: SPLIT — prophylactic gastrostomy gave less weight loss and better quality of life at 6 months in the randomised trial and less short-term critical weight loss in the pooled review, but the largest propensity-matched cohort (526 patients) found greater weight loss with prophylaxis (median 5 kg vs 3 kg at 6 weeks) and less with the reactive approach to 1 year
6118: POSSIBLE (benefit, narrow) — early oral feeding did not increase leakage or pneumonia in any carded trial and sped bowel recovery and 2-week quality of life, but NUTRIENT II found no faster functional recovery (7 vs 8 days; the treatment made no difference)
6119: POSSIBLE (benefit) — glutamine-supplemented parenteral nutrition reduced postoperative infections in relative terms in two surgical meta-analyses (relative risk 0.48 and 0.60), with no significant mortality difference in either
6120: POSSIBLE (benefit, observational evidence) — no randomised trial in the intermediate-risk band; untreated febrile neutropenia was 9% per course prospectively, and prophylaxis was associated with modestly lower first-cycle rates in claims cohorts (2.6% vs 2.7–3.7%), with risk concentrated in patients with added risk factors
6121: POSSIBLE (same-day pegfilgrastim is less effective, observational evidence) — febrile neutropenia was higher with same-day administration in all three cohorts: 11.4% vs 8.4% in cycle 1 (Medicare), 24.6% vs 11.7% on dose-dense AC, and 9.4% vs 5.1% of CHOP cycles
6122: LIKELY (benefit) — adding an NK1 antagonist improved complete response in moderately emetogenic chemotherapy (80.2% vs 64.6% in the carboplatin phase 3 subgroup; pooled relative risk 1.14), with the benefit significant for carboplatin-based but not oxaliplatin-based regimens
6123: POSSIBLE (benefit) — olanzapine 5 mg appears as effective as 10 mg for nausea and vomiting control (complete response 58.6% vs 62.9% in the one direct trial, within a wide −25% non-inferiority margin) with less sedation in the pooled dose literature; the direct evidence is a single small trial
6124: POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference) — adding empirical vancomycin/glycopeptide in febrile neutropenia without resistant gram-positive infection did not reduce mortality in two meta-analyses (relative risk 0.86; odds ratio 0.67, both crossing 1) and roughly doubled nephrotoxicity
6127: POSSIBLE — aspirin vs enoxaparin in myeloma on immunomodulatory drugs: no significant difference in two randomised trials (composite 6.4% vs 5.0%; VTE 2.27% vs 1.20%), with wide confidence intervals and few events
6128: SPLIT (endpoint/era) — small early venography trials found large reductions in catheter thrombosis with low-dose warfarin/dalteparin, but the largest placebo-controlled trial (symptomatic thrombosis 4.6% vs 4.0%) and an 8-trial meta-analysis (relative risk 0.59, CI crossing 1) found no benefit
6129: LIKELY — avatrombopag avoided platelet transfusion or rescue in 65.6–88.1% vs 22.9–38.2% across the two ADAPT phase 3 trials in chronic liver disease, with a concordant phase 2 trial
6130: POSSIBLE (observational evidence for the schedule outcome) — romiplostim corrected platelets in 93% vs 12.5% in a 23-patient randomised phase, and observational cohorts report most patients resuming chemotherapy without dose delay or reduction
6131: LIKELY — fluconazole prophylaxis reduced systemic fungal infection vs placebo in two randomised trials (2.8% vs 15.8% and 7% vs 18%), with better survival in one trial (31 vs 52 deaths) and in transplant-subgroup pooling (relative risk 0.62)
6132: POSSIBLE — corticosteroids improved appetite (77% of evaluable patients in a 40-patient crossover) and quality-of-life scores (403-patient trial) vs placebo in advanced cancer, on old short-term evidence with mixed review findings
6133: MAYBE (weak evidence) — a higher dexamethasone dose has not been shown to improve walking in malignant spinal cord compression: the one bolus comparison (37 patients) found no difference, and the one dose pilot (20 patients) never completed
6134: POSSIBLE — ondansetron prevented vomiting during abdominal radiotherapy in the one direct placebo-controlled trial (complete emesis control 67% vs 45%) and beat metoclopramide and prochlorperazine in the same population, but the systematic review found most published data invalid, no benefit beyond 24 hours, and an inconsistent nausea effect
6135: POSSIBLE (observational evidence) — stepping down from an echinocandin to fluconazole at about day 5 in candidemia patients who are already responding was associated with outcomes as good as continued intravenous therapy in one prospective programme and two retrospective cohorts, with no randomised trial of the step-down decision
6138: POSSIBLE — oral antibiotic therapy was as effective as intravenous therapy for uncomplicated mild-to-moderate cellulitis in one double-blind non-inferiority trial (failure 4.2% vs 6.1%), one non-randomised route analysis, and a Cochrane subgroup comparison; severe cellulitis is untested
6139: POSSIBLE (harm, observational and small-trial evidence) — adding an aminoglycoside to a beta-lactam in native valve staphylococcal endocarditis showed no mortality, success or relapse benefit in pooled trials (261 patients) and increased kidney injury (significant fall in creatinine clearance 22% vs 8% with initial low-dose gentamicin)
6140: POSSIBLE — adjunctive corticosteroid made no difference in herpes simplex encephalitis: DexEnceph found verbal memory 71 vs 69 at 26 weeks (adjusted difference 1.77, 95% CI −9.57 to 13.12), the pooled randomised relative risk for unfavourable outcome was 1.00, and a 3,933-patient cohort found no mortality or functional benefit
6142: SPLIT — replacing the catheter before antibiotics improved early clinical status (25 vs 11 patients) and relapse (3 vs 11) in the one small direct randomised trial (Raz, 54 patients), but the only other randomised comparison, which bundled exchange with a shorter antibiotic course, found 100% cure both ways with higher recurrence after exchange; a 2024 review of all four existing studies calls the evidence conflicting
6143: POSSIBLE (observational evidence) — in prosthetic joint infection, oral step-down achieved failure rates no worse than prolonged intravenous therapy in three PJI-specific retrospective cohorts (failure 9.2% vs 15.6% in the largest, 172 patients); the randomised OVIVA anchor is homed on live #312 and is not re-carded here (precedent (b))
6144: POSSIBLE — linezolid is at least as effective as vancomycin for clinical cure of MRSA complicated skin infection, and was more effective in the proven-MRSA population of the largest trial (cure 88.6% vs 66.9%); the dedicated MRSA trial's per-protocol analysis was similar between the drugs
6145: POSSIBLE (observational) — retrospective series totalling 873 patients found serological cure on doxycycline statistically indistinguishable from benzathine penicillin (failure 0% vs 5.5%; 12-month response 92.4% vs 96.2%); no randomised trial exists in the fetched records
6146: POSSIBLE (observational) — registry evidence: tuberculosis on anti-TNF therapy was 7 times more likely when latent-TB screening recommendations were not followed (BIOBADASER), and none of RATIO's 69 cases had received correct chemoprophylaxis; no randomised trial exists
6147: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — rising iron stores raise hepatic hepcidin (urinary hepcidin greatly increased in iron overload, tracking ferritin), hepcidin degrades ferroportin, and absorption falls measurably within 24 hours (next-dose fractional absorption down 35–45% after a ≥60 mg dose) (Guyton & Hall; Ganong)
6148: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — gut (portal-drained viscera) is the largest ammonia source, the cirrhotic and shunted liver clears little, skeletal muscle removes more ammonia than the liver (fixing it as glutamine), and the kidney becomes a major producer after a gut bleed (production up 6-fold) (Guyton & Hall; Ganong)

7166: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — total haemoglobin mass about 780–850 g in small healthy samples (≈14 g/kg and blood volume ≈100 mL/kg in elite runners), about 30% higher with endurance training, measured by optimised CO rebreathing to about 2% typical error; the Nadler formulas are not validated by any fetched record and carry no accuracy figure here
7167: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — erythrocyte sedimentation rate in health is low (about 76% under 9 mm/h), rises with age and runs higher in women, with 95% upper limits of 12–19 mm/h (men) and 18–23 mm/h (women) in 3,910 Norwegians, corroborated by 4,202 Danish donors and 989 Italians across Westergren and automated methods; one classic (Böttiger & Svedberg 1967) was refused for an empty abstract
7168: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING — phase angle at 50 kHz follows a concordant life-course arc (midlife peak, men above women, decline after 50) across 13,256 Chinese and 5,049 Colombian adults, but values are population-specific (5th–95th ranges from 4.49–6.12° in Yao women to 5.53–7.65° in Korean men) and its determinants explain only 42–54% of variance, so no universal range exists yet

7190: LIKELY (benefit) — two phase 3 placebo-controlled trials (RAJ4 and the 2024 Asian phase 3) plus a dose-finding phase IIb trial concordantly show peficitinib 100/150 mg superior to placebo on ACR20 (about 56–64% vs 22–24%) with less radiographic progression in RAJ4; the base is single-region (Japan/Asia, approved in Japan only) and carries JAK-class harms (serious infections, herpes zoster)
