7192: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — a failed programme: both phase 3 trials (1,176 and 1,030 patients) missed the structural endpoint with no claimable symptom benefit, and the post-hoc endotype analysis found no significant overall treatment effect; only a small 84-day phase 2 trial (n=53) pointed the other way
7193: POSSIBLE (benefit) — SINGLE-TRIAL FLAG: one phase 3 trial (SEKOIA) reported in several publications showed a small slowing of joint space narrowing (0.10–0.14 mm over 3 years) and a symptom responder advantage at 2 g/day only; the drug was restricted and withdrawn in Europe over cardiovascular safety and never FDA-approved
7194: POSSIBLE (benefit) — two placebo-controlled trials (n=116 over 2 years; n=169 crossover) favour colchicine for mucocutaneous and articular manifestations, but the base is old, the 2001 benefit was concentrated in women, the long-term follow-up found no reduction in immunosuppressive use, and one 1980 anchor was refused at build for an empty PubMed abstract
7195: POSSIBLE (benefit) — three randomised head-to-head trials show benzbromarone reaching urate target at least as often as low-dose febuxostat (61% vs 32% in one; 35.7% vs 39.5% in another) and more often than probenecid after allopurinol failure (92% vs 65%), but the endpoint is a surrogate, comparators were fixed low doses, trials were short, and the drug was withdrawn in several markets over hepatotoxicity and is unavailable in the US
7196: POSSIBLE (benefit) — noninferiority to darbepoetin on haemoglobin shown in three Japanese phase 3 trials (ESA-naive non-dialysis, ESA-treated non-dialysis, and haemodialysis; differences −0.38 to +0.13 g/dL) with up-to-36-month extension support, but haemoglobin is a surrogate throughout, the programme is single-region (Japan; not FDA/EMA-approved), and cardiovascular-safety experience is shorter than for ESAs
7197: POSSIBLE (benefit) — haemoglobin control shown across the programme: noninferiority to darbepoetin (SYMPHONY HD) and to erythropoietin (ENARODIAL), a clear placebo-controlled Hb rise in non-dialysis CKD (+1.60 g/dL), phase 2b dose response, and single-arm target maintenance in peritoneal dialysis (n=37); haemoglobin is a surrogate throughout and the programme is single-region (Japan/China; approved in Japan, not FDA/EMA-approved)
7198: POSSIBLE (benefit) — noninferiority to epoetin alfa (DREAM-D, n=392) and to darbepoetin (DREAM-ND, n=588) on haemoglobin, with more Hb responders on desidustat in both and a dose-related phase 2 signal; haemoglobin is a surrogate throughout, both phase 3 trials were open-label and 24 weeks, and the programme is single-region (India; not FDA/EMA-approved)
7199: POSSIBLE (benefit) — randomised trials from a single region (China) show leflunomide comparable to azathioprine for maintenance (kidney flares 15.7% vs 17.8%) and to cyclophosphamide for induction (complete remission 23% vs 27%), never superior; supporting reports are a single-arm refractory study (N=20, labelled, not load-bearing) and a 2005 controlled trial (n=51); teratogenicity and hepatotoxicity warnings lead the harm side
7200: POSSIBLE (benefit) — one open-label phase 3 randomised trial (n=250) found oral mizoribine noninferior, not superior, to intravenous cyclophosphamide for lupus nephritis induction (total remission 66.1% vs 76.8%); the remaining base is small uncontrolled Japanese reports (n=17, n=10 and a labelled sub-floor N=6), and the programme is single-region (China/Japan)
7201: LIKELY (benefit) — three phase 3 randomised trials (n=535, 739, 533) consistently showed chiglitazar lowered HbA1c versus placebo, was noninferior to sitagliptin, and added benefit on metformin, with slight weight gain and mild oedema; the stamp is for glycaemic control only — HbA1c is a surrogate, the evidence is single-region (China), and no cardiovascular-outcomes trial exists
7202: POSSIBLE (benefit) — based on a very small evidence base (n=18, 16 completers and n=19; three short phase 2 reports, treatment 3–28 days): avexitide consistently raised glucose nadir and reduced hypoglycaemic events, including against placebo in the n=18 PREVENT crossover, but there is no phase 3 or long-term evidence and two reports enrolled women only
7203: POSSIBLE (benefit) — a single phase 3 trial (n=1,054, Japan) reported in three publications (primary plus two post-hoc analyses, labelled as one programme) found eldecalcitol reduced vertebral fractures versus the active comparator alfacalcidol (13.4% vs 17.5%; hazard ratio 0.74, relative), with more frequent increases in serum and urinary calcium; there is no placebo comparison and no second trial
7205: LIKELY (benefit) — the NATRON phase 3 trial (n=133) showed benralizumab added to background therapy reduced the hazard of a first HES flare versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.35, relative) with similar adverse-event rates, supported by a separate small phase 2 programme (n=20) and its long-term extension (14 followed, exposure up to 10.1 years); the base is two programmes, not three trials
7206: SPLIT — the European 12-week trial (n=130) showed a walk-distance benefit for beraprost versus placebo, but the US 12-month trial (n=116) found benefits only at 3–6 months, not at 9–12 months; the network meta-analysis carded here is a prostacyclin-class pool, not a third beraprost trial, and the withdrawn prostacyclin network meta-analysis is fenced and not carded
7207: SPLIT — levofloxacin inhalation solution improved FEV1 and sputum Pseudomonas density (phase 2, n=151) and was noninferior to tobramycin inhalation solution (phase 3, n=282), but the placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (n=330) missed its primary endpoint of time to exacerbation; dysgeusia was the most frequent adverse event
7208: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — three Japanese noninferiority trials (996, 184 and 201 patients analysed) found a single inhaled dose of laninamivir gave times to illness alleviation similar to a 5-day oseltamivir course in adults, children and patients with chronic respiratory disease; treatment question only, the prophylaxis programme is deliberately not folded in, and laninamivir is licensed in Japan only
7209: SPLIT — high-dose rifampicin speeds sputum culture conversion (PanACEA 35 mg/kg hazard ratio 1.78, relative; meta-analysis of 8 RCTs: week-8 conversion relative risk 1.06, relative) and 40 mg/kg was tolerable in small cohorts, but 50 mg/kg was not tolerated (n=17) and RIFASHORT's 4-month high-dose regimens failed noninferiority versus 6-month standard treatment, so no shorter or more effective regimen is proven
7210: LIKELY (benefit) — PURSUIT induction gave week-6 response 51.0-54.9% versus 30.3% on placebo and PURSUIT-M maintained response through week 54 in 47.0-49.7% of induction responders versus 31.2% on placebo; a single programme, with a responder-enriched maintenance design
7211: POSSIBLE (benefit) — PRECISE 1 gave only modest response gains (35% vs 27% at week 6) with no significant remission difference, while responder-enriched PRECISE 2 maintained response (63% vs 36%) and remission (48% vs 29%) to week 26; US-only Crohn's licence
7212: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — the phase 3 trial (n=701, terminated for futility) found week-12 remission 22.8% on mongersen versus 25% on placebo, failing to reproduce the small phase 2 trial's 55-65% remission; the phase 2 batch controversy is flagged on the face
7213: LIKELY (benefit, small absolute gain) — budesonide MMX 9 mg induced remission in 17.9% (CORE I) and 17.4% (CORE II) versus 7.4% and 4.5% on placebo: absolute remission under 18%, gains of about 10-13 percentage points; 6 mg ineffective
7214: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — the two large EPIC trials (738 patients combined) found no relapse prevention (31.6% vs 35.7%; 47.8% vs 48.8%) and the Cochrane low-bias pool was null, outweighing the small positive 1996 trial (n=78); the era split is on the face
7215: SPLIT — small gluten-challenge trials show mucosal protection on a surrogate endpoint (2014 positive; 2022 primary endpoint P=.057), but the large symptomatic-patient trial (n=494) was negative on its primary endpoint, and the seropositive symptom signal is post-hoc
7216: MAYBE (weak evidence) — small trials only (n=41; crossover n=12; crossover n=10 at the floor; one labelled sub-floor n=8 limb): short-term PN/absorption gains, Cochrane verdict inconclusive, effects short-lived after stopping
7217: SPLIT — sphincterotomy benefited only manometry-verified stenosis in two small older trials (n=47, n=81), while EPISOD (n=214, unselected suspected dysfunction) found it worse than sham (23% vs 37% success) and manometry non-predictive; Cochrane certainty very low
7218: LIKELY (benefit) — ramosetron at sex-specific doses (5 µg men, 2.5 µg women) beat placebo in three Japanese phase 2/3 trials (stool consistency 50.3% vs 19.6% in men; global improvement 50.7% vs 32.0% in women) and a ramosetron-specific meta-analysis (relative risks 1.41-1.72); PARTIAL to pack #2772's class question, whose meta-analysis is not re-carded

7220: SPLIT (benefit) for spleen-volume response / (no difference) for symptom score — TRANSFORM-1 randomised data show SVR35 63.2% vs 31.5% with a non-significant symptom-score difference (P=.2852) and more cytopenia; post-ruxolitinib evidence is single-arm phase 2 only
7221: SPLIT (no difference) on the primary efficacy endpoint / (benefit) on tolerability for zanubrutinib — ASPEN's primary endpoint was non-significant (VGPR 28% vs 19%, P=.09; no complete responses) while atrial fibrillation and several other adverse events were less common and neutropenia more common with zanubrutinib
7222: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm, uncontrolled evidence only (ELM-1/ELM-2): complete response 73.4% in relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma and 31.5% in DLBCL, with cytokine release syndrome in roughly half of patients; no randomised or comparative data exist
7223: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm, uncontrolled evidence only (C-144-01): objective response 31.4% with median response duration 36.5 months at 5 years, offset by near-universal grade 3/4 toxicity from the lymphodepletion/interleukin-2 package; no comparative data exist
7225: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm, uncontrolled evidence only: sustained clinical complete response at 12 months in 37 of 49 completed rectal patients in the expanded phase 2 and 68% in AZUR-1, allowing omission of chemoradiation and surgery under surveillance; no randomised comparison exists
7226: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme, uncontrolled primary evidence (MOUNTAINEER): objective response 39.3% with median response duration 15.2 months in chemotherapy-refractory HER2-positive, RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer; no randomised comparison against standard therapy exists
7227: LIKELY (benefit) — two randomised trials show progression-free-survival benefit: SERENA-6 ctDNA-guided switch (16.8 vs 9.2 months; hazard ratio 0.45, relative) and SERENA-2 vs fulvestrant (7.2-7.7 vs 3.7 months); overall survival not yet reported in the carded records

7230: LIKELY (benefit) — one phase 3 randomised trial (TALAPRO-2) showed talazoparib + enzalutamide improved radiographic PFS and final overall survival versus enzalutamide alone in first-line mCRPC, with the survival benefit concentrated in HRR-deficient (especially BRCA1/2) disease (HRR-deficient OS 45.1 vs 31.1 months, HR 0.62 relative; all-comer OS 45.8 vs 37.0 months, HR 0.80 relative), at the cost of grade 3–4 anaemia in about 41–49%; the US approval is limited to HRR gene-mutated disease, and the HRR-non-deficient survival effect was not significant
7231: LIKELY (benefit) — the single phase 3 CROWN trial showed first-line lorlatinib gave far more durable progression-free and intracranial control than crizotinib (median PFS not reached at 7 years vs 9.1 months; 5-year PFS 60% vs 8%, absolute rates printed), with chronic hyperlipidaemia, oedema, weight gain and CNS effects as the main harms; no completed overall-survival comparison exists yet, and crizotinib is a superseded first-generation comparator

7233: POSSIBLE (benefit) — based entirely on single-arm, uncontrolled phase 2 programmes (GEOMETRY mono-1 for capmatinib, VISION for tepotinib) in MET exon 14-skipping NSCLC: response rates of 41–68% (capmatinib) and 45–57% (tepotinib) by treatment line, with no randomised comparator, no survival comparison, and no basis for ranking the two drugs; peripheral oedema is the class harm

7239: LIKELY (benefit) — the single phase 3 MARIPOSA trial showed first-line amivantamab + lazertinib improved progression-free survival (23.7 vs 16.6 months) and final overall survival (HR 0.75 relative; 3-year survival 60% vs 51%) versus osimertinib in exon 19 deletion/L858R EGFR-mutated NSCLC, with the lazertinib-alone arm comparable to osimertinib alone, at the cost of grade 3-or-higher toxicity in 80% vs 52% including venous thromboembolism and infusion-related events
7240: LIKELY (benefit) — single-programme evidence (ALINA, n=257): adjuvant alectinib for 24 months improved 2-year disease-free survival versus platinum chemotherapy (93.8% vs 63.0% in stage II–IIIA; hazard ratio 0.24, relative) with a CNS disease-free-survival advantage; overall survival was immature, so this is a recurrence benefit, not yet a proven survival benefit

7263: SPLIT — fostamatinib beat placebo on ACR20 in methotrexate and TNF inadequate responders in phase III, but failed its radiographic endpoint, failed outright in biologic inadequate responders, was inferior to adalimumab as monotherapy, and carries consistent hypertension/diarrhoea/neutropenia harm; the RA programme was discontinued after phase III and the drug was never marketed for RA
7264: POSSIBLE (benefit) — one small placebo-controlled RCT improved patient-reported ESSPRI versus placebo, and an active-comparator RCT missed its primary endpoint while favouring iguratimod on secondary activity measures; the whole base is small and single-region (China), and a retracted iguratimod report is fenced and not counted

7282: POSSIBLE (benefit) — zafirlukast 20 mg twice daily improved symptoms and lung function versus placebo over 13 weeks in two trials in mild-to-moderate asthma (762 and 146 patients; symptom-free days 7.0 vs 3.7 per month in absolute terms), while a small 2-week mechanistic crossover found low-dose fluticasone superior on bronchial hyper-responsiveness; 1990s programme, no exacerbation-outcome trial
7283: POSSIBLE (benefit) — montelukast beat placebo in a 895-patient phase 3 trial and added significant benefit to inhaled beclomethasone in 642 patients, but was inferior to inhaled beclomethasone head-to-head and the trials predate modern ICS/LABA care; the largest effect is confined to aspirin-intolerant asthma (80 patients)
7284: SPLIT — chronic-dosing trials show a modest bronchodilator edge for levalbuterol (first-dose peak FEV1 0.92 vs 0.82 L; paediatric MDI significant versus placebo where racemic albuterol was not), while acute-asthma evidence shows no advantage: one continuous-nebulisation trial favoured racemic albuterol and a 7-trial meta-analysis (1,625 participants) found no significant difference
7285: POSSIBLE (benefit) — two placebo-controlled trials showed inhaled zanamivir shortened influenza by a median 1–1.5 days (2.5 days in high-risk patients), with the complication evidence resting on a small high-risk subgroup and a retrospective pooled analysis rather than a dedicated high-risk trial
7286: SPLIT — the two phase 3 trials (one publication) disagree on time to illness alleviation (+14.4 hours significant in US316, not significant in US317) despite consistent antiviral effects, and the open-label AD ASTRA platform trial was positive on viral clearance but not on symptom resolution
7287: LIKELY (benefit) — three randomised household-contact trials from one Japanese programme consistently reduced clinical influenza (4.5% vs 12.1% for a single 40 mg dose; 11% vs 19% in children), with relative risk reductions of 45.8–78.1% relative and absolutes printed on every card; laninamivir is licensed in Japan only
7288: SPLIT — the international STRIVE trial (492 patients) found no effect on mortality or ventilator-free days with a higher 180-day mortality signal, while the earlier Japanese phase 3 programme (230 patients) reported improved pulmonary-function ratings and shorter ventilation without a survival benefit; the 2017 meta-analysis (6 RCTs, 804 patients) was null on mortality (relative risk 0.94)
7289: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — a failed programme: the phase 2 NEJM trial missed its primary endpoint (70-point response 54% vs 44%, P=0.28), the Cochrane pool of 3 studies (537 patients) found no significant remission benefit (relative risk 1.67, 95% CI 0.80 to 3.50) on low-quality evidence, and no phase 3 confirmation ever followed
7340: SPLIT — aleglitazar lowered HbA1c dose-dependently in the SYNCHRONY phase II study (−0.36% at 50 µg to −1.35% at 600 µg vs placebo), but in AleCardio (7,226 post-ACS patients) it showed no difference in cardiovascular outcomes (9.5% vs 10.0%; hazard ratio 0.96, a relative measure) with more renal dysfunction (7.4% vs 2.7%) and gastrointestinal haemorrhage (2.4% vs 1.7%); AleCardio was terminated early for futility and safety and the programme was discontinued, never marketed. The renal and exposure–response cards are labelled programme reports, not independent trials
7341: LIKELY (benefit) — evogliptin 5 mg improved glycaemic control across four randomised trials: non-inferior to sitagliptin added to metformin (difference 0.06%, 95% CI −0.10 to 0.22; and −0.022% in EVOLUTION INDIA) and to linagliptin (−0.10%, 95% CI −0.32 to 0.11), and superior to placebo when added to dapagliflozin plus metformin (−0.65% at week 24, −0.55% at week 52); the benefit is on the HbA1c surrogate only, the evidence is single-region (South Korea/India; not FDA/EMA-approved), and no cardiovascular-outcomes trial exists for this agent
7343: POSSIBLE (benefit) — gemigliptin lowered HbA1c versus placebo as add-on to dapagliflozin + metformin (SOLUTION, −0.66 points at 24 weeks) and matched linagliptin in renal impairment (GUARD extension), but the base is single-region (South Korea), HbA1c is a surrogate, no outcomes trial exists, and the BALANCE report is a fixed-dose combination read labelled as such
7344: LIKELY (benefit, glycaemic control only) — four randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in China and Korea consistently show teneligliptin 20 mg lowers HbA1c by 0.71–0.94 points more than placebo over 16–24 weeks, alone or added to metformin, with placebo-like safety; HbA1c is a surrogate, the base is single-region (East Asia), and no outcomes trial exists
7345: POSSIBLE (benefit) — anagliptin lowered HbA1c by 0.80 points versus placebo added to metformin + empagliflozin in one phase 3 trial, and twice-daily dosing improved glycaemic variability versus once-daily sitagliptin, but REASON — its longest trial — is open-label with an LDL-cholesterol primary endpoint and only a −4.5 mg/dL absolute difference; single-region (Japan/Korea) evidence, surrogate endpoints, no outcomes trial
7346: MAYBE (weak evidence) — piclidenoson (CF101) met COMFORT-1's primary endpoint only at 3 mg with a modest PASI 75 rate of 9.7% versus 2.6% on placebo, its phase II/III trial missed the same endpoint (8.5% vs 6.9%), and the phase 2 signal rests on 75 patients; safety is consistently placebo-like, but the efficacy base is weak and the agent is not FDA/EMA-approved for psoriasis
7347: LIKELY (benefit) — in the single GLOW programme, glycopyrronium 50 µg once daily improved trough FEV1 by ~100 mL versus placebo in two trials (822 and 1,066 randomised), improved dyspnoea and health status, reduced moderate/severe exacerbations by 31–34% in relative terms on secondary endpoints, and matched open-label tiotropium; the pooled analysis is a programme report, not a third trial
7348: LIKELY (benefit, lung function) — two replicate 48-week placebo-controlled trials (one publication; 624 and 642 patients evaluated) show olodaterol 5 µg and 10 µg significantly improve FEV1 responses, pooled one-year safety in 3,104 patients is comparable to placebo and formoterol, and TONADO shows the fixed-dose combination beats the olodaterol mono-component; the licensed dose is 5 µg and the 10 µg arm is a trial dose
7349: LIKELY (benefit, lung function and symptoms) — three randomised trials (1,683, 1,002 and 1,732 patients) consistently show once-daily indacaterol raises trough FEV1 by 170–180 mL versus placebo and by 60–100 mL versus twice-daily salmeterol/formoterol, with dyspnoea and health-status improvements; a 2010–2011 programme with no exacerbation-outcome or mortality trial, and INHANCE's tiotropium arm was open-label
7350: LIKELY (benefit, airway function) — nebulised arformoterol beat placebo on trough FEV1 across at least four 12-week trials in three reports (1,456 pooled subjects and 717 patients), improved dyspnoea versus placebo, and showed stable one-year safety in an open-label comparison with salmeterol, with more tremor (13.4% vs 1.1%); endpoints are airway function and safety, not exacerbations or mortality, and the two-trials-one-publication report counts once
7351: POSSIBLE (benefit) — four small placebo-controlled trials from 1988–1996 (89, 188, 30 and 26 randomised) consistently show modest symptom and peak-flow benefits from adding inhaled nedocromil in chronic and steroid-dependent asthma; the steroid-resistant trial (N=12 nedocromil completers, printed on its card) is never load-bearing, there is no exacerbation-outcome trial, and the drug was withdrawn from several markets for commercial reasons
7352: SPLIT — MIST1, the large definitive trial of intrapleural streptokinase alone (454 randomised), found no benefit on death or surgical drainage (31% vs 27%; relative risk 1.14), while the Cochrane syntheses pooling MIST1 with smaller older trials report fewer surgical interventions (2019 odds ratio 0.37, low certainty) that disappear when restricted to low/unclear risk-of-bias trials; no mortality benefit in any analysis; the tPA + DNase (MIST2) question stays at live #816 and is not re-carded here
7353: POSSIBLE (benefit) — two small double-blind placebo trials (n=42 with delayed gastric emptying; n=30) found levosulpiride improved dyspeptic symptoms and accelerated gastric emptying versus placebo, and a 140-patient pilot found it at least as effective as cisapride; the base is small, old and short, the drug is a dopamine D2 antagonist (hyperprolactinaemia and extrapyramidal effects) and it is not licensed in the US/UK
7354: MAYBE (weak evidence) — the largest placebo-controlled trial (566 patients evaluated) and the overall meta-analysis of 13 trials (relative risk 0.999) found mosapride made no difference versus placebo; positive signals appear only in sensitivity subsets, and the 2021 and 2024 active-comparator trials have no placebo arm, so a small benefit cannot be excluded but is not demonstrated
7355: SPLIT — the large German placebo trial (n=223) found gabexate made no difference to mortality or complications and the 1995 meta-analysis of five trials found no mortality effect, but the same meta-analysis found fewer complications (relative odds ratio 0.69) and a small 52-patient severe-disease trial and an aprotinin-comparator trial read positively; an old programme split by severity, era and endpoint
7356: POSSIBLE (benefit) — two placebo-controlled randomised trials (n=135 randomised in India; n=181 single-centre in China) and a 2025 meta-analysis of seven studies suggest ulinastatin reduces death and new organ dysfunction in severe acute pancreatitis; the base is small and single-region, one trial's abstract gives no mortality counts, the meta-analysis mixes ulinastatin-alone and combination use, and a third named anchor (Yao & Li 2019) was refused at build as a results-free review protocol
7357: POSSIBLE (benefit) — base stated on the face: two open-label randomised trials from a single Mexican programme (n=70 and n=135) found large survival gains when metadoxine was added to prednisone or pentoxifylline in severe alcohol-associated hepatitis, and the verified metadoxine limb of a 2026 systematic review agrees (28-day mortality relative risk 0.47 versus corticosteroids alone); there is no replication outside that programme, and better abstinence on metadoxine confounds the drug claim
7358: SPLIT — the Orrego programme's long-term trial (310 compliant patients) found cumulative mortality 0.13 versus 0.25 with a relative hazards ratio of 0.38, but the severe-hepatitis trial (n=67) found the treatment made no difference and the Cochrane review (2005 version, the one version carded) pooling six trials and 710 patients found no significant effect on mortality, complications or histology; a historical programme with an unconfirmed signal, for a drug that itself carries a severe-hepatotoxicity warning
7359: SPLIT — transdermal nicotine was superior to placebo for induction of remission in the small pooled placebo trials (19 of 71 versus 9 of 70; relative odds ratio 2.56) but showed no advantage over standard therapy and caused far more adverse-event withdrawals (relative odds ratio 5.82), while nicotine enemas made no difference versus placebo (remission 27% versus 33%); an induction-only programme abandoned in practice
7360: POSSIBLE (benefit) — small 1980s trials with Ns printed on the face (60 randomised to enemas plus a 40-patient oral trial; 105 patients; 66 sulfasalazine-intolerant patients) show modest benefit, strongest on rectal endoscopy and in sulfasalazine-intolerant patients (improvement 35% versus 16% on placebo, rising to 50% at 3 g/day); olsalazine's dose-limiting secretory diarrhoea is the clinically decisive harm
7361: POSSIBLE (benefit) — balsalazide shows a dose-response (6.75 g/day significantly better than 2.25 g/day for induction; 3 g twice daily maintained remission in 77.5% versus 43.8% on low-dose balsalazide) and faster onset than mesalamine, BUT every mesalamine comparator is low-dose by modern standards (1.2–2.4 g/day, flagged on the face), there is no placebo arm, and 12-month remission in ABACUS was equal (58% both) — nothing here shows superiority over modern-dose mesalamine
7362: MAYBE (weak evidence) — failed programme, stamped plainly: ALPINE 2/3 (171 randomised) missed its primary fibrosis endpoint with no dose response (P=0.55) and aldafermin's development for MASH was discontinued; the phase 2 trial (n=78) significantly reduced liver fat but not fibrosis or MASH resolution, and the later compensated-cirrhosis trial (n=160) improved a fibrosis biomarker score (ELF −0.5 at 3 mg) in a separate population, which does not rescue the failed F2–F3 programme; LDL-cholesterol elevation is the FGF19 class effect
7363: POSSIBLE (benefit) — besifovir was noninferior to entecavir and to tenofovir for HBV DNA suppression in every comparative report, with consistently better-preserved bone mineral density and renal function and no detected resistance, but the whole programme is single-region (South Korea), the long-term phase 3 reads are open-label extensions, and carnitine depletion is a real offsetting harm; POSSIBLE rather than LIKELY because no non-Korean or independently replicated evidence exists
7364: LIKELY (no difference) — the only large sham-controlled trial found no efficacy for induction (remission 17% vs 11% on sham), the small sham-controlled maintenance trial was also non-significant, the 2010 systematic review found no significant benefit against sham across 10 RCTs, and the open-label trials' positive signals are secondary endpoints after missed primaries; the blinded evidence governs the stamp
7365: SPLIT — on exactly 2 randomised reports (phase 2, n=152; phase 3, n=201): the phase 2 trial significantly reduced nausea versus placebo at 4 weeks, but the phase 3 trial missed its prespecified primary endpoint (P=.741) and secondary endpoints, with positive findings only post hoc; per the row's builder condition the programme is presented as failed at phase 3 on the face, so no benefit stamp is proposed
7366: SPLIT — in JAK-inhibitor-naive myelofibrosis momelotinib met spleen-response noninferiority versus ruxolitinib but missed symptom-response noninferiority (28.4% vs 42.2%) while improving transfusion outcomes, and in ruxolitinib-pretreated disease it was not superior to best available therapy (89% continued ruxolitinib) for spleen response, with similar survival in both trials (PARTIAL shelf: MOMENTUM versus danazol stays homed at pack #4865, cross-pointed only)
7367: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme evidence (one trial, three reports): ponatinib significantly increased the molecular primary endpoint, MRD-negative complete remission (34.4% vs 16.7%), with comparable early safety, but event-free survival was immature and overall survival did not differ in the companion analysis, so the stamp rests on remission depth, not on a proven survival benefit
7368: LIKELY (benefit) — a single phase 3 trial (TOWER) showed significantly longer overall survival with blinatumomab than chemotherapy in relapsed/refractory adult B-ALL (median 7.7 vs 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.71, relative) with deeper remissions and better quality of life in companion reports of the same trial; LIKELY rather than stronger because the entire base is one trial and absolute survival remains short
7369: LIKELY (benefit) — a single phase 3 trial (E1910) showed significantly better overall survival when blinatumomab was added to consolidation in MRD-negative adult B-ALL (3-year survival 85% vs 68%; hazard ratio 0.41, relative), corroborated as the approval basis in the FDA summary; LIKELY rather than stronger because the base is one trial reported at an interim analysis in a selected deep-remission population, with more neuropsychiatric events on blinatumomab
7370: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm bases cap at POSSIBLE with the uncontrolled base stated: the single-arm ZUMA-3 trial produced complete remission or better in 71–73% of infused adults with relapsed/refractory B-ALL and median overall survival of 25.6 months at 3 years, echoed by a 189-patient real-world cohort, but no randomised comparator exists and grade 3-or-worse cytokine-release syndrome and neurotoxicity affected roughly a quarter to a third of patients
7371: LIKELY (benefit) — a single phase 3 trial (S1826) showed significantly better progression-free survival with nivolumab-AVD than with the active standard brentuximab vedotin-AVD (2-year 92% vs 83%; hazard ratio 0.45, relative), with consistent subset reports in older patients (where overall survival and non-relapse mortality also favoured nivolumab-AVD) and adolescents, and a better tolerability profile; whole-population overall survival was immature, which is stated on the face
7372: LIKELY (benefit) — a single phase 3 trial (PEACE-3) showed improved radiographic progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.69, relative) and, at the final analysis, improved overall survival (median 38.2 vs 32.6 months; hazard ratio 0.76, relative; P=.0096) for enzalutamide plus radium-223 versus enzalutamide alone in first-line bone-metastatic mCRPC, conditional on the mandatory bone-protecting-agent co-treatment that is part of the tested intervention and is printed on the face, with more grade 3-or-worse toxicity and fractures as the costs
7373: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports of one trial (CAPItello-281): the primary report showed a significant radiographic-PFS benefit for capivasertib plus abiraterone in PTEN-deficient mHSPC (33.2 vs 25.7 months; relative hazard ratio 0.81) but overall survival was not significant at that confirmatory read (relative hazard ratio 0.90); the second report is an ad hoc descriptive update only (relative hazard ratio 0.82, nominal), and toxicity is frequent (diarrhoea 51.9%, hyperglycaemia 38.0%, rash 35.4%)
7374: LIKELY (benefit, progression-free survival) — PARTIAL, single programme (DUO-E, one trial in three reports): durvalumab maintenance hazard ratio 0.71 and durvalumab + olaparib 0.55 versus control (both relative), with the olaparib increment principally in pMMR disease (0.57 vs 0.77) and little added in dMMR disease (0.41 vs 0.42); overall survival was immature (about 28%) and not significant for durvalumab alone, so no survival claim is made
7375: LIKELY (benefit) — single programme (COLUMBUS, one trial in three reports): encorafenib + binimetinib prolonged progression-free survival versus vemurafenib (14.9 vs 7.3 months; relative hazard ratio 0.54) with durable long-term rates (7-year overall survival 27.4% vs 18.2%, absolute); qualified because the comparator is the dated first-generation vemurafenib benchmark and no head-to-head against dabrafenib + trametinib exists
7376: LIKELY (benefit, tumour response) — one randomised trial (ENLIVEN, 120 randomised): week-25 response 39% vs 0% on placebo, with durable responses in open-label follow-up (about 60%); qualified by mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity (enrolment stopped early for it; about 3% in pooled cohorts, reversible) and by a pain benefit that is modest and missed its primary definition
7377: SPLIT — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports: both zanidatamab arms beat trastuzumab + chemotherapy on progression-free survival (12.4 vs 8.1 months; relative hazard ratios 0.63 and 0.65), but only the tislelizumab-containing arm has a significant overall-survival read at this interim analysis (26.4 vs 19.2 months; relative hazard ratio 0.72), while zanidatamab + chemotherapy does not (relative hazard ratio 0.80, P=0.06); diarrhoea is the main added harm
7378: LIKELY (benefit, route and tolerability) — PARTIAL + FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports of one trial (PALOMA-3): subcutaneous amivantamab + lazertinib was pharmacokinetically noninferior to the intravenous route with similar response (30% vs 33%), far fewer infusion-related reactions (13% vs 66%) and far shorter administration (4.8 minutes vs 5 hours first dose); the overall-survival difference was exploratory only and is explicitly not claimed
7379: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports of one single-arm phase 2 trial (LUMINOSITY): responses in 28.6–29.2% of biomarker-selected patients (about 35% c-Met-high, about 23–24% c-Met-intermediate) with median duration about 7–8 months and neuropathy in about a third; a single-arm base has no comparator and can support no more than POSSIBLE, with the base stated
7380: SPLIT — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports of one trial (RATIONALE-301): tislelizumab met overall-survival noninferiority versus sorafenib (15.9 vs 14.1 months; relative hazard ratio 0.85) but did NOT meet superiority, while response (14.3% vs 5.4%), response durability (36.1 vs 11.0 months), tolerability (grade ≥3 treatment-related events 22.2% vs 53.4%) and quality of life favoured tislelizumab and median progression-free survival numerically favoured sorafenib (2.1 vs 3.4 months)
7381: POSSIBLE (benefit) — per class, from a 35-RCT synthesis with its primary trials carded: silver relative risk 0.78 (a 22% relative reduction, moderate certainty) with mixed primary trials (one significant, three not), DACC relative risk 0.49 on a thin, single-centre caesarean base that does not meet a ≥3-independent-trial class claim, and mupirocin not associated with benefit; no pooled 'antimicrobial dressings work' claim is made
7382: SPLIT — coffee sped bowel recovery in both gynaecological trials (flatus, defecation and food tolerance all significantly sooner; ileus 2.0% vs 14.9% laparoscopic) but caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee were both null in the one three-arm colorectal trial, while isolated caffeine capsules shortened time to first stool by 18 hours on a single endpoint in one small trial; no trial showed a shorter hospital stay, and whether caffeine is the active agent remains unresolved
7383: LIKELY (benefit) — small bites fascial closure reduces incisional hernia after elective midline laparotomy: STITCH showed 13% vs 21% hernia at 1 year with a 13-year cumulative incidence of 34% vs 49%, Millbourn and ESTOIH point the same way, and the 7-trial synthesis gives a relative risk of 0.46; the one null trial was a small factorial study in high-risk patients using a composite outcome
7384: SPLIT — oral glutamine reduced mucositis pain and duration in small chemotherapy and autologous bone-marrow-transplant trials, but the head-and-neck radiotherapy phase 3 trial was null and the pooled randomised estimate for mucositis incidence is a relative risk of 0.91 (95% CI 0.78 to 1.05); the answer differs by treatment setting
7385: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme (FLOOR-RISK): the only randomised evidence is the ChEETAh cluster trial (13,301 patients, seven LMICs), which reduced 30-day SSI from 18.9% to 16.0% (adjusted risk ratio 0.87) with essentially unchanged cost; the protocol and cost-effectiveness reports are labelled reports of that same programme, and the claim is confined to LMIC abdominal surgery
7386: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — carotid IMT reference intervals are established in four primary datasets across three ultrasound methods (echotracking percentiles in 4,234 healthy people; B-mode norms in Andean-Hispanic and UK populations; RF-ultrasound values in 3,053 Han Chinese adults), with age-, sex-, segment- and population-specific limits printed per dataset
7387: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — blood-pressure responses to maximal treadmill (FRIEND, 2,917 adults), submaximal treadmill (NHANES, 2,544 multiethnic participants), workload-indexed bicycle ergometry (3,839 healthy subjects with reference equations) and maximal bicycle exercise in athletes (1,876) are established per mode, with upper limits and percentiles printed per dataset
7388: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — DXA whole-body body-composition reference values are established in four adult population datasets (NHANES 1999-2004; LEAD 10,894 adults; Mexican cohort 9,518 subjects; Singapore Yishun 537 adults), carded per device with age-, sex- and ancestry-specific fat-mass, lean-mass and appendicular lean-mass indices
7389: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING — central (aortic) pressure and augmentation-index reference values exist in four primary datasets (tonometry/oscillometry profiles in 1,688 healthy subjects; Mobil-O-Graph references in 867 healthy adults; Arteriograph values in 1,009 Mexican adults; SphygmoCor values in 120 Omani adults), graded down because every value is device- and site-specific and the healthy denominators are modest
7290: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — a failed programme: the three-trial long-term programme (1,200 patients) failed every primary ascites endpoint, did not reduce hepatic encephalopathy, and showed higher mortality on satavaptan in one trial (hazard ratio 1.47); short-term weight and sodium effects never converted into long-term ascites control, and the drug was never marketed
7291: POSSIBLE (benefit) — a Japanese short-term programme: dose-dependent reductions in body weight and ascites volume over 7 days in two double-blind studies (participant counts and numeric effects not documented in their records) and a greater 7-day weight loss than added furosemide in one small open-label randomised study (56 patients; −3.21 vs −1.75 kg); no decompensation, transplant or survival outcomes tested
7292: POSSIBLE (benefit) — for transient improvement only: the one large crossover trial (527 patients) found neurological improvement in 17.5%/14.7% versus 3.8%/2.7% on placebo, the rest of the base is small and old (the next carded trial is 14 patients, 18 episodes), and the Cochrane review (867 participants) found an encephalopathy benefit but no mortality effect, on low-quality evidence
7293: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — failed programme: the phase 3 trial (n=290) found no effect on new organ failure (57% vs 58% developed organ failure) and no significant mortality difference, superseding two small early trials (n=83, n=50) that improved organ-failure scores only; lexipafant was never licensed
7294: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm, uncontrolled base stated: pivotal trial n=28 (response at 24 h in 28/28; bleed control 24/28) plus US (n=53) and EU (n=50) post-authorisation cohorts with 80.3% and 37/50 bleeds resolved; the defining harm is anti-porcine-FVIII inhibitors (8.0% in the US cohort). REBUILD: the at-floor cohort base slate 10 missed. The Japanese n=5 report is excluded, below floor
7295: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports, both single-arm with the uncontrolled base stated: myelofibrosis phase 1/2 (n=89; spleen-volume reduction in 23/35 with week-24 data) and essential thrombocythemia phase 2 (n=73; platelet response 49/64 evaluable, 77%); slices labelled separately and never pooled; no third report exists
7296: LIKELY (benefit) — phase 3 head-to-head trial (n=338): divarasib vs sotorasib/adagrasib control gave median PFS 9.8 vs 5.7 months (HR 0.58, relative) and median OS 17.7 vs 12.0 months (HR 0.56, relative), response 58.4% vs 32.3%, with fewer grade 3–4 treatment-related events; the control split (156 sotorasib, 15 adagrasib) makes this a class verdict, not a separately powered adagrasib comparison; phase 1 slices are single-arm
7297: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm base stated (Lung02 randomised dose, not treatment): confirmed response 50.0% at the licensed 5.4 mg/kg dose vs 56.0% at 6.4 mg/kg, while adjudicated drug-related ILD was 14.9% vs 32.0% (Lung02 final analysis) and 26% with 2 deaths at 6.4 mg/kg in Lung01 — the lower dose carries roughly half the ILD for a similar response rate
7298: SPLIT — randomised TROPION-Lung01 (n=604): PFS improved vs docetaxel (4.4 vs 3.7 months; HR 0.75, relative) but OS was null (HR 0.94, not significant), the benefit was driven by nonsquamous histology (HR 0.63, relative) and squamous disease numerically favoured docetaxel (HR 1.41, relative); single-arm TROPION-Lung05 response was 35.8% in genomically selected disease. Stomatitis and ILD are the priced harms
7299: LIKELY (benefit) — three distinct randomised slices, never pooled: HARMONi-2 PFS 11.1 vs 5.8 months vs pembrolizumab (HR 0.51, relative; OS immature); HARMONi-6 PFS 11.1 vs 6.9 months vs tislelizumab + chemotherapy (HR 0.60, relative); post-TKI HARMONi-A OS 16.8 vs 14.1 months (HR 0.74, relative) with the global HARMONi showing PFS benefit (HR 0.52, relative) but non-significant OS (HR 0.79). All but the global trial were run in China; grade ≥3 toxicity is consistently higher on ivonescimab
7300: POSSIBLE (benefit) — PARTIAL, single-programme (one trial, MARIPOSA-2 n=657, multiple reports): amivantamab–chemotherapy median PFS 6.3 months and amivantamab–lazertinib–chemotherapy 8.3 months vs 4.2 months on chemotherapy (HR 0.48 and 0.44, relative), response 64%/63% vs 36%; the lazertinib arm required a mid-trial regimen change for haematologic toxicity. Post-osimertinib question only; first-line MARIPOSA is pack #7239, cross-pointed in prose
7301: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme (one trial, FURLONG n=358, three reports): furmonertinib vs gefitinib median PFS 20.8 vs 11.1 months (HR 0.44, relative), CNS PFS 20.8 vs 9.8 months (HR 0.40, relative), grade ≥3 treatment-related events 11% vs 18%. Comparator is first-generation gefitinib, not osimertinib; furmonertinib is approved in China only, not FDA/EMA-approved
7302: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme (one trial, AENEAS n=429, two reports; plus a small n=33 real-world cohort carded as context only, not an AENEAS report): aumolertinib vs gefitinib median PFS 19.3 vs 9.9 months (HR 0.46, relative), response 73.8% vs 72.1% with duration 18.1 vs 8.3 months, CNS PFS 29.0 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.31, relative). Comparator is first-generation gefitinib, not osimertinib; aumolertinib is approved in China only, not FDA/EMA-approved
7303: LIKELY (benefit) — on a single phase 3 programme (TROPiCS-02, 543 randomised): sacituzumab govitecan improved median PFS (5.5 vs 4.0 months; HR 0.66, a relative measure) and final median overall survival (14.4 vs 11.2 months; HR 0.79, relative) versus physician's-choice single-agent chemotherapy in heavily pretreated HR+/HER2− metastatic breast cancer, at the cost of more grade ≥3 neutropenia (51% vs 38%) and diarrhoea (9% vs 1%); the small Japanese cohort did not meet its response endpoint and is not confirmatory
7304: LIKELY (benefit) — on a single phase 3 trial (ASC4FIRST, 405 randomised): asciminib gave a higher week-48 major molecular response than investigator-selected TKIs overall (67.7% vs 49.0%, absolute rates), driven by the imatinib stratum (69.3% vs 40.2%); against second-generation TKIs the difference was smaller and not significant (66.0% vs 57.8%), and grade ≥3 events and discontinuations were fewer on asciminib — a molecular-surrogate benefit, with no survival advantage shown
7305: LIKELY (benefit) — on a single phase 3 trial (IMROZ, 446 randomised): adding isatuximab to VRd in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed myeloma gave estimated 60-month PFS of 63.2% vs 45.2% (HR 0.60, a relative measure) with deeper responses (MRD-negative complete response 55.5% vs 40.9%) and similar serious-event and discontinuation rates, the benefit holding in frail and non-frail subgroups; no overall-survival result is reported in the carded records
7306: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, on a single phase 3 trial (AQUILA, 390 randomised) with one small subgroup report: daratumumab monotherapy delayed progression to active myeloma or death versus active monitoring (HR 0.49, a relative measure; 5-year PFS 63.1% vs 40.8%, absolute) with 5-year survival 93.0% vs 86.9%, but about 59% of monitored patients had not progressed at 5 years, so the stamp stays at POSSIBLE until a second report exists; the benefit is delayed progression, not prevention
7307: SPLIT — on a single phase 3 trial (PSMAfore, 468 randomised): ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 prolonged radiographic PFS versus ARPI change in taxane-naïve mCRPC (updated median 11.60 vs 5.59 months; HR 0.49, a relative measure) and delayed quality-of-life, pain and skeletal-event worsening, but the final intention-to-treat overall-survival analysis was null (median 24.48 vs 23.13 months; HR 0.91; P=0.20) with 60.3% crossover — the crossover-adjusted HR 0.59 is model-based and does not displace the ITT result
7308: LIKELY (benefit) — on a single phase 3 trial (ARANOTE, 669 randomised): darolutamide plus ADT without docetaxel improved radiological progression-free survival versus ADT alone (HR 0.54, a relative measure), consistently across disease-volume and risk subgroups, with delayed pain progression and less fatigue than placebo; overall survival was not significant at the primary cutoff (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.59 to 1.12) and no survival claim is made
7309: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on four small randomised trials, each of a named programme: semi-occluded vocal-tract therapy plus vocal hygiene beat vocal hygiene alone (n=34), stretch-and-flow beat vocal hygiene alone (N not documented in the record), EMG biofeedback added muscle-activity but not voice benefit over placebo biofeedback (n=22), and flow-resistant-tube therapy was noninferior to Vocal Function Exercises (n=20); a 2008 systematic review supports combined therapy versus no intervention but warns true effects are probably smaller — weak comparators and small samples throughout
7310: SPLIT — by dressing class and endpoint: hydrogel is unsupported by a Cochrane review (2 trials, 162 participants; possibly slower healing than alginate/gauze, low certainty); povidone-iodine foam epithelialised fastest in one 106-patient RCT and a hydrocolloid and a film beat a foam in a 73-site RCT, while polyurethane versus calcium alginate shows no healing or pain difference (comfort favours polyurethane, dressing-change burden favours alginate); no class differed on infection
7311: SPLIT — by backbone regimen: thalidomide improved delayed-phase complete response and no-nausea rates when added to older 5-HT3-antagonist ± dexamethasone backbones (two overlapping meta-analyses, delayed complete response 70.6% vs 50.4%, RR 1.53, a relative measure; one crossover RCT agreeing), but the single modern trial adding it to a four-drug olanzapine-containing backbone after failure of that backbone was null on its primary endpoint (no nausea 16% vs 21%); sedation, constipation and teratogenicity handling price any use
7312: SPLIT — by incision site and study design: for closed groin incisions in arterial surgery, RCT evidence supports incisional NPWT (7 RCTs, SSI OR 0.35, a relative measure; primary trials split — one significant, one null and underpowered); for closed laparotomy incisions the evidence is unsettled (a mixed-design meta-analysis found OR 0.25, relative, but the RCT-only meta-analysis found RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.30 to 1.03, not significant); three retracted syntheses in this literature were fenced and not carded
7313: SPLIT — closure time and cost consistently favour barbed suture in every synthesis and primary RCT carded, and pooled wound complications do not differ, but primary RCTs split on complications by layer: full-layer barbed closure raised incision complications to 19.7% in a 582-patient three-arm trial while capsule-only barbed closure (7.2%) matched traditional closure, and one TKA RCT found fewer complications with barbed suture (2 vs 11)
7314: MAYBE (weak evidence) — FLOOR-RISK base stated on the face: the Cochrane review found only one eligible RCT (857 minor-excision patients; infection 8.5% vs 8.8%, RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.48) and the carded primary RCTs total 444, 51 and 32 patients, with a 7-RCT meta-analysis (1,881 patients) finding no infection difference for showering on or before day 2; no increase in infection is shown anywhere, comfort and satisfaction favour early showering, but the intervals are too wide to settle the question
7331: LIKELY (benefit) — for short-term (12–24 week) HBV DNA suppression and ALT normalisation in three Korean placebo-controlled trials (median reductions about 4.3–5.1 vs 0.2–0.5 log10 copies/mL); single-region programme (Levovir, South Korea; never FDA-approved) whose development elsewhere was halted over myopathy — 3.9% on longer exposure, reversible — with resistance in 11% by 60 weeks
7332: POSSIBLE (benefit) — entecavir plus adefovir beat continuing lamivudine plus adefovir in one randomised rescue programme (virological response 29% vs 4% at 52 weeks; extension to 104 weeks and a concordant three-way comparison), on a small single-region base answering a historical-era question; one commissioned anchor (PMID 25587617) refused for an empty abstract record
7333: LIKELY (benefit) — lorundrostat's phase 3 programme (carded here as a PARTIAL slice of live shelf #743, which holds the phase 2 and class evidence) lowered systolic pressure beyond placebo in two distinct randomised trials: Launch-HTN (phase 3, n=1,083) by a placebo-adjusted 9.1 mm Hg in office pressure at week 6, and Advance-HTN (n=285; typed phase II in its PubMed record) by 7.9 mm Hg (stable dose) and 6.5 mm Hg (dose-adjustment) in 24-hour pressure at week 12; benefit is on the blood-pressure surrogate only — no outcomes trial exists — and hyperkalaemia, hyponatraemia and reduced kidney function were more frequent on lorundrostat. FLOOR-RISK base: exactly 2 reports / 2 trials, stated on the face
7334: LIKELY (benefit) — three placebo-controlled NEJM trials (a 32-patient preliminary dose-ranging trial, a 143-patient US initial-treatment trial and a 288-child trial) consistently showed lamivudine suppresses HBV DNA, normalises ALT and improves histology in chronic hepatitis B; the stamp is historical — lamivudine is a superseded first-line agent because YMDD resistance accumulates on continued therapy (the carded reports print no resistance rate, so none is claimed), and the advanced-liver-disease trial is carded in the live library and cross-pointed, not re-carded here
7335: LIKELY (benefit) — two independent NEJM placebo-controlled trials (HBeAg-positive, n=515; HBeAg-negative, n=185) showed adefovir dipivoxil 10 mg improves liver histology (53% and 64% vs 25% and 33%), suppresses HBV DNA and normalises ALT at 48 weeks, and the HBeAg-negative programme's extension report (labelled lineage, not a third trial) showed benefit maintained to 144 weeks on continued therapy and lost on stopping; the stamp is historical — adefovir is superseded, with renal laboratory abnormalities at the 30 mg dose and resistance mutations in 5.9% by 144 weeks
7336: POSSIBLE (benefit) — telbivudine was superior to lamivudine on therapeutic response, HBV DNA suppression and resistance at 1 and 2 years, but the entire base is ONE programme (the single GLOBE trial and its reports, flagged on the face), the comparator is itself a superseded agent, grade 3/4 creatine-kinase elevations were more frequent on telbivudine (12.9% vs 4.1%), and telbivudine was withdrawn from the US market in 2016 with a myopathy/peripheral-neuropathy warning history; the renal report is a labelled secondary analysis and carries no independent weight
7337: WITHDRAWN (2010) — LIKELY (harm): sibutramine (Meridia/Reductil) was withdrawn after SCOUT (9,804 randomised high-risk patients) showed a higher primary cardiovascular outcome rate on sibutramine than placebo (11.4% vs 10.0%; hazard ratio 1.16, a relative measure), driven by nonfatal myocardial infarction (4.1% vs 3.2%) and nonfatal stroke (2.6% vs 1.9%) with no increase in death; its weight-loss efficacy (dose-related in Bray 1999; maintenance in STORM) is real but does not offset that harm, and SCOUT's harm figure belongs to its high-risk population, as printed on the face
7338: WITHDRAWN (1997) — POSSIBLE (benefit) for short-term weight loss only: fenfluramine and dexfenfluramine were withdrawn worldwide in 1997 after valvular-heart-disease and pulmonary-hypertension signals, and that withdrawal leads this stamp; the carded 1989–1998 evidence shows only modest short-term weight loss at obesity doses (dexfenfluramine 15 mg twice daily: 3.2 kg in 12 weeks and 6.9 kg in 15 weeks in active-comparator trials; the placebo-controlled ISIS interim report gives proportions, no kilogram figure), on an old, short-duration base. The low-dose epilepsy use at live shelf #992 is a different question and is not covered by this stamp
7339: WITHDRAWN (2000) — POSSIBLE (benefit) for glycaemic control: troglitazone (Rezulin) was withdrawn in 2000 for idiosyncratic hepatocellular injury including liver-failure deaths, and that withdrawal leads this stamp; the carded record shows real glycaemic efficacy (approximately 20% lower fasting and postprandial glucose at 400–600 mg in a 6-month placebo-controlled metabolic trial; HbA1c −0.4% to −1.8% at 600 mg in labelled open-label extensions, completers only), which is historical and does not rehabilitate the drug. The Diabetes Prevention Program onset report is fenced — not carded here — and any onset wording says 'delay', never 'prevent'
7390: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — normal 24-hour ambulatory values are established by population reference datasets (Belgian 95th percentiles 129/80 mmHg 24-hour, 137/88 daytime, 121/72 night-time; British means 115/72 awake and 97/58 asleep) and outcome-driven thresholds by IDACO (ambulatory hypertension 130/80, 140/85 and 120/70 mmHg), with the two kinds of number distinguished on the face and the row's third-dataset condition met by the verified Belgian dataset
7391: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING — brachial-ankle PWV reference ranges are established in three large East-Asian datasets (21,094 Chinese subjects; 7,881 healthy Japanese subjects; 974 healthy Northern Chinese subjects with decade upper limits), graded down because all datasets are East-Asian and single-device-family, so ranges beyond those populations are not established; the row's third-dataset condition was met at build
7392: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING — liver-panel reference intervals are supported by three primary datasets (Chinese multicentre intervals in 3,210 adults; CARDIA distributions in over 5,000 young US adults; metabolically verified ALT limits of 34 U/L in men and 22 U/L in women in 1,553 screened donors), graded down because the base is three datasets from different population-definition traditions and the ALT upper limit is definition-dependent
7393: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — four primary datasets (two very large indirect derivations, an over-60 verification study and an athlete verification study) agree the screening panel needs no sex partitioning and only minor age adjustment, while aPTT remains reagent/analyser-specific and no universal aPTT range is claimed
7394: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — four population datasets (Japanese, Thai, Iranian, US white) agree on a young-adult peak near 1.42 and an age decline that is faster in women, while absolute levels and cut-points are population- and software-specific, as printed on each card
7395: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — four population datasets (NHANES post-fortification n=9,196; Hordaland n=11,941; Canary Islands n=557; Turkish N=159 labelled small) agree on the sex/age gradient and on folate, smoking and coffee as the dominant acquired determinants; fortification-stratified, never merged
7396: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING — the B12 population distribution is settled (NHANES III, n=11,851) and a modern-assay interval is directly established (250.8–957.1 pg/mL (185–706 pmol/L)), but methylmalonic acid's need for age-specific intervals (NHANES 2011–2014) is a stated need not yet standard practice, and B12 intervals remain assay-generation-bound
7397: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — PARTIAL slice vs pack #7072 (diurnal rhythm home): the harmonised 2.5th–97.5th percentile interval of 264–916 ng/dL (9.2–31.8 nmol/L) in non-obese men 19–39 (Travison 2017, 9,054 men, CDC-harmonised assays) is the settled reference range; age decline and symptom thresholds are carded as distinct kinds of number
7398: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING — three normative datasets (bilateral charts n=137 fulfilling; unilateral pilot n=97 fulfilling; Turkish controls n=219, mean 137.8 L/min) establish PNIF's normative structure, but two print no numeric range in their records, values are technique-bound, and serial/home reproducibility is unquantified in the fetched records
7399: POSSIBLE (benefit) — three Japanese randomised trials show consistent HbA1c efficacy (non-inferior to daily alogliptin; superior to placebo in severe renal impairment/ESRD and as insulin add-on, differences −0.72% and −0.63%), but HbA1c is a surrogate, the evidence is single-region, and no cardiovascular-outcomes trial exists
7400: POSSIBLE (benefit) — mitiglinide matched nateglinide in two randomised trials (n=291, n=225; the one numerical advantage was non-significant, P = 0.06) and beat pioglitazone alone as add-on (−0.45%/−0.67% vs −0.02%), but the evidence is single-region (Japan/China), HbA1c is a surrogate, and no outcomes trial exists
7401: POSSIBLE (benefit) — PARTIAL vs live #72 (AMPLITUDE-O gated there, cross-point only): the glycaemic programme (2 publications, 4 phase 3 trials) shows superiority to placebo as monotherapy and non-inferiority to dulaglutide, but three trials were terminated early for sponsor funding, the drug was never marketed, and HbA1c is a surrogate endpoint
7402: SPLIT — PROSPECTIVE (n=876) showed only a non-significant trend to fewer events, PQRST (n=274 analysed) was null on femoral imaging, and FAST (n=246) was positive on carotid IMT with fewer cardiac events (2.4% vs 13.6% absolute); probucol lowers HDL cholesterol (≈24% relative) and was withdrawn from the US market in 1995, remaining in use chiefly in Japan
7403: SPLIT — the three abstracted 1970s reports split: Walker 1977 found a statistically significant mean weight loss of 1 lb/patient/week on mazindol and Enzi 1976 found greater, longer-maintained loss than controls, but Atkinson 1977 found no advantage of either mazindol preparation over placebo; two empty-abstract typed-RCT reports were refused as anchors
7404: LIKELY (benefit) — three placebo-controlled trials of diethylpropion/amfepramone (the same drug under two names) agree on weight loss at 6–12 months (−9.8% vs −3.2% of body weight; −7.7 vs −1.1 kg; −10.0 vs −3.1 kg), with dry mouth and insomnia the most frequent harms and no cardiovascular or psychiatric signal in the trial that measured them; the empty-abstract 1973 report was refused as an anchor
7405: LIKELY (benefit) — on the biochemical endpoint only: three randomised programme trials (n=74, 84, 83) each found conivaptan raised serum sodium by about 6–9 mEq/L vs about 1–3 mEq/L on placebo over 4–5 days; no trial measured mortality, falls or cognition, the oral formulation was investigational, and infusion-site reactions caused withdrawal in up to 15% at the higher intravenous dose
7406: LIKELY (benefit) — on exercise capacity and anginal symptoms only: three randomised crossover placebo-controlled trials (n=90, 533, 50) consistently improved work performance and exercise duration and reduced anginal attacks and sublingual nitrate use, maintained over 2–6 weeks; no outcomes trial exists, the agent is not FDA-approved, and hypotension was significantly more frequent on the 16 mg once-daily formulation
7407: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK base of exactly 2 publications / 3 component trials, stated on the face: the placebo-controlled phase 2 trial prolonged time to ST depression (172.1 vs 44.0 s at peak, P = 0.001) but not exercise duration significantly and not angina frequency, and the Japanese programme showed a significant dose–response on exercise measures; surrogate endpoints only, and intracoronary vasospastic/microvascular reports were not merged
7408: SPLIT — DISCONTINUED, never-marketed programme: omapatrilat lowered blood pressure more than enalapril (OCTAVE, n=25,302) and was non-inferior, not superior, on heart-failure outcomes (OVERTURE, n=5,770; hazard ratio 0.94), but angioedema occurred in 2.17% vs 0.68% — the risk that ended the programme; the single-dose haemodynamic report is mechanism support only
7409: POSSIBLE (benefit) — a small, old base (total randomised N under 90): prolactin normalised more often on quinagolide in two trials (8/11 vs 2/9 at 8 weeks, P < 0.002; 81% vs 70%) with milder, less persistent adverse reactions, while the third trial's counted long-term phase (n=12) found equivalence; its n=7 acute phase is sub-floor, labelled, and never load-bearing; quinagolide was never FDA-approved
7410: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on the surrogate endpoint of PTH suppression: one efficacy trial (n=138 haemodialysis) showed a 55% fall, target reached in 83%, and maintenance on drug vs return to baseline on placebo in a randomised withdrawal phase, with more hypercalcaemia on drug; the n=27 report is a dose-conversion study and the n=60 report is in children on peritoneal dialysis — neither is adult efficacy evidence, and no outcomes trial exists
7411: LIKELY (no difference) — single-region (Japan) base: maxacalcitol did not differ significantly from calcitriol on intact PTH over 12 months (n=91) or in crossover (267 vs 343 pg/mL, P = 0.11; dose ratio 5.5:1; n=31), and target achievement vs paricalcitol was 30.5% vs 27.7% (n=255); serum calcium was higher on maxacalcitol during early treatment only, PTH is a surrogate, and no outcomes trial exists
7412: LIKELY (benefit) — on the surrogate lipid endpoint in a pre-statin-era base: the load-bearing dose-ranging trial (n=152) found relative LDL reductions of 16.3%, 22.8% and 27.2% at 5, 10 and 15 g/day vs 2.7% on placebo (P < 0.001), supported by the n=65 comparison (total cholesterol 333 to 266 mg/dL); the n=27 single-blind report is labelled and never load-bearing, no outcomes trial exists, and triglyceride rise is the harm-side signal
7413: POSSIBLE (benefit) — three randomised placebo-controlled trials (n=120, n=120, n=60) in distinct acute-heart-failure populations consistently improved haemodynamic and echocardiographic surrogates over 6-24 hours (wedge pressure, E/e', systolic blood pressure), but no trial tested mortality, hospitalisation or symptoms, dyspnoea and NT-proBNP did not separate from placebo, and istaroxime is investigational and unapproved; the 2025 prolonged-infusion report is programme support, not a fourth trial
7414: LIKELY (benefit) — a Cochrane pool of 18 trials (6,343 participants) plus three adult primaries show ciclesonide improves lung function and control versus placebo over 8-12 weeks and reduces prednisone dose by 47-63% in severe steroid-dependent asthma; no exacerbation, mortality or long-term safety evidence exists
7415: SPLIT — pranlukast improved peak flow and FEV1 versus placebo (4 weeks, 1997) and matched a doubled beclomethasone dose as an add-on in two protocols of 41 and 39 patients, but in the only step-down trial (n=40) switching from low-dose inhaled steroid to pranlukast left fewer patients controlled (72.2% vs 90%) with FeNO rising; small, old, short evidence throughout, and the drug is not licensed in the US/UK
7416: LIKELY (benefit) — for 24-hour bronchodilation only: a 487-patient placebo-controlled trial showed significant peak-flow (10 and 20 mg) and FEV1 (20 mg) benefit over 4 weeks, supported by a 29-patient dosing-time crossover and an elderly dose-finding study; a pre-LABA-era oral beta-agonist with dose-related tremor and palpitations, never licensed in the US, and no exacerbation or outcome evidence
7417: SPLIT — inhaled flunisolide added to salbutamol in the ED improved airflow at 90-180 minutes (n=94), was indistinguishable from continued systemic steroids after IV treatment in a 40-patient inpatient trial too small to prove equivalence, and gave no benefit with more nocturnal wheezing after ED discharge (n=104, 28% lost to follow-up)
7418: LIKELY (no difference) — the Cochrane 2012 pool of 17 trials found no significant added bronchodilation or reduction in admission when IV aminophylline was added to inhaled beta-2 agonists, with significantly more vomiting and palpitations/arrhythmias; the two named primaries are small old trials (n=21 positive, n=59 negative) that do not outweigh the pool
7419: LIKELY (no difference) — a 302-patient double-blind multicentre trial found no benefit on mortality, complications, pain, surgery or stay, and the agent-specific meta-analysis (11 trials, 720 participants) found non-significant relative risks for mortality (0.88) and complications (1.08); the two small positive reports carry design flags (inconsistent design wording with 50 of 60 analysed; sequential allocation, n=43) and do not outweigh them
7420: SPLIT — induction limb: mesalamine does not induce remission in active Crohn's disease (Cochrane, 20 studies: 4 g/day not superior to placebo; the Pentasa meta-analysis's net CDAI gain is -18 points, of unclear clinical significance); postoperative limb: symptomatic recurrence reduced in one trial (31% vs 41%, n=163) and clinical recurrence intermediate in another (58% vs 77% on placebo, n=131) with endoscopic recurrence identical to placebo — the two limbs are labelled and never pooled
7421: POSSIBLE (benefit) — induction only, at 800 mg twice daily: two multicentre placebo-controlled trials (n=83, remission 52% vs 33%, not significant overall; n=402 for the extended-intestinal-release formulation, 62% vs 43%, P=0.005), with no dose-response; the 2014 maintenance report's implausibly complete result (100% remission at 12 weeks) is flagged on the face and does not carry the shelf
7422: POSSIBLE (benefit) — two small Japanese placebo-controlled trials (n=63, n=62) show more clinical response and mucosal healing on oral tacrolimus at 2 weeks, and the Cochrane pool (5 RCTs, 347 participants) agrees at low certainty for remission and improvement; remission in the hospitalised trial was 9.4% vs 0.0% and not significant, horizons are 2 weeks, and trough monitoring plus nephrotoxicity, tremor and glucose effects are part of the intervention
7423: MAYBE (weak evidence) — no placebo-controlled trial carded showed a significant benefit of cisapride on global dyspepsia outcomes (therapeutic gain 0.1% in the largest trial), and the drug was withdrawn/restricted for QT prolongation and torsades risk; this shelf records a negative-to-mixed programme, not a treatment option
7424: LIKELY (benefit) — maintenance of healing was clearly superior to placebo in two randomised trials (87%/82% and 75%/83% vs 26% and 27% at 6 months by life-table) and healing was non-inferior to lansoprazole across two trials in one publication (92–95% vs 86–92% at week 8); three publications covering four trials, counted on the STRATOS convention stated on the face
7425: SPLIT — liver biochemistry consistently improved (alkaline phosphatase 281→112 IU/L over 4 years in one trial) but the Cochrane pool of 11 trials (716 patients) found no significant effect on deaths (relative risk 1.21) or death/transplantation, no trial showed a histology benefit, and UDCA was superior head-to-head; a pre-UDCA-era programme
7426: POSSIBLE (harm) — no benefit was shown (PUMPS, 265 patients over a median 7.6 years, was stopped for futility), while the mortality record points the wrong way: a 2.9-fold higher death/transplant rate in the long-term placebo-controlled trial (95% CI 0.85 to 10.25), a significant mortality increase in the 2005 Cochrane version, and a pooled relative risk of 1.32 (not significant) in the 2010 update; the mortality concern leads
7427: LIKELY (harm) — two NEJM randomised trials showed no survival, symptom or histology benefit, major side effects forced permanent discontinuation in 22% of patients in one and occurred in 31% in the other, and the Cochrane pool (7 trials, 706 patients) found adverse events significantly increased (relative risk 3.11) with mortality tending to increase; a failed, toxic programme, not a treatment option
7428: SPLIT — in the single SOCA programme (2 trials, 4 reports, labelled as such), foscarnet was associated with longer survival than ganciclovir in the pre-HAART FGCRT (deaths 34% vs 51%; relative risk 1.79) while retinitis control and vision were equivalent and tolerability favoured ganciclovir (46% of foscarnet patients switched, mostly for toxicity); for relapsed retinitis, combination therapy controlled retinitis longest with no mortality difference. The pre-HAART era flag is load-bearing: this record must not be carried into modern practice
7429: POSSIBLE (benefit) — brivudine was equivalent to famciclovir in the 2,027-patient double-blind trial and favoured for postherpetic neuralgia in a seven-trial meta-analysis, but its headline PHN advantage over aciclovir (32.7% vs 43.5%) comes from a survey follow-up of two trials, labelled as such, and its potentially lethal interaction with fluoropyrimidines (5-fluorouracil and prodrugs) is flagged on the face; licensed in parts of Europe, not in the US
7430: LIKELY (benefit) — two large phase 3 trials in two labelled limbs both showed progression-free and overall survival benefits: ASPIRE (KRd vs Rd: median PFS 26.3 vs 17.6 months, HR 0.69 relative; median OS 48.3 vs 40.4 months, HR 0.79 relative) and ENDEAVOR (Kd vs Vd: median PFS 18.7 vs 9.4 months, HR 0.53 relative; interim median OS 47.6 vs 40.0 months, HR 0.791 relative), priced in cardiac failure, hypertension and renal harm
7431: LIKELY (benefit) — for progression-free survival in relapsed or refractory myeloma (PARTIAL beside first-line live shelf #844; only the relapsed/refractory slice is carded here): four phase 3 trials across four backbones all favoured adding daratumumab (hazard ratios 0.37, 0.39, 0.63 and 0.63, relative measures printed with absolutes), and POLLUX's final analysis showed an overall-survival benefit (median 67.6 vs 51.8 months; HR 0.73, relative); priced in infusion-related reactions and neutropenia
7432: SPLIT — progression-free survival improved in both trials (MM-003: median 4.0 vs 1.9 months, HR 0.48 relative, against high-dose dexamethasone alone in doubly refractory disease; OPTIMISMM: median 11.20 vs 7.10 months, HR 0.61 relative) but OPTIMISMM's final overall survival was null unadjusted (median 35.6 vs 31.6 months; HR 0.94, not significant, P=.571), flagged on the face, with the adjusted HR 0.76 labelled a sensitivity analysis only; priced in neutropenia and infection
7433: SPLIT — ixazomib plus lenalidomide–dexamethasone significantly prolonged progression-free survival in TOURMALINE-MM1 (hazard ratio 0.74, relative) but did NOT significantly prolong overall survival at the final 85-month analysis (53.6 vs 51.6 months; hazard ratio 0.939, P=.495); single-trial base, three reports of one trial
7434: SPLIT — ixazomib maintenance significantly prolonged progression-free survival in both TOURMALINE-MM3 (hazard ratio 0.72, relative) and TOURMALINE-MM4 (hazard ratio 0.659, relative), but final overall-survival analyses showed NO benefit in either trial (hazard ratios 1.025 and 1.090, both not significant)
7435: LIKELY (benefit) — elotuzumab plus an immunomodulatory backbone prolonged progression-free and overall survival in both randomised trials in relapsed/refractory myeloma: ELOQUENT-2 phase 3 (OS hazard ratio 0.82, relative) and ELOQUENT-3 randomised phase 2, n=117 (OS hazard ratio 0.59, relative); the negative frontline ELOQUENT-1 trial is cross-pointed in the balance, not carded here
7436: SPLIT — panobinostat plus bortezomib–dexamethasone significantly prolonged progression-free survival in PANORAMA-1 (hazard ratio 0.63, relative) but did NOT significantly prolong overall survival (hazard ratio 0.94, P=.54), with substantially more grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia and diarrhoea; PANORAMA-2 is single-arm support only
7437: SPLIT — WITHDRAWN product (US withdrawal 2021 after the OCEAN survival signal; EU authorisation later revoked): melflufen + dexamethasone beat pomalidomide + dexamethasone on progression-free survival in OCEAN (hazard ratio 0.79, relative) but overall survival numerically favoured pomalidomide (19.8 vs 25.0 months; hazard ratio 1.10, not significant), with grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia 63% vs 11%; HORIZON is single-arm support only
7438: SPLIT — first-line bosutinib beat imatinib on 12-month molecular response in BFORE at 400 mg (47.2% vs 36.9%) but BELA at 500 mg MISSED its primary cytogenetic endpoint (70% vs 68%, P=.601); BYOND is single-arm support in pretreated disease; diarrhoea and transaminase elevation are the pricing harms
7439: SPLIT (across the class) — azacitidine significantly prolonged overall survival in higher-risk MDS in AZA-001 (24.5 vs 15.0 months; hazard ratio 0.58, relative) with supportive response/transformation evidence from CALGB 9221, while decitabine improved response (17% vs 0%) without a demonstrated overall-survival benefit; the class must not be upgraded to a uniform survival claim
7440: LIKELY (benefit, on a pharmacodynamic endpoint) — in the single HERO trial, oral relugolix was superior to leuprolide for sustained castration through 48 weeks (96.7% vs 88.8%) with far faster onset and testosterone recovery; the cardiovascular-event difference (hazard ratio 0.46, relative) is an unpowered secondary analysis, not a proven cardiovascular benefit, and no cancer-outcome endpoint was tested
