7525: SPLIT — PCP prevention broadly similar across co-trimoxazole, dapsone-based regimens and aerosolised pentamidine, but pentamidine leaves toxoplasmosis uncovered (adjusted relative risk 1.81) and dapsone-pyrimethamine carries the heaviest toxicity discontinuations (42 vs 3); pre-HAART era flag on the face
7526: SPLIT — treatment limb: less effective than co-trimoxazole (non-response 20% vs 7%; deaths 11 vs 1) but fewer treatment-limiting adverse effects, mild-to-moderate disease only; prophylaxis-in-intolerance limb: similar to dapsone and aerosolised pentamidine at 1500 mg; limbs never pooled, pre-HAART era
7527: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single programme, labelled: immediate fomivirsen delayed CMV retinitis progression vs deferral (71 vs 13 days) in a 28-patient trial; dose schedules did not differ; pooled safety report is a programme report, not independent evidence; pre-HAART era, drug since withdrawn
7528: LIKELY (benefit) — adjuvant trastuzumab vs observation improved disease-free survival in HERA (HR 0.54 relative; absolute 2-year benefit 8.4 points) and overall survival at 2 and 11 years (HR 0.66 and 0.74, relative), with a concordant 39% relative death-rate reduction in the B-31/N9831 joint analysis; cardiotoxicity on the face; PARTIAL beside the duration shelf #760, vs-observation slice only
7529: LIKELY (benefit) — aromatase inhibitors improved disease-free survival versus tamoxifen in three trials across upfront and switch strategies (DFS hazard ratios 0.68–0.87, relative, with absolute benefits printed), with no demonstrated overall-survival advantage; harm trade (fractures/arthralgia vs endometrial cancer/thromboembolism) and the null ATAC combination arm on the face
7530: LIKELY (benefit) — one trial (MOSAIC, three labelled reports): adjuvant FOLFOX improved DFS (HR 0.77 relative) and overall survival (10-year HR 0.85 relative), driven by stage III (HR 0.80); stage II survival null (HR 1.00) on the face; neuropathy prices the gain
7531: POSSIBLE (benefit, confined to RAS wild-type tumours) — CRYSTAL's overall PFS effect was small (HR 0.85 relative) and overall survival null (HR 0.93); benefit across endpoints in fully RAS wild-type tumours and none in RAS-mutant tumours, with OPUS concordant; skin toxicity on the face
7532: LIKELY (benefit, for progression-free survival; no overall-survival benefit demonstrated) — six trials of gefitinib or erlotinib vs platinum chemotherapy in EGFR-mutant NSCLC consistently doubled median PFS (HRs 0.16–0.49, relative) with less severe toxicity, while survival was not significantly improved (NEJ002 P=.31; ENSURE HR 0.91); IPASS mutation-negative harm (HR 2.85) on the face
7533: LIKELY (benefit) — cisplatin–pemetrexed is non-inferior first-line with a histology interaction favouring pemetrexed in nonsquamous and gemcitabine in squamous disease (JMDB), and pemetrexed maintenance after induction prolonged overall survival in two randomised trials (JMEN HR 0.79; PARAMOUNT HR 0.78, relative measures with ~3-month absolute median gains), in non-progressors only
7534: LIKELY (benefit) in stage II–III resected NSCLC — adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy improved survival in IALT (5-year 44.5% vs 40.4%, HR 0.86) and ANITA (HR 0.80), with LACE's pooled HR 0.89 and 5.4-point absolute 5-year benefit; no benefit shown in stage IB and a harm trend in stage IA (HR 1.40), against ~1–2% toxic deaths (all hazard ratios are relative measures)
7535: LIKELY (benefit) — continuous lenalidomide–dexamethasone beat MPT in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed myeloma (FIRST final median OS 59.1 vs 49.1 months, HR 0.78) and adding bortezomib to Rd improved survival further (SWOG S0777 HR 0.709), two trials with their follow-up reports labelled as the same trials (hazard ratios are relative measures)
7536: LIKELY (benefit) — one trial, three labelled reports: VISTA showed bortezomib plus melphalan–prednisone prolonged time to progression (HR 0.48) and survival (updated HR 0.653, a 35% relative reduction in the risk of death; 3-year OS 68.5% vs 54.0%) versus melphalan–prednisone in transplant-ineligible myeloma, with peripheral neuropathy in 47% that plateaued at ~45 mg/m² and mostly reversed (hazard ratios are relative measures)
7537: LIKELY (benefit) — adjunctive levetiracetam reduced refractory partial seizures in three randomised trials with a dose gradient (≥50% responder rates 22.8–33.0% at 1,000 mg/day and 31.6–39.8% at 2,000–3,000 mg/day vs 10.4–10.8% on placebo), with modest harms; the monotherapy-conversion report is labelled responder-selected
7538: POSSIBLE (benefit) — adjunctive lamotrigine reduced refractory partial seizures in one parallel-group trial significant only at 500 mg/day (Matsuo, n=216), supported by two labelled crossover companions (Smith n=81; Schapel n=41, small and labelled); a real but modest effect at adequate dose
7539: LIKELY (benefit) — gabapentin reduced pain versus placebo in postherpetic neuralgia (two trials) and in painful diabetic neuropathy (one trial), labelled as separate limbs and never pooled; the absolute advantage is a modest ~1–2 points on an 11-point scale, bought with dizziness and somnolence in roughly a fifth to a quarter of patients
7540: LIKELY (benefit) — modafinil improved objective and subjective daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy in a crossover trial (MWT latency +40% at 200 mg, +54% at 400 mg vs placebo, relative measures) and a 283-patient parallel-group trial, and a labelled randomised-withdrawal trial showed the benefit is lost on stopping; nocturnal sleep was not disrupted
7541: LIKELY (benefit) — subcutaneous sumatriptan 6 mg relieved migraine at 1 hour (70% vs 22% mild/none; 49% vs 9% complete relief) and oral sumatriptan relieved it at 2 hours (67% at 100 mg vs 27% on placebo), with a flat oral dose–response above 100 mg against rising adverse events; the Ferrari triptan meta-analysis is carded as a labelled companion
7542: LIKELY (predictive) — NEWS/NEWS2 showed good discrimination for death, cardiac arrest or unanticipated ICU admission within 24 hours (AUROCs 0.72–0.89; 0.91 for 1-day mortality in the independent Finnish cohort), best or joint-best in 120 of 123 diagnostic groups and undiminished in COVID-19; this is predictive performance only — no evidence here that using the score improves outcomes — and three of four reports share the Smith-group database lineage, labelled
7543: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — field-dependent: ARISCAT discriminated excellently at derivation (AUROC 0.88–0.90), held up in emergency abdominal surgery (AUC 0.83, absolute risk under-predicted), performed poorly in lung resection (c-index 0.60, as did all comparators), and pools at a summary c-statistic of 0.76 across cohorts; a prognostic-accuracy stamp, not a treatment stamp
7544: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — modest and time-dependent: ROX AUROC rose from 0.679 (2 h) to 0.759 (12 h) at derivation in pneumonia with time-point-specific cut-offs (≥4.88 success; <2.85 / <3.47 / <3.85 failure), but COVID-19 validations found weak 2-hour discrimination (0.57 in Japan; 0.612 in Thai EDs, below the plain SpO2/FiO2 ratio's 0.651); a prognostic-accuracy stamp, not a treatment stamp
7548: POSSIBLE (benefit) — PARTIAL + FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports: ACHIEVE-1 (HbA1c −0.83 to −1.07 percentage points vs placebo) and ACHIEVE-2 (−0.42 to −0.75 vs dapagliflozin, non-inferiority exceeded) show glycaemic benefit at 40 weeks on a surrogate endpoint, with GI events in 46–54% and discontinuation in 15–20% in the active-comparator trial; the #1091 fence (ACHIEVE-3/-5/-4, gated, never carded) and the deliberate slate-16 adjudication rowing this slice are printed on the face; no outcomes claim
7549: SPLIT — PARTIAL (glycaemic HARMONY slice beside live #72): albiglutide beat placebo (HbA1c −0.8 percentage points, HARMONY 1) and sitagliptin in renal impairment (−0.83% vs −0.52%), with 3-year durability in the pooled programme, but FAILED non-inferiority against liraglutide in HARMONY 7 (difference 0.21%, non-inferiority P = 0.0846) — and the agent was withdrawn from the market in 2018; the cardiovascular-outcomes result is homed at live #72
7550: POSSIBLE (benefit, glycaemic) — omarigliptin was non-inferior to daily sitagliptin (HbA1c −0.47% vs −0.43%) and modestly beat placebo (−0.39 percentage points) on a surrogate endpoint, with a neutral cardiovascular estimate (MACE HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.29) from a safety study TERMINATED EARLY on truncated follow-up; approved in Japan only, never marketed in the US — both facts on the face
7551: LIKELY (benefit on fractures, with development-ending harm) — LOFT showed odanacatib reduced vertebral (3.7% vs 7.8%, HR 0.46), hip (0.8% vs 1.6%, HR 0.53) and non-vertebral fractures, but increased stroke (1.7% vs 1.3%, HR 1.32; HR 1.37 with extension data), on which the sponsor abandoned development; the agent was never marketed, the stroke signal leads the balance, and the supporting trials are BMD (surrogate) trials only
7552: SPLIT — bococizumab lowered LDL by 54–56% in relative terms, but antidrug antibodies attenuated the effect's magnitude and durability, and the SPIRE outcomes trials were discordant (HR 0.99 in the lower-risk trial vs 0.79 in the higher-risk trial; combined HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.02, P = 0.08) on follow-up truncated by an early stop; the discontinued, never-marketed programme's immunogenicity leads the balance
7553: LIKELY (benefit) — three concordant Chinese phase 3 trials show large LDL-cholesterol reductions versus placebo (−57% to −65% relative); surrogate endpoint only, no cardiovascular-outcomes data, and the entire evidence base is single-region (China), where the drug is approved but not FDA/EMA-approved
7554: SPLIT — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 results reports: a 60-patient phase 2 trial found albuminuria lower on verinurad + febuxostat (−49.3% relative at week 24), but the 861-patient SAPPHIRE trial found no albuminuria reduction at any dose versus allopurinol alone or placebo, so the larger negative trial governs and no albuminuria benefit is established
7555: LIKELY (no benefit) — a single programme of four trials in which the only positive trial was the experimental human challenge study in healthy adults, while all three patient trials (HCT upper respiratory, HCT lower respiratory, and lung transplant recipients) missed their primary endpoints with no clinical benefit; presatovir was never marketed
7556: SPLIT — of the two concurrent phase 3 trials of inhaled liposomal ciprofloxacin (ARD-3150), ORBIT-4 prolonged time to first exacerbation (hazard ratio 0.72) while ORBIT-3 was flatly null (hazard ratio 0.99) and the pooled estimate was non-significant; the phase 2 trial showed only a sputum bacterial-density effect in 42 patients
7557: SPLIT — the largest trial (171 patients) found biofeedback no better than standard care with advice (53% vs 54% improved), while a 108-patient trial found biofeedback plus exercises superior to exercises alone after a conservative run-in (adequate relief 76% vs 41%); regimen and home-vs-office limbs showed no differences, so structured conservative therapy is supported but biofeedback's added value over standard care is unproven
7558: LIKELY (no benefit) — the programme's large double-blind trial (JAPAN-PD, 224 randomised) missed both coprimary endpoints for daikenchuto TJ-100 (Tsumura) after pancreaticoduodenectomy (ileus 33.7% vs 36.9%), and the smaller limbs show only transit/stool/gas signals against no treatment or an active comparator, with no ileus, complication or stay benefit in any trial
7559: SPLIT — the largest trial of rikkunshito (TJ-43) in functional dyspepsia missed its global-response primary endpoint (33.6% vs 23.8%, P=0.09), while the DREAM trial was positive (P=.019) only in patients still symptomatic after a placebo run-in; the Belgian mechanistic and domperidone-comparator limbs are small and never load-bearing
7560: POSSIBLE (benefit) — in adults, racecadotril reduced day-1 stool weight versus placebo in a single 70-patient trial and matched loperamide on diarrhoea duration in larger comparisons (55.0 hours in both groups, n=945) with significantly less rebound constipation; equivalence with loperamide, not superiority, is what the base shows
7561: LIKELY (no benefit) — the striking 1988 single-centre survival result (n=100) was not reproduced by the 549-patient VA trial in advanced alcoholic cirrhosis (mortality 49% vs 45%) or the HBV trial (n=100), and the Cochrane pool of 15 trials found mortality relative risk 1.00 with adverse events significantly increased (relative risk 4.35)
7562: MAYBE (weak evidence) — based on a very small total N = 135 across 4 trials: only the 55-patient US trial showed a between-group histological benefit (NAS fall ≥2 points in 38.5% vs 13.8%), while the three smaller trials (n=30, 30, 20) showed within-arm or surrogate changes without significant between-group separation
7563: POSSIBLE (benefit) — based on a very small N = 45: FLOOR-RISK, exactly 3 crossover reports (45 adults, 1988–1991, limbs ≤14 days) all favoured rifampicin for short-term cholestatic itch relief versus placebo or phenobarbitone; the n=9 limb is sub-floor and never load-bearing; harms (anaemia/renal-failure withdrawal, hepatitis risk, enzyme induction) are on the face
7564: SPLIT — gatifloxacin matched chloramphenicol, azithromycin and ofloxacin on treatment failure and beat cefixime (early-stopped trial), but failed culture-confirmed patients against ceftriaxone (26% vs 7%) once high-level fluoroquinolone resistance emerged; nalidixic-acid-resistance-era results that do not transfer to XDR settings, and the drug was withdrawn in many markets over dysglycaemia
7565: POSSIBLE (benefit) — one Lao phase 2 programme (3 publications / 4 trials, labelled): tribendimidine cured ~94% with 99.9% egg reduction and fewer adverse events than praziquantel, but non-inferiority on cure was NOT shown (−3.8 points; lower limit −7.1 vs −3 margin); parasitological endpoints only, no phase 3
7566: LIKELY (no benefit) — PARTIAL vs pack #7009 (carding only whether to aspirate at all): three small trials (n=39, 39, 57) found metronidazole alone sufficient in uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess, with at most faster tenderness relief in the first 3 days in one trial; the Cochrane synthesis could neither support nor refute aspiration
7567: LIKELY (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports (SHARP n=602 and Asia-Pacific n=226, both re-verified this session): sorafenib prolonged median overall survival by ~2–3 months in advanced HCC (hazard ratios 0.69 and 0.68, relative), with no significant delay in symptomatic progression in SHARP and hand–foot skin reaction, diarrhoea and weight loss as the pricing harms
7568: SPLIT — by window (never pooled): alteplase benefits acute ischaemic stroke within 3 hours (NINDS, two-part design labelled) and, more modestly, at 3–4.5 hours (ECASS III), but IST-3's primary endpoint up to 6 hours in a wider, older population was not significant, with symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage of ~2–7% pricing every window
7569: LIKELY (benefit) — one trial, three labelled reports (CLL8, 817 randomised): rituximab added to fludarabine–cyclophosphamide improved progression-free survival (3-year 65% vs 45%; long-term median 56.8 vs 32.9 months) and overall survival in fit first-line CLL, with benefit absent in del(17p) and more neutropenia as the pricing harm
7570: SPLIT — bevacizumab added to paclitaxel–carboplatin prolonged overall survival in E4599 (12.3 vs 10.3 months) with 15 treatment-related deaths including 5 pulmonary haemorrhages, while on a cisplatin–gemcitabine backbone (AVAiL) it improved progression-free survival only, with overall survival not significantly increased (hazard ratios 0.93 and 1.03)
7571: LIKELY (benefit) — one trial, three labelled reports (BR.21, 731 randomised): erlotinib prolonged survival in pretreated, biomarker-unselected NSCLC (median 6.7 vs 4.7 months; hazard ratio 0.70, relative) and delayed symptom deterioration, with a non-significant overall-survival contrast and higher toxicity in the elderly subgroup on the face
7572: LIKELY (benefit) — one trial, three labelled reports (MA.17, 5,187 enrolled; stopped early at the first interim analysis): letrozole after five years of tamoxifen improved disease-free survival (updated hazard ratio 0.58, relative), with overall survival null overall and improved only in the node-positive subgroup (hazard ratio 0.61), and more osteoporosis diagnoses as a pricing harm
7573: LIKELY (benefit for recurrence-free survival; no overall-survival benefit shown) — one double-blind randomised trial (Z9001, n=713) with a large recurrence-free-survival effect (98% versus 83% at 1 year; hazard ratio 0.35, relative) sustained at long-term follow-up (hazard ratio 0.6, relative), on a labelled single-trial / three-report base
7574: LIKELY (benefit) — two randomised trials in complementary age bands (median overall survival 51.6 versus 33.2 months aged 65–75; 44.0 versus 29.1 months over 75) supported by a six-trial individual-patient-data meta-analysis (hazard ratio 0.83, relative; 6.6-month median gain), with peripheral neuropathy as the pricing harm
7575: LIKELY (benefit) — ATRA added to anthracycline-based chemotherapy transformed chemotherapy-era APL outcomes in APL91 (4-year survival 76% versus 49%), maintenance further reduced relapse in APL93, and cytarabine omission increased relapse in APL2000; three successive questions carded as labelled slices, not pooled
7576: LIKELY (benefit) — two concordant large placebo-controlled trials (monthly frequency −2.1 to −2.4 versus −1.1 on placebo; responder rates ~47–54% versus ~23%) plus an active-control trial matching propranolol at 100 mg/day, with no added gain and worse tolerability at 200 mg/day
7577: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — moderate discrimination in mixed noncardiac surgery (AUC 0.75) but poor in vascular surgery (AUC 0.64), poor for death (median AUC 0.62), and miscalibrated under modern troponin surveillance (c-statistic 0.60 with systematic underestimation) — a prognostic-accuracy stamp, not a treatment stamp
7578: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — high, severity-graded sensitivity for detecting OSA in surgical patients (pooled 85–90%, specificity only 27–47%) but no adjusted association with postoperative mortality, cardiac complications or length of stay in the largest surgical cohort — a prognostic-accuracy stamp, not a treatment stamp
7579: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — postoperative troponin elevation is common (8.0% by fourth-generation MINS criteria; 17.9% by hsTnT criteria; 9% versus 15% by hs-cTnI versus hs-cTnT in the same patients), mostly silent, and strongly and gradedly associated with 30-day and 1-year mortality across one labelled programme (VISION) and one independent cohort — a prognostic stamp, not a treatment stamp
7580: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — CURB-65 stratifies 30-day mortality in hospitalised community-acquired pneumonia (0.7% to 57% across scores 0–5 at derivation) but its per-score mortality is setting-dependent (flattened low-score gradient in a lower-mortality Korean cohort) and its discrimination is modest (ROC area 0.67 in a UK cohort) — a prognostic-accuracy stamp, not a treatment stamp
7581: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — the Apfel score's four-factor incidence gradient (10% to 79%) is steep and it beat five rival models on discrimination, calibration and simplicity, but discrimination is modest everywhere (AUC 0.61–0.75) and calibration failed on external validation in hepatectomy (slope 0.49) — a prognostic-accuracy stamp, not a treatment stamp
7582: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED — six independent healthy-population datasets across four assay approaches consistently establish that plasma renin and aldosterone reference intervals are assay-, sex- and age-specific (including a 59% radioimmunoassay-versus-LC-MS/MS aldosterone bias in plasma), even though each interval belongs to its own method and population and several datasets' numeric limits are not printed in their fetched records
7584: LIKELY (no benefit) — the only imaging trial (A-PLUS) was null on plaque progression while LDL cholesterol rose on the drug, the lipid trial's only wins were triglyceride/VLDL surrogates with no LDL change, and the agent was never marketed
7585: POSSIBLE (benefit) — consistent short-term LDL lowering (surrogate endpoint only) across three trials, but the phase 3 was terminated over cartilage damage in dogs with only 69 patients analysable at 6 weeks, liver enzymes rose, and the agent was never marketed
7586: SPLIT — GENERATIONS reduced vertebral fractures (41% relative) and invasive breast cancer (56% relative) but did not reduce nonvertebral fractures and increased venous thromboembolic events 2.3-fold relative; the supporting trials are BMD surrogates, and the agent was never marketed
7587: POSSIBLE (benefit) — glycaemic (HbA1c, surrogate) benefit shown in three trials including a 1,912-patient phase 3 superior to pioglitazone at 1.5 mg, but the agent was never marketed, one trial lost over half its participants early, and the class harms (oedema, weight gain) are in its own data
7588: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — BEST, the definitive 2,708-patient trial stopped early by its monitoring board, found no significant mortality benefit (30% vs 33%; adjusted P = 0.13); favourable secondary endpoints and two small short LVEF trials do not borrow the class effect of the beta-blockers that succeeded
7589: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) — the large ESSENTIAL programme found no difference in mortality (HR 0.97) or mortality/cardiovascular hospitalisation (HR 0.98); the programme's arc runs from a small 1990 trial with significantly more deaths on the drug to a small exercise-capacity win, and exercise capacity is a surrogate, not clinical benefit
7590: SPLIT — in HFrEF, PICO showed better exercise duration, peak VO2 and quality of life over 12 weeks (surrogate / soft endpoints, no mortality trial); in HFpEF with RV–PA uncoupling, MONACO was null and terminated early; the Japanese evidence is a programme summary, labelled as such
7591: POSSIBLE (benefit) — phase 2 only: a 54-week phase 2b trial (n=834) with significant HbA1c and weight reductions vs placebo, a 32-day CKD phase 2a trial (n=41) and a short mechanistic hepatic-glycogen trial; the programme was not advanced to phase 3 on the glycaemic question and no outcomes trial exists
7592: SPLIT — real dose-dependent lipid lowering across two trials (triglycerides down up to 56.8% relative, non-HDL cholesterol down 22.0–27.7% relative, both surrogate endpoints) against the dose-dependent hepatic-fat increase (up to 76% relative; up to 44.4% with >3× transaminase elevations) that discontinued the programme; three reports but only two distinct trials, labelled
7593: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK: exactly 2 phase 3 reports, both positive on the day-7 serum-sodium surrogate in euvolaemic hyponatraemia only (6.7 vs 4.5 mmol/L (approx. 15.4 vs 10.4 mg/dL) inpatient; 3.2 vs 0.8 mmol/L (approx. 7.4 vs 1.8 mg/dL) outpatient), with reversal within 7 days of stopping and no mortality or length-of-stay data
7594: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK: exactly 2 results reports totalling 106 patients, both short-term, on surrogate/soft endpoints only (peak VO2, energetics, NYHA class); the two trials disagree on ejection fraction and no outcomes trial exists
7595: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK: exactly 2 randomised trials (161 and 66 patients, 8-12 weeks) showing relative lipid improvements, plus one sub-floor open-label HoFH report (N=8) that is never load-bearing; surrogate endpoints only, no outcomes trial
7596: LIKELY (no difference) — six randomised trials across outpatient, mild inpatient and hospitalised-on-oxygen settings met no primary endpoint anywhere; the one positive reading is a secondary endpoint, and the RACCO trial showed an imaging-defined pneumonia-progression harm signal (relative risk 2.08)
7597: SPLIT — symptom and quality-of-life scores improved versus sham in the early small trials while oesophageal acid exposure and medication use did not, and the one trial in PPI-refractory heartburn was flatly negative (primary endpoint 3.4% radiofrequency vs 15.1% sham)
7598: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK: exactly 6 randomised reports from 1988-1997, documented N=87 plus one report with N not documented, all on surrogate endpoints (natriuresis, diuresis, weight over hours to days); greater short-term natriuresis on torasemide, no difference at 70 days, and no clinical-outcome data
7599: SPLIT — four small randomised trials (total n=136) split on the HVPG surrogate: responder/within-group advantages in two, equal responders in one, and no HVPG effect in the largest post-bleeding trial, which also showed a GFR fall in Child-Pugh B patients; the originating ~45% relative fall was non-randomised programme support and was never replicated
7600: LIKELY (no difference) — both histology-primary trials were negative at conventional dose (n=166) and high dose (n=185); the one positive trial had an ALT (surrogate) primary endpoint, and the UDCA-plus-vitamin-E limb cannot attribute its signal to UDCA
7601: LIKELY (no difference) — one positive developer-linked programme trial (SVR 79% vs 50%) was not reproduced by two larger independent trials (50% vs 48% and 58.2% vs 60.8%); all evidence is peginterferon-era genotype 4 and the question is closed by the direct-acting-antiviral era
7602: SPLIT — topical paromomycin beat vehicle in ulcerative disease in Tunisia (81-82% vs 58%) and Bolivia (77.5% vs 10%), the Panama trial compared two active creams with no vehicle arm (79% vs 78%), and the one non-ulcerative trial was negative; absolute benefit is species- and setting-dependent
7603: POSSIBLE (benefit) — daily acyclovir modestly slowed HIV-1 disease progression in two randomised trials in ART-naive, HSV-2-dually infected people (hazard ratios 0.84 and 0.75, both relative measures with absolute event counts 284 vs 324 and 95 vs 110 printed beside them), supported on markers only by a postpartum valacyclovir limb that is never load-bearing; a pre-treat-all-era record, not a current treatment option
7604: MAYBE (weak evidence) — failed programme: four double-blind placebo-controlled trials of camostat in COVID-19 (n=205, 155, 342 and 216) met no primary endpoint in hospitalised or outpatient disease, including at supratherapeutic dose in CANDLE; the in-vitro TMPRSS2 rationale did not translate
7605: SPLIT — based on exactly 2 trials: ETASS (n=361, single-blind) was borderline positive on 28-day mortality (26.0% vs 35.0%; relative risk 0.74, 95% CI 0.54–1.02; P=0.062 unstratified / P=0.049 log-rank), while the TESTS phase 3 trial (n=1,106, double-blind) found no benefit (23.4% vs 24.1%; hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.77–1.27; P=0.93)
7606: LIKELY (benefit, for progression-free survival) — ICARIA-MM and IKEMA both improved PFS when isatuximab was added (hazard ratios 0.596 and 0.58 on updated analysis, relative measures with absolute medians beside them), while overall survival is borderline in ICARIA-MM (final hazard ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.59–1.02) and not different in IKEMA (hazard ratio 0.855, 95% CI 0.608–1.202)
7607: LIKELY (benefit, for response and progression-free survival) — single-arm KEYNOTE-087 response rates of 69.0–71.4% with durable responses, and randomised KEYNOTE-204 superiority over brentuximab vedotin on progression-free survival (13.2 vs 8.3 months; hazard ratio 0.65, relative); overall survival was not analysed at the reported interim analysis, so no survival claim is made
7608: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single programme, labelled: CheckMate 205 alone (single-arm, 243 patients after autologous transplant failure) showed nivolumab objective response rates of 66.3–71.2% across its three reports with median response durations of 16.6–18.2 months; there is no comparator, so no comparative or survival-effect claim is made
7609: LIKELY (benefit) — PARTIAL, founding slice only, beside live #1804/#845: one small placebo RCT (TRIUMPH, n=87; haemoglobin stabilisation 49% vs 0%, median transfused units 0 vs 10) plus a single-arm companion (SHEPHERD, n=97) and pre/post analyses, including thromboembolism at 1.07 vs 7.37 events per 100 patient-years (85% relative reduction, 6.3 absolute, not a randomised contrast)
7610: LIKELY (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, based on exactly 2 reports of one trial (TROPIC, n=755): cabazitaxel plus prednisone prolonged median overall survival after docetaxel versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone (15.1 vs 12.7 months; hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.59–0.83, relative), with pain palliation comparable to mitoxantrone and grade ≥3 neutropenia in 82% vs 58%
7611: PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE — CPET rules out postoperative risk far better than it rules it in: anaerobic-threshold negative predictive values of 96–100% against positive predictive values of only 2.9–42.1% in the 36-study classifier audit, with field-specific thresholds (AT 11 general, 9.9 hepatic; VE/VCO2 34.5 hepatic vs 41 pancreaticoduodenectomy) that are never merged, and no CPET score externally validated
